/330-WoodBadge27.desc:
Wood Badge 10-330-27
What is Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is an advanced leadership training course open to all adult members of Scouting America including Cub Scouting, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts, and Explorers, as well as the district and council levels.
The purpose of Wood Badge is to develop skilled leaders who can strengthen Scouting units in achieving the mission of Scouting America.
“One of the purposes of Wood Badge training is to get Scouters to think about the practice of Scouting, to meet together, to exchange experiences, and to live together in the spirit of the Scout Oath.” – Sir Robert Baden-Powell
Why should you attend Wood Badge?
If you completed your position specific training and want to learn more about being a Scout leader… attend Wood Badge.
If you want to …
Improve Communication
Solve Problems
Lead Change
Share Ideas with Other Leaders
Develop Your Team
Enhance Your Leadership Skills
Make Your Unit Youth-Led
Connect with Your Scouts
Understand the Aims of Scouting
Empower Your Youth Leadership
Improve Your Scouting Unit
Have a More Diverse Team
Reignite Your Scouting Spirit
Manage Conflicts
Learn to be a Coach & Mentor
And have fun while learning… attend Wood Badge!
Who can attend Wood Badge?
Each person participating in Wood Badge training must be a registered member of Scouting America and have completed the basic training courses for his/her Scouting position.
Additional Information
The course is limited to 48 participants. After the first 48, applicants will be placed on a waiting list. Acceptance from the waiting list will first be given to fully paid registrations.
Participants must provide a completed BSA Annual Health & Medical Record (Sections A, B, and C with a doctor’s signature).
Health forms will be collected utilizing Camp Docs.  An email invite from Camp Docs will be sent to you within four (4) months of the course beginning.  Note Part C must be current and extend through the course completion of October 4, 2027.
Participants must complete a pre-course assignment which includes 5 online training modules (~30 minutes) and a pre-course questionnaire.

/330-okpik.desc:
Okpik Winter Camping Experience is intended to teach youth participants how to have fun and
thrive
in the cold!  In 2027 we are offering three levels of adventure; Okpik Snowbirds, Okpik Adventurers & Okpik Explorers!  See the description below for more information about each program including participation requirements. The Snowbirds & Adventurers programs are organized to help you acquire skills and experience which you can bring back to your Troop, Crew, or Ship.  The Okpik Snowbirds program will participate in the outdoor program and skill building activities but sleep indoors both nights.  The Okpik Adventurers will build on their existing skills, participate in the winter programs, and sleep one night indoors and one outdoors!  The Okpik Explorers program is a back country camping adventure to use the advanced skills previously learned in the Okpik Adventurers program.  The Okpik Explorers will arrive, check gear and head out into the GSR back country for a two night winter camping adventure!  All planned Okpik programs are subject to change & weather.  Minimum age for each program is listed below; particiapants must not turn 21 until Monday 2/1/2027.
Okpik Snowbirds program includes:
Shelter building, snowshoeing, cold weather cooking, winter games, ice fishing, hiking, night sky viewing and more!  Open to all Scouts, Sea Scouts & Venturers age 12+
Okpik Adventurers program includes:
Shelter building, snowshoeing, cold weather cooking, winter games, ice fishing, hiking, night sky viewing and more!  Open to all Scouts, Sea Scouts & Venturers ages 14+ or to participants who have previously sucessfully completed the Snowbirds program.
Okpik Explorers program includes:
Hiking, snowshoeing, cold weather cooking & night sky viewing. Open to all 14+ Scouts, Sea Scouts & Venturers that have previously sucessfully completed the Okpik Adventurers program.  This program is a back country camping expedition that will test your skills and build your confidence.  You will arrive, assemble with your assigned crew, requisition patrol gear, do a quick shakedown, safety review and then depart for your back country adventure!  Participants must conform to the Height & Weight restrictions outlines in Part C of the
Annual Health & Medical Record
.
Please review Part C to ensure compliance before registering
.  Participation in Okpik Explorers is limited to those youth who have previopusly completed the Okpik Adventurers program.

/333-116818.desc:
You must be registered and paid with the BSA  to attend this training.
This full weekend course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their pack activities. BALOO training consists of an online pre-requisite component in addition to an overnight hands-on practical training experience. BSA’s Cub Scout level camping policies are taught by experienced scouters, along with the discovery of the necessary tools to help units deliver a successful camping experience. Completion of this course is mandatory for a MINIMUM OF ONE registered adult on a pack or den overnighter.
Note that this course will not include IOLS (Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills) content, which is focused on Troop overnight activities.
Course Prerequisite (Mandatory)
BALOO is a two-part blended learning format. The online modules comprise the first step to become BALOO-trained. The online training modules contain introductory and basic information that are built upon during the practical training, which  is completed during an in-person course offered by Northern NJ Council. The online component must be completed prior to the practical component and the course facilitator will verify completion prior to check-in at the in-person training event.
The online prerequisite training is available in the BSA Learn Center on My.Scouting; below are instructions to access the training session.
Four required learning modules provide the necessary knowledge base prior to engaging in the BALOO outdoor course. These segments are required prior to attending the outdoor portion. They will take about 30 minutes to complete.
Log in to My.Scouting.org and navigate to the BSA Learning Center
Click on the "Catalog"
From the Catalog screen, type the word “BALOO” into the search field and hit enter
The in-person practical portion is facilitated by the Northern NJ Council Training Committee and includes the overnight portion of the training. Participants must be present and attend all sessions of the program, including the overnight experience, to qualify and receive the qualification of BALOO-trained. Please do not ask your course director for permission to be absent from any of the sessions or to leave early on Sunday.
Your course director will offer a preparation session one to two weeks in advance of the overnight experience to provide guidance on how to prepare for the session, what and how to pack, and items to bring to the session as well as those to leave behind. Note that the registration fee covers all meals and tent space at the campsite. You are responsible for your own gear, including a personal tent or hammock.

/333-116830.desc:
A Den Chief is a Scout, Venturer or Sea Scout assisting a Cub Scout den. But the story is far more important than those words suggest as the Den Chief:
• Serves as a Scouting role model for the Cub Scouts in the den, as well as the entire pack;
• Promotes Scouting in general and the local troop in particular;
• Encourages the transition of Webelos Scouts into Scouts BSA;
• Holds a leadership position in the troop or crew, thus fulfilling an advancement requirement in the unit. In addition, a trained Den Chief:
• Assists the den leader with planning and conducting den meetings;
• Understands the Cub Scouting program and the differences between Cub Scouts and other Scouting programs;
• Understands the den leader's duties and confidently helps lead portions of the den meeting program;
• Knows a variety of resources for age-appropriate activities for Cub Scouts in the den;
• Brings a repertoire of activities that Cub Scouts enjoy.
This training is designed to build on each of these ideas using a framework that will allow the new Den Chief, or perhaps the experienced Den Chief looking for new ideas, to have fun and learn the role.

/333-WB27.desc:
Join NNJC for a two weekend program that will teach all participants to internalize the 5 themes of Wood Badge: Living the Values, Growing, Connecting, Guiding, Empowering.
What is Wood Badge?
Reflecting the best of nearly a century of Scouting experience, Wood Badge draws upon the most current leadership models used by corporate America, academic circles and successful organizations throughout the country.
Wood Badge training was begun by Baden Powell in 1919 as a way to insure that the leaders of Scout troops were properly trained. Since then Wood Badge has been held worldwide, providing advanced leadership training to thousands of Scout leaders. Wood Badge builds upon the best traditions and experiences of the Boy Scouts of America and also draws from a wide range of courses within and beyond the bounds of Scouting to present the latest in leadership theory and team development.
Who should attend?
Wood Badge is designed to meet the advanced leadership needs of all Scouters, particularly unit level Scouters, such as Cub leaders, Scoutmasters and assistants, Venturing Crew Advisors, Committee Chairs and members. Additionally Scouters serving at the district and council levels can achieve greater effectiveness through Wood Badge.
To attend a Wood Badge course, individuals must:
Be registered members of the Boy Scouts of America. (Youth 18 and older may attend as long as the appropriate Youth Protection guidelines are followed. They do not need to be registered in an adult leadership role.)
Have completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
All participants are required to complete parts A, B, & C of the  Annual Health and Medical Record form
Why attend?
By taking Wood Badge, Scouters will acquire valuable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning and leading change. Participants will better learn to understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our society. They will learn skills that will make them a better Scout leader. Units with trained leaders are able to deliver an improved program and a more meaningful experience for the youth Scouting serves.
(Cost includes all meals, program materials, insurance, administrative costs, T-shirt, other course materials and recognition items.)

To attend a Wood Badge course, individuals must:
Be registered members of the Boy Scouts of America. (Youth 18 and older may attend as long as the appropriate Youth Protection guidelines are followed. They do not need to be registered in an adult leadership role.)
Have completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
All participants are required to complete parts A, B, & C of the  Annual Health and Medical Record form
Why attend?
By taking Wood Badge, Scouters will acquire valuable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning and leading change. Participants will better learn to understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our society. They will learn skills that will make them a better Scout leader. Units with trained leaders are able to deliver an improved program and a more meaningful experience for the youth Scouting serves.
(Cost includes all meals, program materials, insurance, administrative costs, T-shirt, other course materials and recognition items.)

/364-120912.desc:
Wakpominee Adirondack Trek Expeditions Are Here!
WAK-Treks is a week long canoeing/fishing adventure program that is offered during July & August that is based at Camp Wakpominee.
Group adventures start on Saturday with an afternoon arrival at camp.  They will meet their highly trained guide who will lead them through getting equipment organized, required training review,  along with canoe practice including water rescue techniques and be with them for the entire week.
Crews are provisioned with all back country food and crew equipment.  Each participant must bring some basic high adventure personal equipment.
Trips depart either Sunday PM or Monday AM, following their pre-planned itinerary enjoying the views, wildlife and fishing opportunities throughout the Adirondack Forest preserve.
All Treks return to base camp on Friday PM, clean up crew gear and enjoy a relaxing evening before their drive for home on Saturday AM.
How Do I Register For a WAK Trek?
Should be made with a $100 deposit per participant.  Crew size should be a minimum total of 6 with no more than a maximum total of 8.
Youth participants must be a registered Scout, 13 years of age and completed the 8th grade.  Two leaders must be 21 years of age and be current in YPT certification.
Co-ed groups are required to include one male and one female advisor.  Trek leaders are assigned to every group and are certified with all NYS and Scouting America certification.
What Do I Need In Order to Trek at WAK?
All participants must have a signed waiver / consent form along with current Scouting America ABC Medical Forms.
Each participant must have the classification of "swimmer" under Scouting America's swim requirements.
Who Do I Contact If I Have Questions?
Please direct any questions to: treks@campwakpominee.org

Are you READY for ADVENTURE!!!!
Welcome to Camp Wakpominee, a 1,000+ acre Adirondack Mountain wilderness area of beautiful Washington County, NY.  The camp has operated for more than 100 years and celebrated this anniversary in 2020.  Camp Walpominee is owned and operated by the Twin Rivers Council, and will be offering one week of Scout Resident Camp in 2027.  In addition to Scout and Cub Resident camps, the camp offers year round cabin and campsite rentals.  We also have opportunities for outside groups to utilize the camp through rental and program area interest.
The experienced staff members at Camp Wakpominee are trained to provide the most exciting, high quality outdoor program for Scouts.  Our highlights include:
Wilderness Mountain Biking
ATV Experience
Kayaking and Canoeing
Small Boat Sailing
COPE High Ropes Course
Shotgun and Rifle Shooting
Archery and Atlatl Spear Throwing
Community Safety
Trades MB Area
Scoutcraft and Handicrafts Area
Ecology & Conservation
Fishing
Trail to First Class Program
Adirondack Canoe Treks
Are you ready for the adventure?  We look forward to seeing you at camp!
Financial Aid:
All families needing financial assistance are encouraged to apply for camp assistance here:  https://trcscouting.org/forms/    All applications must be received no later than April 1, 2027 in order to be considered for a summer camp allowance in 2027.

Tuscarora Scout Reservation
is the perfect destination for Scouts looking for a memorable summer camp experience. Nestled in the foothills of the Catskill Mountains on the New York/Pennsylvania border, our 900-acre camp features everything from thrilling aquatic activities on the 35-acre Summit Lake to hands-on learning opportunities in Nature, Handicraft, Scoutcraft, Shooting Sports, Music & Arts and more. With top-notch amenities including a 40-foot climbing tower, modern individual-stall shower house, full-service dining hall, and quality campsites, you’ll find everything you need for a great week of summer adventures and Scouting fun.
900-acres of beautifully forest at the foothills of the Catskills
35-acre lake including boating, swimming, paddleboarding, water slide, and giant inflatable Action Tower.
Over 50 merit badge and skill instruction classes
Full-service dining hall
40-foot climbing tower
16-miles of marked hiking trails
Archery, rifle and shotgun ranges
Creative Handicraft, Music & Arts and Eagle's Nest programs
Hands-on outdoor skills at Scoutcraft and Nature
Top-notch "Trailblazer" program for first-year Scouts
Exciting afternoon and evening "theme" programs
Quality campsites and amenities
Enthusiastic and experienced staff
And so much more!
Our 2026 summer camp theme is
The Tuscarora Detective Agency
. All week long, Scouts will step into the role of detectives as mysteries unfold around camp. From uncovering secret clues and decoding hidden messages to solving puzzles and cracking escape room riddles, every day will bring new challenges. Investigative-themed merit badges—including Crime Prevention, Law, Fingerprinting, and Signs, Signals, & Codes—will give Scouts the chance to sharpen their skills. Join the case, unlock new abilities, and help solve the biggest mysteries of the summer!

/373-Fall27Balooiols.desc:
Fall 2027 BALOO & IOLS
Longhouse Council's Outdoor Training Team offers two essential courses over one incredible weekend: BALOO for Cub Scout leaders and IOLS for Scouts BSA Leaders. Come for a weekend of fun and learning from great instructors!
When: Training starts Friday evening (arrival between 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM) and wraps up on Sunday morning.
Where: Camp Woodland
What to Expect: An action-packed weekend of hands-on learning, fellowship, and fun!
Course Options
1. Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO)
This course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities.
Requirement: Completion of this course is mandatory for a minimum of one adult on any Pack overnighter.
Format: This is a two-part blended learning format:
Online Pre-requisite: You MUST complete the online training modules on the training portal prior to arriving for the practical component. These modules contain introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the weekend.
In-Person Practical: An overnight, hands-on practical course covering Scouting America Cub Scout-level camping policies and the necessary tools to help units carry out a successful camping experience.
2. Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS)
This hands-on course, conducted in a patrol setting, provides adult leaders with the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts safely and confidently in the outdoors.
Requirement: Along with Scoutmaster Specifics, this course is required for all direct-contact leaders registered in Scouts BSA Troops to be considered officially “trained.”
What You'll Learn: Upon completion, leaders should feel comfortable teaching Scouts the basic outdoor skills required to obtain the First Class rank.

Join us for an exciting, hands-on week dedicated entirely to earning merit badges. This unique event gives scouts the chance to dive into practical, rewarding fields, learn directly from industry professionals, and discover potential career paths or lifelong hobbies.
Whether you are looking to master a new tool, understand how things work behind the scenes, or check off those hard-to-find requirements, this week is built for you.
Why Attend?
Professional Instruction:
Learn from certified experts and tradespeople who bring real-world experience to the camp.
Hands-On Experience:
Move past the textbooks; scouts will be actively working on projects, using tools safely, and building tangible skills.
Rare Merit Badges:

/373-beyondarrow27.desc:
What is Beyond the Arrow? Let’s start with what it is not. It is not about AOL Adventure requirements or Shooting Sports, however will aid in completing the AOL Bobcat adventure, with a focus on the Scouts BSA program.
It is an outdoor adventure designed to aid in the AOL-to-Scout transition plan. This event is designed to introduce AOL Scouts and their parents to the exciting Scouting adventures that lay ahead of them and help make the transition into Scouts BSA more exciting while preparing them for the next step in scouting. The event is filled with fun activities, intriguing demonstrations, and plenty of outdoor adventure. All demonstrations and activities will be conducted by the Scouts from our council troops, and will showcase the Scout-run aspect of Scouts BSA.
Purpose
: AOL Scouting and the activities of the AOL Patrol should form a natural stepping stone for the AOL Scout and their parents to move into Scouts BSA. The purpose of this event is to create in all AOL Scouts a genuine desire to know more about Scouts BSA Scouting, and through a fun-filled series of demonstrations give them a preview of some of the activities, thrills and adventure that await them in Scouts BSA.
The program capitalizes on the AOLs’ interest in adventure in the great outdoors as it exposes them to the fun and skills of their next step in Scouting. It also offers an opportunity for parents to gain a perspective on the Scouts BSA program, how the different Troops run their programs, the differences between the Cub Scout and Scouts BSA programs, and their opportunities for adult leadership.
As a result of this program, participants should come away with:
An understanding of the Scouts BSA program, the skills required, and the fun that awaits.
An appreciation of the Scouts BSA Troop - how it is run, and how it differs from a Cub Scout Pack.
An increased desire to continue in Scouting as a Scout in a Scouts BSA Troop.
A "feel" for the various Troops in our council, and an idea of which one they may want to join.
Schedule:
Friday night: Arrival and set-up
Saturday: Troop led sessions and parent sessions throughout the day
- Meals in troop sites
- Campfire
Sunday: Departure

/373-springbalooiols28.desc:
Spring 2028 BALOO & IOLS
Longhouse Council's Outdoor Training Team offers two essential courses over one incredible weekend: BALOO for Cub Scout leaders and IOLS for Scouts BSA Leaders. Come for a weekend of fun and learning from great instructors!
When: Training starts Friday evening (arrival between 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM) and wraps up on Sunday morning.
Where: Camp Woodland
What to Expect: An action-packed weekend of hands-on learning, fellowship, and fun!
Course Options
1. Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO)
This course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities.
Requirement: Completion of this course is mandatory for a minimum of one adult on any Pack overnighter.
Format: This is a two-part blended learning format:
Online Pre-requisite: You MUST complete the online training modules on the training portal prior to arriving for the practical component. These modules contain introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the weekend.
In-Person Practical: An overnight, hands-on practical course covering Scouting America Cub Scout-level camping policies and the necessary tools to help units carry out a successful camping experience.
2. Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS)
This hands-on course, conducted in a patrol setting, provides adult leaders with the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts safely and confidently in the outdoors.
Requirement: Along with Scoutmaster Specifics, this course is required for all direct-contact leaders registered in Scouts BSA Troops to be considered officially “trained.”
What You'll Learn: Upon completion, leaders should feel comfortable teaching Scouts the basic outdoor skills required to obtain the First Class rank.

Requirement: Completion of this course is mandatory for a minimum of one adult on any Pack overnighter.
Format: This is a two-part blended learning format:
Online Pre-requisite: You MUST complete the online training modules on the training portal prior to arriving for the practical component. These modules contain introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the weekend.
In-Person Practical: An overnight, hands-on practical course covering Scouting America Cub Scout-level camping policies and the necessary tools to help units carry out a successful camping experience.
2. Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS)
This hands-on course, conducted in a patrol setting, provides adult leaders with the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts safely and confidently in the outdoors.
Requirement: Along with Scoutmaster Specifics, this course is required for all direct-contact leaders registered in Scouts BSA Troops to be considered officially “trained.”
What You'll Learn: Upon completion, leaders should feel comfortable teaching Scouts the basic outdoor skills required to obtain the First Class rank.

/375-107337.desc:
Birchbark Expeditions is a Nationally Accredited week-long, fully guided high adventure canoe experience in Algonquin Provincial Park, steeped in the rich Age of Exploration history of Upper Canada.  Operated by volunteers from the Great Falls Scout Council, the program is open to Scouts BSA and Venture Scouts at least 13 years old and a "swimmer".  Algonquin Adventure Expeditions take place in Ontario Canada's Algonquin Provincial Park and offers world-class canoe tripping among the thousands of lakes and unspoiled wilderness.
Participants traveling to Canada will need a passport, passport card or Enhanced Drivers License. Youth will also need a permission slip, (a completed and signed Informed Consent and Health Form with parents signature(s), address and phone number)
Expeditions start on Saturday with an early drive from the Buffalo/Niagara area to base camp in Algonquin's Whitefish Group Campground. Here crews will meet their highly-trained Guide for the duration of our trip. Sunday morning, crews will take the opportunity to visit the Algonquin Visitor Centre or Logging Museum.  Upon returning to base camp, crews will organize equipment, practice some water rescue techniques and get rested for an early launch on Monday morning. Crews are provisioned with all necessary back country food and crew equipment, including: canoes, paddles, PFDs, tents and cooking equipment.  Each participant must bring some basic high-adventure personal equipment.
Monday through Friday have crews following their custom pre-planned itinerary through the pristine lakes and forests of the Algonquin interior, enjoying the incredible views, wildlife and camaraderie.
Crews return to base camp on Friday afternoon, clean up their crew gear, visit one of the local outfitters to pick up some souvenirs, and get some rest for their drive home.  Crews depart early Saturday morning, driving back to the Buffalo/Niagara area.
Crews from outside the Buffalo/Niagara area are encouraged to add a visit to Niagara Falls while in the area.
Program:
In addition to the standard expedition outlined above, Birchbark Expeditions also offers optional enhanced program elements, including:
Canoeing Merit Badge
Paddle Craft Safety Certification
St. George Religious Medal Treks
ACA Whitewater Training
Leave No Trace

IOLS Training
Gorton
Registration is required for this training as food must be purchased and supplies will be prepared for the numbers who register.
WHAT:
ITOLS is a hands-on training program to give adult leaders the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the Outdoors. Imagine having hands-on knowledge about setting up a campsite, pitching a tent, hiking, outdoor cooking, etc. – all the skills necessary to see the outdoor program of the SBSA come to life.
An equipment list is available for this training. The training will be held rain (snow) or shine and is an outdoor training!
You will need to attend both the Saturday night and Sunday sessions of the ITOLS training to complete the outdoor portion of the training. Check-in will begin at 8:00 AM Saturday and end by 11:00 AM Sunday.
Youth Protection Training is required for every leader/adult who has direct contact with youth. Please be aware that everyone attending IOLS must complete YPT. This is a National BSA, not just a GFC, requirement. Please bring along a copy of your certificate or a copy of your YPT pocket card. Online YPT:
https://my.scouting.org/
click on the YPT icon.
Because this training includes an overnight, you need to bring a current completed BSA Annual Health and Medical Record - Parts A&B.
https://www.scouting.org/health-and-safety/ahmr/
Campsite will be assigned when you check in. You will park your vehicle in the parking lot and walk to the camping area. There will be wagons to help transport your camping equipment (tent, sleeping bag, ground pad etc.)
Saturday lunch, dinner and snacks and Sunday breakfast will be provided.
This training will take place regardless rain (snow) or shine, so please come prepared. Note the ITOLS  packing list for "what to bring." We will be both indoor and outdoor for sessions.  We will have access to indoor bathrooms and showers.
Please come prepared with a song, skit, or a short story to share during the campfire planning session. Your ideas will help to build the campfire program on Saturday night.
You will need to complete Scoutmaster Position Specifics (available online) in order to be considered fully trained as a Scoutmaster or Asst. Scoutmaster.
Once registration is complete you will receive an email confirmation. If you do not get it, check your spam folder for a email from

Cub Adventure Camp
During your stay at Camp Scouthaven, you can participate in fun activities like a nature hike, fishing, BB Guns & Archery, outdoor skills training, swimming, boating and much more:
Enjoy fun in the water and on the water with swimming, boats of all sorts, and fishing.
Hone your marksmanship skills at our BB & Archery Ranges.
Learn about the wildlife, plants and trees that live at camp; play a fast-paced game of Gaga; and learn outdoor skills in our other program areas.
Create a one-of-a-kind craft at our Handicraft area using leather, beads, paint and whatever else you can find!
Learn more about science and technology in our ever growing STEM area.
AOL's enjoy a Special Overnight Program on the Hill on our last night.
Our program is 3 full days of fun, Campers arrive Thursday morning and leave Sunday after our closing campfire.
What makes Cub Scout Adventure Camp different from any other Cub Scout camp around? Our campers are immersed in a themed experience during their stay. You’ll live in a tent, participate in age-appropriate programs, earn your whittling chip (Bears, Webelos, and Arrow of Light Scouts) and many other activities in the camp and interact with the costumed staff.
Advancement Opportunities
While at Cub Adventure Camp, you can work on all kinds of Adventure loops and Webelos pins, as well as Cub awards like the Range and Target Activities Awards, the World Conservation Award. The only limit is what you choose NOT to do! Our staff will work with your Pack to provide advancement opportunities that meet your needs. Check out our Program Guide for more information on advancement opportunities.
Den Chiefs at Cub Scout Resident Camp
Den Chiefs are encouraged to come to camp to assist the Pack leadership in ensuring a positive experience
throughout the week. Den Chiefs are Scouts BSA Scouts who stay with a Den, but are there to provide support to the Cub Scouts. While Den Chiefs are welcome to participate in activities with their Den, priority is given to the Cub Scouts if space is limited.
Den Chiefs are to stay in their own tent or share a tent with another Den Chief. They are able to participate in
all activities in camp throughout their stay. Den Chiefs are not adult leadership and cannot be counted on as an adult leader at any time. We ask them to go through Den Chief Training before attending camp with their Cub Pack.

/375-WoodBadge2027.desc:
In 1919, Lord Baden Powell, the founder of Scouting, held the first Wood Badge course at Gilwell Park to ensure that adult leaders were properly skilled to lead youth in the Scouting program. For the last century, Scouters worldwide have been continuing the legacy of taking Wood Badge to ensure that the methods of effective mentoring and leadership remain strong for the youth we serve.
What is Wood Badge?
It’s Scouting’s ultimate leadership training for adults. Wood Badge is a 2 weekend, 5-day action-packed program. During the course, you’ll get to be a Scout experiencing a month’s worth of an exciting program while learning critical leadership skills. Most participants say that it has helped not only in their Scouting role but also in their professional and family life as well.
Who may attend?
Any registered adult Scouter from Cub Scouting, Scouts BSA, Sea Scouting and Venturing, who meets the following eligibility requirements:
Be registered as a member of Scouting America (there are no minimum tenure requirements).
Have completed the courses required to be "Position Trained" in your registered Scouting position
Have completed the outdoor skills training programs appropriate for their Scouting positions.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
Available to attend all sessions
There are no make-up opportunities. If an attendee has to miss any of the sessions they will be dropped from the course and will be asked to return the following year to attend the entire program. This includes attendance at any patrol meetings during the intervening week between the first and second weekend.
Outcomes
You will have the opportunity to join with other Scouters to share ideas, discuss challenges and locate resources. Attendees form new and lasting friendships during their Wood Badge experiences, Wood Badge is an intense leadership training that will change your life.
Wood Badge teaches leadership and team-building skills in a comfortable outdoor setting. There isn’t anything else in Scouting like it. Best of all, Wood Badge is FUN! Please join us on the trail to a mountaintop experience in one of the greatest adventures in Scouting.
When:
Weekend #1: August 27-29, 2027 (Camp Gorton)
Weekend #2: September 18-19, 2027 (Camp Scouthaven)
Registration deadline: July 29, 2027.
Participants must attend BOTH weekends to complete the course. Check-in begins at 7 am BOTH weekends.

/375-gortoncubadventurecamp27.desc:
Cub Adventure Camp
During your stay at Camp Gorton, you can participate in fun activities like a nature hike, fishing, open shoot at both ranges, outdoor skills training, swimming and much more:
Enjoy fun in the water and on the water with swimming, boats of all sorts, and fishing.
Hone your marksmanship skills at our popular shooting sports range.
Learn about the wildlife, plants and trees that live at camp; play a fast-paced game of Gaga; and learn outdoor skills in our other program areas.
Create a one-of-a-kind craft at our Handicraft area using leather, beads, paint and whatever else you can find!
Learn more about science and technology in our ever growing STEM area.
What makes Cub Scout Adventure Camp different from any other Cub Scout camp around? Our campers are immersed in a themed experience during their stay. You’ll live in a tent, participate in age-appropriate programs, earn your whittling chip (Bears, Webelos, Arrow of Light Scouts) and many other activities in the camp and interact with the costumed staff.
Advancement Opportunities
While at Cub Adventure Camp, you can work on all kinds of Adventure loops and Webelos pins, as well as Cub awards like the Range and Target Activates Adventures Awards, the World Conservation Award. The only limit is what you choose NOT to do! Our staff will work with your Pack to provide advancement opportunities that meet your needs. Check out our Program Guide for more information on advancement opportunities.
Den Chiefs at Cub Scout Resident Camp
Den Chiefs are encouraged to come to camp to assist the Pack leadership in ensuring a positive experience
throughout the week. Den Chiefs are Scouts BSA Scouts who stay with a Den, but are there to provide support to the Cub Scouts. While Den Chiefs are welcome to participate in activities with their Den, priority is given to the Cub Scouts if space is limited.
Den Chiefs are to stay in their own tent or share a tent with another Den Chief. They are able to participate in
all activities in camp throughout their stay. Den Chiefs are not adult leadership and cannot be counted on as an adult leader at any time. We ask they go through Den Chief Training before attending camp with their Cub Pack.
It is strongly recommended that Unit Leaders enable parent portal. When this is done you will have log-in cards to print and give to your parents. They can then log in and access their Scouts registration, fill out forms and make payments.
Registration Timeline
Unit Deposit - Unitl 1/31 - Only $100 Deposit and approximate number of adults and Scouts needed Deposits do not guarantee a campsite. You may choose 2 preferences, but this is not a specific site holder.

Tucked away in the heart of New York's beautiful Catskill Mountains,
Onteora Scout Reservation (OSR)
is more than a summer camp - it's a home away from home. Known proudly as
"The Land in the Sky,"
Onteora is where Scouts come to grow, explore, and build lasting memories. Every Scout who arrives is greeted with the same warm message:
"Welcome Home."
At Onteora, generations of Scouts have experienced the perfect mix of classic Scouting spirit and modern adventure. Whether your Scout is just beginning their journey or working toward Eagle, our program offers opportunities for every level — from first-year camper experiences to advanced merit badges and high adventure challenges. Each summer brings new experiences, new friendships, and lifelong lessons in leadership and teamwork.
Parents can be confident knowing that OSR is operated by Scouting America Long Island, dedicated to providing a safe and high-quality summer camp experience. Our trained staff are passionate about Scouting and committed to maintaining a welcoming, well-run camp — with great food, clean facilities, engaging programs, and exceptional service for every unit that visits.
Onteora’s story stretches back decades and is woven into the history of Scouting in New York. From its early beginnings to today’s thriving summer program, OSR has been shaped by the Scouts, leaders, and volunteers who’ve called it home.

/386-SpringNYLT.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth with leadership skills and experience that they can apply within their troops and in other situations requiring leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a six-day course that emphasizes hands-on learning in a fun, engaging environment. Through a blend of activities, presentations, challenges, and games, participants will develop confidence and leadership abilities while working together as a team.
The course content is designed to build leadership concepts progressively, using practical exercises to reinforce learning. Participants embark on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership, which brings the leadership lessons to life as they apply their skills throughout the course.
In order to attend an NYLT course, youth must meet the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Annual Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members must be at least 13 years old by the first day of the course and no older than 17 years old. They must also have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops and achieved the rank of First Class.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14 years old (or 13 and completed the eighth grade) and can be no older than 20 years old. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships and have some basic camping experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.

/386-WoodBadge.desc:
Wood Badge is an advanced, national leadership course open only to Scouting volunteers and professionals.
Scouters from Cub Scouting, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts, and Explorers, and district and council Scouters all are welcome and belong here.
What do we see on the course?
We do many things on the course, like:
Listening
Managing conflict
Leading change
Stages of team development
Coaching & Mentoring
Leadership for different stages
Servant leadership
Project planning
Problem solving
And more!
These come to you in presentations, games, discussions, activities, and other methods.
Why do you want to go?
You want to participate in a Wood Badge course because of the things you will learn and do. Here are some of the benefits:
Stronger units.
You will make your Scouting unit - and your childrens' units - stronger.
What and why of Scouting.
You will have a deeper understanding of what Scouting is and why we do it.
Experience.
You will learn and experience things that will stay with you in Scouting and the rest of your life.
Fun.
You will have fun and you will meet interesting people.
Other groups.
You will make your other groups, like work, church, even family, stronger.
Here’s another summary of why to go. This was originally aimed particularly at Scouters in the Cub Scout program, but it applies equally to all of us.
This course will help you better understand how all the Scouting programs tie together. It will provide you with many useful leadership tools to help enable our youth to have the best possible Scouting experience. There is no better time to attend a Wood Badge course and make a difference in your unit than when you are a Cub Scout Leader.
Purpose of Wood Badge
The purpose of Wood Badge is to develop skilled leaders who can strengthen Scouting units in achieving the mission of Scouting America.
When we accomplish the mission of Scouting, we do it in the units. Therefore, the short form of the purpose is, the purpose of Wood Badge is to strengthen units.
Although the course is different today, what Baden-Powell said in 1919 still applies:
One of the purposes of Wood Badge training is to get Scouters to think about the practice of Scouting, to meet together, to exchange experiences, and to live together in the spirit of the Scout Oath.

/386-bhscscoutday.desc:
Did you just cross over from Webelos to Scouts BSA or are you new to Scouts BSA all together?  Are you looking to attend Day Camp in addition to other Scouting adventures this summer?  Do you want to get a jump start on advancement?  Then Scouts BSA Day Camp is the program for you!
Scouts BSA Day Camp is intended for new Scouts to work on Rank Advancement, earn a couple of Merit Badges and enjoy exciting outdoor activities.  And the best part...you do not have to be a Scout to attend so invite a friend to join you!
Scouts will have an opportunity to work on requirements for Tenderfoot, Second Class and First Class.  Some of the Merit Badges offered during Boy Scout Day Camp are: Space Exploration, Canoeing, Fishing, Game Design, Geocaching, Orienteering, Swimming, Archery, Weather and much more!  Our camp progam runs daily from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.  Lunch is provided.
A note regarding merit badge classes:  The Scouts BSA Day Camp Program participants will have additional opportunities for merit badges not listed in the main online catalog.  They will be able to add/change selections when they check-in on Monday morning.

/386-bhscspecialty.desc:
Many Scouts first experience summer camp with their Troop. Joining your Troop for summer camp is a great time and every Scout should try to camp with their Troop. There are, however, additional camping opportunities offered at Baiting Hollow to help a Scout round out their camping experience or help advance in rank.
All Scouts BSA Camp programs listed below are
resident/sleep away
programs.
Aquatics Camp
August 15th - August 20th
Splash into adventure at Lake Arrowhead. Spend a week in the water swimming, kayaking, canoeing, rowing, paddling, sailing, snorkeling and life-saving. Aquatics camp will also include motor boating and water skiing on Long Island Sound.
Aquatics Camp is a
resident/sleep away
camp program.
The fee for Aquatics Camp is:
Before April 1st - $610 per scout                    After April 1st - $635 per scout
Bridge Camp
June 27th - July 2nd
Bridge camp is a program for Scouts who have just bridged over from Webelos. During the day the Scout will be involved with our Brownsea "first year camper program". At night they will be in a campsite with other Scouts their age. They will have a chance to work on Totin' Chip, Fireman Chit, Baiting Hollow Naturalist and participate in all of the other camp programs. Additionally, they will have the opportunity to work on their first merit badge.
Bridge Camp is a
resident/sleep away
camp program.
The fee for Bridge Camp is:
Before April 1st - $610 per scout                    After April 1st - $635 per scout
Counselor-in-Training (CIT)
July 11th - July24th
A Scout may enroll in the CIT program if they are
at least 14 years old by July 11, 2027.
Half the day is spent working next to experienced staff members to gain a hands-on look at camp programs. The second half of the day is spent on individual advancement and achievements including an opportunity to work on merit badges. Individuals who graduate from the CIT program have the opportunity to be considered for placement as a member of our Junior Staff Intern Program. If selected, Scouts can continue their training at no cost and spend the remainder of the summer working with our camp staff. Please call our camp office at 631-727-1614 for more information about our CIT Program.
CIT Camp is a
resident/sleep away
camp program.
The fee for Counselor in Training Camp is:
Before April 1st - $610 per scout                    After April 1st - $635 per scout
Fishing Camp
August 8th - August 13th
Campers will spend the week working on all things fishing!  They will work towards the Fishing, Fly Fishing and Fish & Wildlife Management Merit Badges all while still having time to participate in all the fun camp has to offer! Enjoy one of the few Council camps in our nation that offers both freshwater AND saltwater fishing on property! Fishing Camp is
a resident/sleep away
program.
The fee for Fishing Camp is:
Before April 1st - $610 per scout                    After April 1st - $635 per scout
Shooting Sports Camp
August 15th - August 20th
Our shooting sports program includes the opportunity to earn merit badges in rifle and archery shooting. Have fun tomahawk throwing, shooting sling shots and learning about black powder rifle. Scouts can earn NRA certifications in rifle shooting and NAA certifications in archery.
Minimum age to attend is 12.
Shooting Sports Camp is a
resident/sleep away
camp program.
The fee for Shooting Sports Camp is:
Before April 1st - $660 per scout                    After April 1st - $685 per scout
Trail to Eagle Camp
August 8th - August 13th
Our most popular specialty camp, Trail to Eagle Camp helps motivated Scouts walk down the trail to the Eagle Scout rank. Programs designed to help Scouts achieve required merit badges are in place and District Advancement Chairpersons are often in attendance to provide counseling on time management, Eagle Scout projects, and the paperwork required for the Eagle rank. /386-bhsctroop2027.desc:
There are a lot of great reasons to spend your summer at Baiting Hollow Scout Camp!
At Baiting Hollow, fun is at the heart of everything we do. Scouts enjoy days at the waterfront, rifle range, archery range, and craft center, along with hands-on merit badge classes that challenge them to learn something new. Evenings are spent gathered around the campfire with friends or watching the sun set over the beautiful waters of Long Island Sound.
Summer camp is a cornerstone of the Scouting experience, and Baiting Hollow is a place where Scouts truly feel like they matter. From the moment units arrive, the excitement builds each day with engaging programs, supportive staff, and a camp environment designed to deliver outstanding value, adventure, and memories that last a lifetime.
Whether you’re discovering Baiting Hollow for the first time or returning to a place filled with Scouting history, this summer offers a unique opportunity to be part of a century-long legacy. Join us for a week of fun, friendship, and adventure at a camp that has been shaping Scouts for 100 years—and counting.

/397-117409.desc:
When emergencies happen in the backcountry, help may be hours away. Wilderness First Aid (WFA) provides Scouts and adult leaders with the knowledge and hands-on skills needed to assess, treat, and manage medical emergencies in remote outdoor environments until professional help arrives.
This comprehensive course covers patient assessment, wound management, environmental emergencies, fractures and splinting, evacuation considerations, and other common outdoor injuries and illnesses. Participants will learn through a combination of online learning, classroom instruction, hands-on practice, and realistic scenarios.
Wilderness First Aid is strongly recommended for anyone participating in outdoor adventures and is required for many Scouting high-adventure programs, including treks at Philmont Scout Ranch, Northern Tier, Florida National High Adventure Sea Base, and Summit Bechtel Reserve.
Certification & Course Format
This course utilizes the Emergency Care & Safety Institute (ECSI) Wilderness First Aid program, which meets the requirements for Wilderness First Aid certification established by Scouting America and accepted for participation in Scouting high-adventure programs.
This is a hybrid course.
Participants must complete a minimum of 8 hours of online coursework prior to attending the in-person session (expect that it may take around 10-12 hours depending on your pace).
Access information for the online portion will be distributed approximately 2-3 weeks before the course date. Completion of all required online modules is mandatory before participating in the hands-on practical sessions and certification activities.
Participants who successfully complete both the online and in-person portions of the course will receive a 2-year ECSI Wilderness First Aid certification. Participants registered for the CPR/AED option will also receive a 2-year ECSI CPR/AED certification upon successful completion.
Who Should Attend?
Adult leaders participating in outdoor programs
First Class Scouts Age 14 and Older
High-adventure participants and advisors
Unit leaders attending long-term camp or extended outdoor activities
Anyone interested in improving their outdoor emergency preparedness
Course Fees
$100 – Wilderness First Aid plus CPR/AED Certification - Starts at 8 AM
OR
$75 – Wilderness First Aid only (must provide proof of current CPR/AED certification) - Starts at 10 AM
Additional Information
Lunch is on your own.  Brown Bag Lunches are welcome, and you will also have a short break to visit nearby take-out restaurants

/397-CSAC27.desc:
Cub Scout Adventure Camp (CSAC)
at J. Warren Cutler Scout Reservation
The Adventure takes place at the J. Warren Cutler Scout Reservation located near Naples, New York in the beautiful Bristol Hills. Cub Scouts live in one of five themed villages for three days and two nights. While there they participate in camp-wide activities such as boating and fishing, swimming, nature, archery, and shooting sports as well as themed village programs.
Cub Scout Adventure Camp Sessions
Cub Adventure Camp is scheduled with our parents in mind. It can be difficult to take time off from work to attend camp with your Scout during the summer but most will agree it’s worth it. Our schedule is family and work friendly.
Camp is fun when you attend as a Parent & Scout pair but it’s MUCH more fun when you attend as a Den or as a Pack. Wolves, Bears, and Webelos Dens can sign up following the Adult to Scout Ratio for Cub Scouts (2 adult to every 8 youth).  Sign up to attending as a group sign or sign up on your own. Cub Scouts can go camping, don’t miss out on the fun this summer.
HOW MUCH
:
Regular rate - $300
Early Bird Rate - $275
Late Fee - $350
Adult rate $100
Do you have more than 1 child attending Cub Scout Adventure Camp? Receive a $25 Sibling Discount off the registration fee!
Send an email to camping@senecawaterways.org with your scouts information to recieve the sibling discount.
Cub Scout Leaders please take note of the following dates:
CAMP FEE SCHEDULE
:
Camper Deposits of $50 per scout must be
paid in full by March 26, 2027
Early Bird Fee must be
paid in full by April 23, 2027
Scouts who missed Early Bird deadline must have fees
paid in full by June 30, 2027
Youth who have joined scouting in the Spring (Feb-June) are Eligible for early bird rates.
Be sure to select "New Scout in Spring"

/397-MSCSummer75.desc:
Welcome to Massawepie Scout Camps
Located in the heart of the Adirondack Mountains of northern New York State, Massawepie Scout Camps offers an experience unlike any other Scout camp. For 75 years, generations of Scouts have come to Massawepie to explore the Adirondacks, learn new skills, challenge themselves, and make memories that last long after summer ends.
In 2027, we celebrate 75 years of Massawepie. From the first Scouts who arrived in 1952 to the thousands of Scouts who visit us today, Massawepie's history is built around adventure, the outdoors, and the traditions of Scouting.
Our 3,800-acre property includes lakes and ponds, remote campsites, miles of trails, and historic camp areas. During our 75th anniversary summer, we are bringing those places and traditions together for a special season of camping and adventure.
Camp Pioneer
Camp Pioneer is Massawepie's primary Scouts BSA resident camp and the home base for a traditional week of summer camp in the Adirondacks.
Pioneer offers more than 50 merit badges and classes across a wide variety of program areas, including Scoutcraft, Handicraft, Ecology and Conservation, STEM, Sports, Aquatics, Range and Target Activities, and C.O.P.E. and Climbing. Scouts can swim and boat on private Massawepie Lake, climb our 30-foot tower or natural rock face, explore our trails and outposts, and take part in a wide variety of open-program activities.
First-year Scouts can take part in Trailblazers, which combines essential Scout skills, Tenderfoot-to-First Class advancement, and an introduction to life at camp. Older Scouts can challenge themselves through C.O.P.E. and Climbing, Aquatics, Range Activities, outposting, and other high-adventure opportunities.
And because this is our 75th anniversary, 2027 will feature several special programs and returning traditions, including:
The Return of the Great Canoe Race — A Massawepie tradition returns for our anniversary summer, celebrating teamwork, adventure, and generations of Scouts on the water.
New Aquatics Activities — Including an inflatable water challenge on the waterfront.
New Merit Badges and Program Offerings — Fresh opportunities for Scouts to explore interests, learn skills, and try something new.
Massawepie Traditions and History — Special opportunities to connect with the places and experiences that have shaped camp over the past 75 years.
Legacy Barkeater Program- Recognizing Scouts and Leaders who have spent 6 or more summers at camp with a unique token, and ceremony.
Whether this is your Scout's first summer at camp or their sixth, there is always something new to discover at Massawepie.
Camp Forester
For the first time in more than 30 years, Scouts will have an opportunity to step back into Camp Forester as part of our 75th anniversary celebration.
The Forester Outpost Experience will offer Scouts a chance to spend time in one of Massawepie's original camp areas, with opportunities for rustic camping, patrol cooking, and outdoor adventure. It is a chance to experience a piece of Massawepie history while building the same outdoor skills, teamwork, and self-reliance that have always been part of the Massawepie experience.
Registration for Forester experiences is available through our Massawepie registration system.
Camp Voyageur & Adirondack Treks
Camp Voyageur is home to Massawepie's Adirondack high-adventure and trek programs.
The Massawepie Adirondack Trek Center offers three-day and six-day backpacking, canoeing, and combination treks through the Adirondack wilderness. Units can add a trek before or after their week of resident camp, or split their group so that some Scouts participate in a trek while others remain at Camp Pioneer.
Explore Voyageur and Adirondack adventure opportunities through the Massawepie registration system and program guide
Camp Mountaineer — Family Camping
Across Massawepie Lake from Camp Pioneer is Camp Mountaineer, our family campground.
Mountaineer operated as a Scout camp for many years before

Tuscarora Scout Reservation
is the perfect destination for Scouts looking for a memorable summer camp experience. Nestled in the foothills of the Catskill Mountains on the New York/Pennsylvania border, our 900-acre camp features everything from thrilling aquatic activities on the 35-acre Summit Lake to hands-on learning opportunities in Nature, Handicraft, Scoutcraft, Shooting Sports, Music & Arts and more. With top-notch amenities including a 40-foot climbing tower, modern individual-stall shower house, full-service dining hall, and quality campsites, you’ll find everything you need for a great week of summer adventures and Scouting fun.

Camp Tusky – Your Camp Home
Located in Windsor, NY at the foothills of the Catskill Mountains, Tuscarora Scout Reservation encompasses 900 acres of beautifully forested land on the New York/Pennsylvania border.
Tuscarora offers 10 traditional “summer” sites with two-person canvas wall tents on platforms and three unique “winter” sites with eight-person lean-tos. Campsites include communal areas with carports, pavilions, picnic tables, in-site latrines, and fire circles.
Tuscarora features a modern individual-stall shower house, a central dining hall that provides three delicious meals each day, and an enthusiastic and experienced camp staff that will make your unit feel at home. Each summer is filled with new programs and activities designed to peak the interests of every Scout – from the newest campers to the seasoned veterans.
2027 Theme – Tusky Tales!
Step into the enchanted world of Tuscarora in 2027, where fairy tales, nursery rhymes, and beloved classic stories come to life. From daring quests and magical kingdoms to legendary heroes and unforgettable characters, Scouts will discover classic storybook adventures around every corner. Throughout the week, program areas will be transformed with imaginative events, bringing timeless tales to life. Scouts will have the opportunity to earn book-themed merit badges, participate in magical adventures, solve enchanted quests, and write their own camp story.

Aquatics on Summit Lake -
The 35-acre Summit Lake at the heart of camp provides great boating opportunities for Scouts and leaders – including sailing, canoeing, kayaking, rowing, and stand-up paddleboarding! The Waterfront is also home to exciting action aquatic activities – including swimming, a waterslide, water trampoline, giant inflatables for climbing, and more!
Climbing
- The camp features a 40-foot, three-sided climbing and rappelling tower. Scouts can come for afternoon open climbs or earn the Climbing merit badge in special classes and sessions.
Eagle’s Nest
- This program area helps Scouts on the trail to Eagle develop life skills with several Eagle-required merit badges – including such skills as communicating and citizenship.
Handicraft
- Handicraft focuses on a wide-range of crafts and trade skills. The area lets Scouts build skills in basket making, leatherworking, wood carving, and more.
Health Lodge
- The Health Lodge at Camp Tuscarora serves as the first aid center, offering medical support and instructional programs, including the First Aid merit badge, to help Scouts to be prepared!

/421-114440.desc:
The Occoneechee Council Wood Badge training is a five-day course held over two weekends at Camp Durant.
You must attend both weekends to successfully complete the course.
Are you an adult who wants to lead the way, inspire youth, and finally understand why Scouting does things the way it does?
Then you need Wood Badge!
What’s Wood Badge?
Only the ultimate adult leadership adventure in Scouting! It’s 5 days of hands-on team-building, communication, and leadership training that’ll level up your skills—not just in Scouting, but in real life too. Yes, even your coworkers and family might notice.
Who’s it for?
Newbie? Old pro? Somewhere in between? If you’re a registered leader (18+), and have done your basic training, you’re in! Cub Scouts to Council, we’ve got room for you.
Pre-Course Online Orientation Fun!
Before you arrive, there’s one more (there’s always more!) thing you will need to do. Wood Badge has put together a 30 minute online pre-course orientation that is intended to let you know what to expect from a Wood Badge course and should alleviate common concerns about what to expect during the training.
Note
:If you click the link before you sign in, then you will be prompted to sign in and will be taken to the homepage.  You’ll need to click the link again to get directly to the course.
All Occoneechee Council Events are stand-alone events and fees do not roll from one event to another. A refund of 100% of event fees can be issued up to 30 days prior to the start of the event. From 30-15 days prior to the event start, a 50% refund can be issued. Within 15 days prior to the event start, refunds will not be issued.

The Occoneechee Council Wood Badge training is a five-day course held over two weekends at Camp Durant.
You must attend both weekends to successfully complete the course.
This year's Wood Badge course will be held Sept. 10-12, 2027 and Oct. 2-3, 2027.  Both weekends begin at 7am.

Then you need Wood Badge!
What’s Wood Badge?
Only the ultimate adult leadership adventure in Scouting! It’s 5 days of hands-on team-building, communication, and leadership training that’ll level up your skills—not just in Scouting, but in real life too. Yes, even your coworkers and family might notice.
Who’s it for?
Newbie? Old pro? Somewhere in between? If you’re a registered leader (18+), and have done your basic training, you’re in! Cub Scouts to Council, we’ve got room for you.

/424-woodbadge.desc:
WOOD BADGE
15-424-27
"Lead Brave" "Lead True" "Lead Connected"?
Are You Ready to be part of a over 100 year-old world-wide legacy?
Are YOU ready to learn new leadership skills?
Are YOU ready to uncover information on how to become a better leader for your Scouts, family, community and work?
Are YOU ready to have fun and discover the leader you didn’t know you could be?
Are YOU ready to see how Baden Powell’s spirit is as important today as it was when he originally developed the Wood Badge program?
What is Wood Badge?
Leadership course for trained: Cub Scout Leaders, Scouts BSA Leaders, Venturing Advisors and Exploring Advisors.
Worldwide training tradition that reaches back to the days of the founding of Scouting. A Five day experience, over the course of one 3-day weekend and one-2-day weekend, in which you learn more about Scouting, leadership and yourself. It is only offered in Tuscarora Council every Two Years so act fast!
All trained adult Scout Leaders are encouraged to attend Wood Badge; space is limited. Wood Badge is the highest and most advanced training course offered by the Boy Scouts of America. While it is rich in Scouting History and tradition, participants will learn modern leadership theories from contemporary scholars such as Ken Blanchard, Steven R. Covey and John C. Maxwell. Many employers are familiar with the value of this leadership training course, and some will even cover a portion of the course fees. (Informational employer letters are available upon request.)
When is Wood Badge held?
February 12-14 2027 – All Day (Friday, Saturday, and Sunday)-Indoor class room
March 13-14 2027 – All Day (Saturday, Sunday) - Patrol camping
You must attend BOTH weekends to complete
Where does it take place?
C
amp Tuscarora Scout Reservation, 965 Scout Road, Four Oaks, NC 27524.
Why Should I Attend Wood Badge
It will make you a more effective leader.
It will be fun while teaching practical applications of listening, communicating, project planning and team building.
You will connect with fellow Scouters who will become friends for life and a valuable resource for years to come.
How much does it cost?
S7-424-21 course fee is $325.00
Pay Early at $275 until 12/11
Fee must be paid in FULL by Jan 12, 2027
The fee will cover meals, lodging, course hat, course notebook, and other program materials for the 5 full days, as well as training recognition.

Visit the link below to begin your registration and pay your deposit to secure your spot! Registration link goes live online on TBD.

Be a registered leader in your Scouting unit (or District) and have completed basic training specific to your Scouting position. This includes the outdoor training course for your registered position, if applicable. (For example: BALOO, Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills, etc.)
Current BSA Health and Medical History form, parts A, B, and C, which must be signed by your medical practitioner. (Physician, Physician’s Assistant, or Nurse Practitioner.)
BSA Class A uniform for your Scouting position
Uniform must include official BSA shirt with shoulder loops.
BSA pants or shorts.
BSA belt.
Total payment $325.00
REFUNDS/CANCELLATIONS
No refunds after DEcember 31, 2026. (Unless We Have a Full Course of 48 fully paid)

/425-NYLT.desc:
What is NYLT? The training of youth leaders in the Unit is important in helping individual Scouts, Venturers, and the Unit grow. The Boy Scouts of America has developed a six-day training experience, the National Youth Leadership Training Course (NYLT) that has proven valuable in the training of youth leaders. The course will stress the skills of leadership that will make youth leaders more effective in their Unit leadership positions. Perhaps more importantly, the Scout or Venturer will be exposed to living skills that will allow the Scout or Venturer to become a successful leader in any organization. This course will provide the youth with the tools that are needed to foster leadership potential. The skills taught will immensely facilitate the Unit Leader’s leadership development of the youth and directly benefit the Unit’s program.
What is its Purpose? Scouting recognizes that Unit Leaders have the responsibility of training their own youth leaders. The purpose of the National Youth Leadership Training Course is not to assume the Unit Leader’s role, but to support it. The course objectives are:
To enhance the relationship between the participant and his Unit Leaders.
To have fun.
To give participants a basic knowledge of the skills of leadership and help them relate these skills to their Troop or Crew responsibilities.
To give participants the opportunity to share ideas and experience with youth from other Units.
To give participants the confidence and knowledge to run the Unit program.

/429-119019.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
is a 6-day leadership experience for youth registered in Scouts BSA, Venturing, or Sea Scouts. It’s designed for Scouts who want to grow as leaders and for units that believe in a strong, youth-led program. Many troops even require NYLT for Senior Patrol Leaders because it helps youth leaders understand not just what leadership is, but how to live it. We find that many troops will cover 50-100% of the participant fee as a way of investing into the troop's health.
At NYLT, participants don’t just sit and listen to presentations. They learn by doing. The course is built to feel like a well-run Scout unit, where youth work together in patrols and take on real leadership challenges. Along the way, Scouts explore the core leadership ideas of
Be, Know, Do
, building skills like communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and ethical decision-making. There’s plenty of hands-on activity, teamwork, and fun woven into the week.
One of the most powerful parts of NYLT is that it is truly youth-led. The course is run by a highly trained youth staff, with adults serving as advisors in the background. This gives participants a clear picture of what a youth-led troop looks like and the confidence to bring that mindset back home. The leadership skills learned at NYLT don’t stop with Scouting; they help Scouts succeed in school, future jobs, and life.
NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, but participants should be comfortable with basic camping and outdoor cooking so they can fully take part in the experience. Before registering, please be sure to get a troop leader recommendation.
Attendance:
Participants must attend the entire course, from the morning of Monday, June 7 through the afternoon of Saturday, June 12. Scouts may arrive after 6:00 PM on Sunday, June 6 and stay overnight before the course begins if they wish.
A complete Leader’s Guide and all required forms are included in the
Welcome Letter
found in the attachments section. The required forms must be sent to
ryan.hansen@scouting.org
or the course leadership by
Monday, June 24
!
Registration Fees & Shirt Sizes:
The cost of the course includes all meals from Monday to Saturday, two course t-shirts, hat, handbooks, recognition materials, and camping supplies.
The early bird fee is
$250
and is available through April 1, 2027. After April 1, the regular registration fee increases to
$350
. Scouts who register after the early bird deadline may still select a shirt size, but availability cannot be guaranteed.
NYLT is more than just a training course; it’s an experience that helps Scouts step up, lead with confidence, and bring the true spirit of youth-led leadership back to their unit.

It is necessary for Packs to register and pay as a UNIT. The system will allow only ONE registration per unit number.
Great Trail Council Scouts receive a $25.00 discount from the above fee as part of the Adventure Fee Program. This discount is noted in each youth registraion as "Applied Coupon".
For a step-by-step instruction of the Deposit and Campsite selection process please select the "
Cub Over Night Reservation Process (2025)
" document in the Attachments Section in the right column.
Cub Scout Resident (Overnight) Camp is an opportunity for Tigers, Wolves, Bears, Webelos and Arrow of Light Scout's to experience the adventure of Camp Manatoc. It's days filled with exciting activities like swimming, boating, rafting, archery, BB-gun marksmanship, hiking, fire-building, and more!
Steps to register:
Gather the Pack and determine the number of Scouts and Leaders that will be attending overnight camp (youth from Bears, Wolves, AOL's, and Webelos are eligible to attend.)
Create a registration for the ENTIRE PACK.
Following the registration form, complete a registration contact, indicate the number of youth and adults you are intending to attend.
Pay the $100.00 deposit for the Pack. (This is part of your total bill.)
Beginning April 28 you may assign camper names and make payments beyond the $100.00 deposit.
If you receive a popup that informs you that a registration has been completed for your unit, please check with the other members of your Pack.

/433-WoodBadge.desc:
Wood Badge 9-433-27
What is Wood Badge?
The Wood Badge course is an internationally recognized leadership development course, with leadership skills taught that are equal to or better than any current leadership training in the industry today.
The course uses indoor and outdoor settings to teach the essentials of leadership. You will learn what makes leadership work and how it works for you and your unit. You will learn to apply those skills to help your unit function more effectively as a team. You will become a better manager by practicing these skills. Finally, you will have the opportunity to state your goals as a leader (your “Ticket”) and implement a plan to achieve these goals.
The positive influence of this course is unparalleled and applies to our everyday lives in our units, at home, and at work.
You must attend both weekends of the course to complete Wood Badge.

/433-manatoc2027.desc:
Why Your Scout Troop Must Experience Camp Manatoc in Peninsula, Ohio
Picture your Scout troop immersed in the heart of Cuyahoga Valley National Park, surrounded by 400 acres of pristine forests, rolling hills, and sparkling lakes! We are a camp with history starting in 1923! it’s a transformative adventure that will ignite your Scouts’ passion for exploration, leadership, and camaraderie. If you want your troop to grow stronger, bolder, and closer than ever, here’s why Camp Manatoc is the ultimate destination:
Unparalleled Adventure That Shapes Scouts for Life:
At Camp Manatoc, your Scouts won’t just camp they’ll conquer challenges that forge character and lifelong memories.  Every activity is designed to push boundaries while teaching practical skills teamwork, problem-solving, and resilienc that Scouts carry far beyond the campfire. With over 70 merit badge options and expert-led programs, your troop will dive into hands-on learning in a setting that feels like a real-world adventure playground.
A Perfect Blend of Tradition and Modern Comfort:
Camp Manatoc balances rugged Scouting spirit with top-notch facilities. Your troop will stay in well-maintained cabins or tents, enjoy meals in a spacious dining hall, and access modern amenities like showers, a well-equipped pool, and dedicated waterfront areas all within in the national park. Whether it’s a week-long summer camp filled with pool games and kayaking, a crisp fall weekend, or a custom retreat, the camp’s flexible programs cater to any troop size or schedule.
Hear exactly what our customers say!
"Compactivity and it's close"  The camp feels open and with the trees they nicely block the area between the program areas!
"Love it. The scenery, the variety of classes for the youth, the hikes, everything. The history, the ability to make things new."  We are always updating our classes that we offer to make camp new. This year we added a Wednesday adventure day where Scouts take a break from the classes and get out into nature!
"It's pretty awesome, the staff is always helpful, and the camp is always beautiful." As we hire over 60 staff members every summer there is always someone around willing and able to help you with any questions you may have!
"It always feels like home. The staff always make it a welcoming and comfortable environment. It’s beauty always has us coming back."  From the Dining Hall to the Waterfront the allure of Manatoc strikes young and old. By the end of your week you'll understand "... to these things you must return.

The University of Scouting is the largest supplemental training
course offered by Great Trail Council to Scouting volunteers at

leaders will present programs to help you improve your skills
and expand your knowledge. You will  meet other leaders,

/438-WoodBadge.desc:
Join us for this life-changing training event!
Reflecting the best of nearly a century of Scouting experience, Wood Badge draws upon the most current leadership models used by corporate America, academic circles and successful organizations throughout the country.
Wood Badge is designed to meet the advanced leadership needs of all Scouters, particularly unit level Scouters, such as Cub leaders, Scoutmasters and assistants, Venturing Crew Advisors, Committee Chairs and members. Additionally, Scouters serving at the district and council levels can achieve greater effectiveness through Wood Badge.
By taking Wood Badge, Scouters will acquire valuable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning and leading change. Participants will learn to understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our society. They will learn skills that will make them a better Scout leader. Units with trained leaders can deliver an improved program and a more meaningful experience for the youth Scouting serves.
Wood Badge courses sell out quickly!
Your registration cost must be paid in full to guarantee your spot in the course.
Need financial assistance? Just ask!
Contact the course director to speak confidentially about a Wood Badge scholarship!
Qualifications:
To attend a Wood Badge course, you must:
Be a registered member of Scouting America, 18 years of age or older
Have completed the basic training courses for your Scouting position.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
All participants are required to complete the Annual Health and Medical Record form (parts A, B and C)
You must be able to attend all sessions

Skilled Trades Merit Badge Workshops and Career Connections
We are thrilled to announce that our brand new, state-of-the-art Dever Family Foundation Skilled Trades Education Center at Camp Friedlander is open! This center provides a safe, effective, and unique venue to introduce, educate, and instruct Scouts in skilled trades and the fulfilling careers they offer.
Join us for a fun and hands-on workshop dedicated to exploring the world of trade skills. This event will provide an opportunity to learn new skills, earn trade skills merit badges, and explore exciting career paths.
Youth can attend a morning and afternoon session and take:
Merit Badge offerings January 24, March 28, September 26 and November 14
Automotive Maintenance
Plumbing
Home Repairs and Painting
Welding
Robotics
Electricity
Merit Badge offerings February 28, August 22, October 17 and December 12

Please note that different Workshop dates offer different Merit Badge opportunities.  Scouts are encouraged to attend multiple days and earn multiple merit badges.
Merit Badge Completion: Please remember that only the 'hands-on' requirements are guaranteed to be completed during the day.
