/438-summercamp27.desc:
Camp Friedlander is the premier Scouts BSA Summer Camp program with a wide variety of merit badge options, activities for younger and older Scouts, training opportunities for adult leaders, and some of the best camping facilities in the country. Each summer, thousands of Scouts from across the nation (and the world!) make Camp Friedlander their summer camp home for a fun week of learning, achievement, leadership, and Scouting at its best.
Registration Timeline:
Registration is now open!
10/1/2026 - Scouts and Leaders may be added to registrations. Scouts attending as individual campers and day campers may also begin registering. Campsite deposits end, at least one individual must be on a registration.
3/5/2027 - Merit Badge Selection Opens. Registered Scouts may begin selecting activities at 9am. They do not need to be paid in full.
5/1/2027 - Late Fee Begins: $15 charge to any new Scout additions to your registration. Adults and new crossovers do not incur a late fee.
30 Days Prior to Arrival - Deadline to Request Refunds: All non-medical refund requests must be submitted.
10 Days Prior to Arrival - Registration Closes, Final Payments Due
Pre-Camp Orientation Meeting
On February 28 at 7pm, we will host our annual Pre-Camp Orientation Meeting. This virtual meeting will go over existing programs, unveil new programs and activities for the summer, and have a question and answer session with the Camp Director! A link to join will be sent out to your Troop's registration contact a week before the event, and they may share with whoever they think will benefit from attending.
Day Camp
Looking to get more out of camp? Sign up for Day Camp! Day Campers are able to select from any of the Merit Badge offerings* our overnight campers have, and get dropped off before their first and picked up after their last session each day. Day Campers are welcome to attend our open programs on Friday, as well as attend the closing campfire Friday evening.
*Merit Badges that require an overnight component, such as Astronomy or Wilderness Survival, may be taken but will not be completed by Day Campers.
Camp Guide
Check out our Camp Guide in the "Attachments" section for more information on preparing for camp, refund policies, registration assistance, and much more!

/438-wfa.desc:
Wilderness First Aid (WFA) is a course for everyone planning a remote high adventure ranging from lay responders to medical professionals. It focuses on prevention, assessment, and treatment for an ill or injured person in a remote environment where definitive care by a physician and/or rapid transport is not readily available. This is defined as being an hour or more away from advanced care.
Diagnosis and care for injuries and illnesses occurring outside the 911 response envelope.  This weekend class prepares you to handle serious back-country emergencies.  Wilderness First Aid is a comprehensive series of lessons in how to react and respond in remote, life threatening situations.  Lots of activity and hands-on work in classroom and outdoor scenarios keeps it fun!
You should bring a pad of paper and a pen for notes and you may want to bring a water bottle as well. All other supplies are provided. The class is broken down into several parts: lecture, hands-on skill practice and outdoor simulations.  We will be outside for significant lengths of time, so please bring weather dependent clothing.
*Please note this training is required for two adult participants leading a High Adventure trip.
We must have a minumum of 5 participants registered 30 days prior to the first day of training or the training will be canceled. IF the training is cancelled, you will be notified 29-25 days before the event from the email NO-REPLY@247SCOUTING.COM. Please make sure that email is labeled a safe sender in your email provider.

/440-106062.desc:
Scoutmaster Basic Training
Are you a new Scoutmaster or ASM?  Thank you for jumping into the volcano!
Scoutmaster Basic Training will give you all the tools you need to lead and train the youth of your Scout Troop.  And we'll do it in an outdoor experience that will give you a lived appreciation for the challenges of a youth learning to lead in a weekend campout.
In this course, you will learn how to deliver on the promise we made to your youth when they signed up for Scouting.  You will learn your proper role in a youth-led unit.  You'll learn how to help them plan, organize and deliver the troop's program.  You'll find new resources and learn how to work with your Troop Committee.  You will get hands-on experience with all the outdoor Scout skills required for a new scout to advance.  You'll learn not only how to be comfortable on a campout but how to teach your other leaders to be successful, too.  You will live the Patrol Method.  After completing this training, you will know how to deliver the full Scouting Program to your Troop.
This course integrates the Scoutmaster Position-Specific Training with the Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills training which are required for all Scoutmasters and ASMs and recommended for any adult leader of outdoor events.
Safeguarding Youth Training (Y01) and Hazardous Weather (SCO_800) are prerequisites for this course. Both can be taken online at
my.scouting.org
.
Please come prepared to be outdoors all weekend.  You will need your Scout Uniform, tent, sleeping bag and pad, mess kit, etc.  A detailed list of what to bring will be sent via e-mail upon registration for the course.  The course textbook is your Scouts BSA Handbook (current edition).
All food, facilities & course materials are included in the course fee.
Note: Your completed registration will be acknowledged by automatic email. But … you are not ACCEPTED into this course until you have RESPONDED to a personal email from the Course Director.
Future Offerings:
Scoutmaster Basic Training is offered the second full weekends of each April and September.  Check the Council Calendar for future dates.  Registration for next year's sessions will open in October.

/440-114301.desc:
WILDERNESS FIRST AID TRAINING
Sponsored by the Lake Erie Council
Curriculum Developed by the Emergency Care & Safety Institute & Officially Endorsed by Scouting America
The Wilderness First Aid course, developed in conjunction with Scouting America is great for Scouts and Scout leaders, outdoor enthusiasts, or people who work in an outdoor environment, including camp staff members. Be prepared for your next backpacking or high adventure trip with Wilderness First Aid! WFA certification is also now a pre-requisite for at least one adult leader on each high adventure crew.
Anyone who works or plays outdoors needs specialized first aid training - training which encompasses all phases of back country emergencies, and which focuses on extended care issues. Wilderness First Aid will teach proper backcountry emergency response for those who live, work, or play in remote areas. The course is for anyone who participates in activities away from traditional EMS service – when there may be a significant delay in arrival of outside assistance or the need to move the victim to more advanced treatment.
Certified and experienced instructors will cover victim assessment, urgent first aid techniques and appropriate decision-making. It is appropriate for anyone regardless of experience level. This sixteen hour course relies upon a combination of classroom instruction, skills practice and outdoor rescue scenarios to teach the response steps and treatment of injuries and illnesses when definitive help is delayed.
All participants will be receiving the E-Book.

Induction workshop is a Lodge training day held at Fireland Scout Reservation that is divided into two basic tracks - Elangomat and Ceremonialist
Lunch and Dinner will be provided
Elangomat Track -The Erielhonan Lodge Elangomat Track is designed to teach future elangomats the symbolism and meaning of all aspects of the ordeal so they can help our candidates better understand the ordeal and our Order. This training enables future elangomats to lead ordeal candidates through their ordeal and set them up for future success in our Order.
Participants will:
Learn the purpose, symbolism, and meaning behind each element of the Ordeal experience.
Understand the elangomat’s role as a friend, guide, and example of the OA’s values.
Develop leadership, communication, and service-oriented skills tailored to the Ordeal.
Gain practical tools for handling challenges, supporting candidates, and reinforcing the OA’s purpose.
Ceremonies Track -The Erielhonan Lodge Ceremonies Track is designed to develop skilled and knowledgeable Arrowmen who are committed to preserving and delivering the meaningful traditions of the Order of the Arrow. This training equips new and experienced members alike with the tools needed to conduct impactful and respectful ceremonies that uphold the values of brotherhood, cheerfulness, and service.
Participants will:
Learn the purpose and significance behind the Pre-Ordeal and Ordeal ceremonies.
Explore ceremonial principles rooted in symbolism, tradition, and the Scout Oath and Law.
Develop strong public speaking, character portrayal, and staging skills.
Practice ceremonies in a supportive environment with constructive feedback.

/440-91026.desc:
Scoutmaster Basic Training
Are you a new Scoutmaster or ASM?  Thank you for jumping into the volcano!
Scoutmaster Basic Training will give you all the tools you need to lead and train the youth of your Scout Troop.  And we'll do it in an outdoor experience that will give you a lived appreciation for the challenges of a youth learning to lead in a weekend campout.
In this course, you will learn how to deliver on the promise we made to your youth when they signed up for Scouting.  You will learn your proper role in a youth-led unit.  You'll learn how to help them plan, organize and deliver the troop's program.  You'll find new resources and learn how to work with your Troop Committee.  You will get hands-on experience with all the outdoor Scout skills required for a new scout to advance.  You'll learn not only how to be comfortable on a campout but how to teach your other leaders to be successful, too.  You will live the Patrol Method.  After completing this training, you will know how to deliver the full Scouting Program to your Troop.
This course integrates the Scoutmaster Position-Specific Training with the Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills training which are required for all Scoutmasters and ASMs and recommended for any adult leader of outdoor events.
Safeguarding Youth Training (Y01) and Hazardous Weather (SCO_800) are prerequisites for this course. Both can be taken online at
my.scouting.org
.
Please come prepared to be outdoors all weekend.  You will need your Scout Uniform, tent, sleeping bag and pad, mess kit, etc.  A detailed list of what to bring will be sent via e-mail upon registration for the course.  The course textbook is your Scouts BSA Handbook (current edition).
All food, facilities & course materials are included in the course fee.
Note: Your completed registration will be acknowledged by automatic email. But … you are not ACCEPTED into this course until you have RESPONDED to a personal email from the Course Director.
Future Offerings:
Scoutmaster Basic Training is offered the second full weekends of each April and September.  Check the Council Calendar for future dates.  Registration for next year's sessions will open in October.

/440-98828.desc:
WILDERNESS FIRST AID TRAINING
Sponsored by the Lake Erie Council
Curriculum Developed by the Emergency Care & Safety Institute (ECSI) & Officially Endorsed by Scouting America
The Wilderness First Aid course, developed in conjunction with Scouting America, is great for Scouts and Scout leaders, outdoor enthusiasts, or people who work in an outdoor environment, including camp staff members. Be prepared for your next backpacking or high adventure trip with Wilderness First Aid! The course meets the requirements for Scouting America High Adventure WFA prerequisites.
The course is for anyone who participates in activities away from traditional EMS service – when you are on your own.  The course will cover how to handle the situation at hand, and what to do if there will be a significant delay in arrival of outside assistance or there is a need to move the victim for more advanced treatment.
Certified and experienced instructors will cover primary and secondary victim assessments, urgent first aid techniques, appropriate decision-making, and CPR/AED techniques.  Previous first aid or CPR training is not required, but it is preferred that Scout participants have the first aid merit badge.   The course relies upon a combination of classroom instruction, skills practice and outdoor rescue scenarios to teach the response steps and treatment of injuries and illnesses when definitive help is delayed.
The general weekend course format is:
Friday 6PM-9:30PM
Saturday 7:30AM – 9:30PM
Sunday 7:30AM – 11AM
Housing and meals are included in the registration.  To be complainant with SAFE Guarding Youth guidelines separate cabins will be available for M & F adults and M & F Scouts.
By default, all registrants will receive a copy of the ECSI WFA eBook.  However, it is recommended that first time participants select the hard copy book upgrade, so they have something easy to reference/review during the course weekend, and also to retain for future reference.

/444-BuckskinTrailFall2027.desc:
2027 Buckskin Fall Course
Course Dates:
Wednesday – Sept 1
Wednesday – Sept 8
Weekend – Sept 17 - 19
Location:
Cricket Holler Scout Camp
6675 Brantford Rd, Dayton, OH 45414
Course Fee:
TBD
What is Buckskin?
The Buckskin Trail course is a fun and exciting course geared toward Cub Scout and Scouts BSA leadership! Participants are put into patrols within a model troop allowing them to experience the patrol method of scouting.
The course is designed to emphasize the outdoor experience, camping and outdoor skills. It incorporates the national BALOO (Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation) training for Cub leaders, and IOLS (Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills) training for Scouts BSA leaders.
A Pack offering camping experiences to Cub Scouts is required to have at least one BALOO trained leader overseeing the preparation and camping experience of the event. Adult leaders registered as Scoutmaster or Assistant Scoutmaster are required to complete IOLS training in conjunction with the online position-specific training. The overall goal of Buckskin is to offer a hands-on outdoor skills and safety program that can be shared with youth in a dynamic and fun way.
Who should attend Buckskin?
The Buckskin Trail is available for all scouting leaders. To most benefit Cub leaders, it is recommended to attend as a Bear, Webelos or Arrow of Light leader. Attending during that time will allow you to gain experience in the patrol method found in the Arrow of Light requirements. You will learn what it is like to be a new scout within a Scouts BSA troop setting, allowing you to better prepare your young scouts for the transition from an adult led unit to a scout led unit. It will also ensure the fundamentals of IOLS that are needed as a Scoutmaster/Assistant Scoutmaster have been learned closer to your leader transition from Cub Scouts to Scouts BSA.
All Cub leaders are required to complete the on-line BALOO training modules prior to attending Buckskin and bring proof of the training to the course.
What to expect?
The course is held over two Wednesday evenings and one full weekend. Participants will tent camp as a patrol similar to a Scouts BSA troop. An additional outside Patrol meeting or meetings may be necessary.
Whether you are new to scouting, were a scout as a youth or have some time under your belt, the Buckskin Trail has something to offer you. New friends and connections from other units around the Council will be made. The latest updates and changes to the scouting program will be presented. Most importantly, you will experience FUN in scouting and learn how to incorporate that in your units.
We look forward to seeing you on the next Buckskin Trail course!

/444-NYLT2027.desc:
Embark on a quest to complete your premier youth training!
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth with leadership skills and experience that they can apply within their troops and in other situations requiring leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a six-day course that emphasizes hands-on learning in a fun, engaging environment. Through a blend of activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and games, participants will develop confidence and leadership abilities while working together as a team.
The course content is designed to build leadership concepts progressively, using practical exercises to reinforce learning. Participants embark on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership, which brings the leadership lessons to life as they apply their skills throughout the course.
Who Should Attend?
NYLT is designed to build the leadership of all Scouts, particularly those in, or planning to take on leadership positions in their unit.
To attend an NYLT course, youth must meet the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form including parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members must:
Be at least 13 years old by the first day of the course and no older than 17 years.
Have completed the Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops training.
Achieved the rank of First Class.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must:
Be at least 14 years old (or 13 and completed eighth grade) and be no older than 20 years.
Completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships training.
Have some basic camping experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.
Why Attend?
By taking NYLT, Scouts will acquire valuable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning and leading change.  Participants will learn to understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our society.  They will learn skills that will make them a better Scout leader.

/456-114119.desc:
Wood Badge 2027
Camp Betz
What is Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is advanced leadership training for Cub Scout, Scouts BSA and Venturing adult leaders at the unit, district, council, and professional levels. It is taught by living the experience of a Scouts BSA Troop, utilizing the patrol method, over two weekends.
Wood Badge is about learning and developing Leadership skills, rather than basic Scouting skills - skills that can be used in Scouting and in all facets of life.
By using a variety of learning techniques, including lectures, demonstrations, group discussions, and hands on exercises, participants will learn contemporary leadership skills and tools needed to provide the youth members of their units with the highest scouting experience.
A Wood Badge course teaches leadership skills by focusing on five key areas: Living the Values, Growing, Connecting, Guiding and Empowering.
What to Expect:
The course will be delivered over
two weekends
and one orientation meeting ahead of the course.
Please note the 7 AM CST start time for both weekends.
Pre-Course Orientation
: 6:30 PM - 9:00 PM, Thursday, March 11, 2027. St. Michael's Church in La Grange Park, IL.
Weekend 1
: 7:00 AM, Friday, April 9 - 5:00 PM, Sunday, April 11, 2027. Camp Betz.
Weekend 2
: 7:00 AM, Saturday, May 1 - 5:00 PM, Sunday, May 2, 2027. Camp Betz.
Participants must be registered members of Scouting America, have current Safeguarding Youth Training, provide a current Scouting America Medical Form Part A, B, C and be "Trained" for their registered position.
During both weekends, participants will tent camp. During the first weekend all meals will be prepared by the staff. During the second weekend, most meals will be prepared using the patrol method, in patrol campsites.
Scholarships are available!

Save the Date
2027 Summer
National Youth Leadership Training
About NYLT
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for Scouts to gain leadership skills and experience they can use in their home units and in other situations demanding direction of self and others. Courses will be held at Camp Betz in Berrien Springs, Michigan.
Participant Qualifications
All participants must be a registered member of a Scouting America troop, crew or ship. Members of a Scouts BSA troop must be at least
13 years of age
and at least
First Class
.
All participants should have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills.
Transportation to/from camp will not be provided.
NYLT patrols may be coed, with a minimum of two Scouts of a gender in a patrol.
2027 Dates
(all listed times are Central/Chicago time)
Session 1
Course: Sunday, June 6, 2027 at 1:00pm - Friday June 11, 2027 at 8:00pm
Closing Banquet: Friday, June 11 at 6:00pm
Session 2
Course: Sunday, June 13, 2027 at 1:00pm - Friday, June 18, 2027 at 8:00pm
Closing Banquet: Friday, June 18 at 6:00pm
2027 Fees
Deposit: $150 due at time of registration
Course: $325 ($375 if not paid in full before 5/7/2027 for Session 1 or 5/14/2027 for Session 2)
Banquet: $15 per person (participant's banquet ticket is included with their course registration)
Scholarship Information
Council Scholarship:
The Pathway to Adventure Council NYLT Scholarship is available to any Scout registered in a Troop, Crew, Ship or Post. Scholarships usually do not exceed 50% of the fee. The allocation process, and information used in it, is confidential and will not be shared outside of PTAC professional staff.
Fearless Girl Scholarship:
The Fearless Girl NYLT Scholarship is available to girls registered in a Scouts BSA troop.  It was launched in 2018 by industry mavens, Amy Shelly and Joanne Moffic-Silver, the first women to break the glass ceiling by Chairing the prestigious LaSalle Street Event; supported by Chicago’s financial district for nearly 50 years.
Only two young women per troop can qualify per year. Scoutmasters must complete the recommendation form below.
Scouts should register through the Black Pug event link on this page, and the required deposit must be paid up front. Once the Scout completes NYLT and returns the post-course survey from the funding committee, the deposit will be refunded.
No-shows will not be refunded; NYLT cancellation policy applies.
If you have any questions, or if a Scout needs additional support to be successful at this event, please email
nyltptac@gmail.com
.

Wilderness and Remote
First Aid Certification Class
Course Length:
16 hours - attendance and participation for the full schedule is required to receive certification.  This class meets the requirements established by Scouting America for participating in high adventure.
6:00 PM -10:00 PM Friday and 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Saturday
2027 dates are subject to a change in location. Unless otherwise noted, classes will be at the Pleasantview Fire Protection District.
November 13 - 14, 2026
January 8 - 9, 2027
February 5 - 6, 2027
March 5 - 6, 2027
April 2 - 3, 2027
May 7 - 8, 2027
Length of Certification:
2 years
Who can attend:
Any registered youth or adult Scout age 14 or older.
Pre-requisites:
Adult CPR/AED card from any agency that was issued within 12 months of class is required.  A copy of your certification will need to be emailed to the instructor prior to class.  If you need Adult CPR/AED contact Cathy Prosser,
prosserc@aol.com
, to arrange for a blended learning class with the in-person portion to be completed during the WFA class.  Additional cost of $22.00, cash at class.  On line pre-work is required, about 2.5 hours.
Cost:
$70.00 for in-council attendees; $80.00 for out-of-council attendees – Includes Red Cross Wilderness and Remote First Aid Manual and Pocket Guide.
Meal plan (
Food NOT provided
):
Friday:  Eat dinner before you come or bring a sack dinner.  Water bottle.
Saturday:  Eat breakfast before you arrive.  Bring lunch, dinner and snacks that do not require refrigeration or heating.  Water bottle.  Pack food that can be eaten as class continues.  We will not take any formal breaks and will not be leaving campus.
What to wear/materials:
Wear clothing suitable to spend time outside intermittently on Saturday, check the weather before you come.  No special materials needed for class, instructors will provide what is needed.
Please let me know if there are any questions or concerns.  Looking forward to seeing everyone!

/456-122278.desc:
BASIC ADULT LEADER OUTDOOR ORIENTATION
When: Saturday, April 17 - Sunday, April 18, 2027
Where: Camp Palos, Lemont IL
Cost is $45.
BALOO is the Cub Scout leader training required for any Cub Scout den or pack outdoor event, including pack camping overnighters and Webelos den overnighters.
BALOO training is comprised of two components—an online component and this practical, hands-on component. Both must be completed to qualify as BALOO trained. The online component is available through the Scouting America LearnCenter at
my.scouting.org
and must be completed
prior

/460-BALOO.desc:
Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO)
Get Ready for Cub Scout Outdoor Adventures
BALOO (Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation) is the required outdoor training for Cub Scout leaders who want to conduct safe and successful overnight camping experiences. This course combines online learning with an immersive, hands-on outdoor weekend to prepare you to lead Pack and Webelos overnight events with confidence.
Course Requirements
BALOO training consists of
two required components:
Online Training -
Complete the BALOO online course through the Scouting America Learn Center at my.scouting.org before attending the in-person course.
Hands-On Outdoor Training
- Attend the weekend of practical training.
Please bring a copy of your online course completion certificate with you to check-in.
You must complete both portions to be recognized as a Trained BALOO Leader.
Why Take BALOO?
Scouting America requires that
at least one registered adult
attending any Cub Scout Pack or Webelos overnight campout be BALOO trained.
During the course, you'll learn how to:
Plan and lead successful Pack overnight camping trips
Conduct safe outdoor activities for Cub Scouts
Organize engaging campfire programs
Cook outdoors using Cub Scout-appropriate methods
Select and properly use camping equipment
Lead outdoor games, ceremonies, and other activities
Apply Scouting America's outdoor safety guidelines

/460-NYLT.desc:
Become the Leader Your Unit Needs
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is Scouting America's premier leadership course for Scouts BSA and Venturing youth. This exciting six-day outdoor experience builds confidence, strengthens leadership skills, and prepares participants to lead both in Scouting and in everyday life.
NYLT is the next step in the Scouting leadership journey, building on the leadership training received in a Scout's home unit. Through hands-on activities, team challenges, discussions, and outdoor adventures, participants learn practical leadership skills they can immediately apply in their troop, crew, school, workplace, and community.
Throughout the week, participants are placed into a model unit where they experience the patrol method in action while learning from an outstanding youth-led staff supported by experienced adult advisors. The course is fast-paced, interactive, and designed to challenge participants while making leadership fun.
Course Schedule
NYLT is a
six-day resident course.
Check-in:
12:00 PM
Course Begins:
1:00 PM
Course Concludes:
Approximately 6:00 PM
Please note:
Lunch is not provided on the first day (Sunday) and dinner is not provided on the final day (Friday).
What Participants Will Learn
During NYLT, Scouts will:
Build confidence as leaders.
Develop effective communication and teamwork skills.
Learn how successful teams are formed and grow.
Practice planning, problem-solving, and decision-making.
Experience the stages of team development through real-world challenges.
Create a personal vision for leading in their home unit.
Form lasting friendships with Scouts from across the council.
Have an unforgettable week of adventure and fun.
Who Can Attend?
Participants Must:
Be registered in a Scouts BSA troop or Venturing crew.
Be at least
13 years old
by the first day of the course.
Be under
18 years old
for Scouts BSA (under 21 for Venturers).
Have completed their home unit's youth leader training.
Demonstrate proficiency in basic camping skills.
Receive approval from their Scoutmaster or Venturing Advisor.
Because most Scouts attend NYLT only once, participants should be prepared for an advanced leadership experience that requires maturity, teamwork, and active participation.
Course Experience
NYLT is designed to model a month in the life of a Scout unit. The first part of the course features meetings, planning sessions, and leadership instruction that prepare participants for an exciting overnight outpost experience later in the week.
As the course progresses, each team works together on a leadership challenge that allows participants to apply everything they have learned. Throughout the week, the youth staff demonstrates effective leadership while participants build their own "leadership toolbox" filled with practical skills they can take back to their home unit.
The course begins with teams creating a shared vision and concludes with each participant developing a personal plan to put their new leadership skills into action.
Why Attend NYLT?
NYLT is more than a leadership course—it's an experience that challenges Scouts to grow, inspires them to serve others, and equips them with skills that will benefit them for years to come.
Whether leading a patrol, serving in a troop leadership position, or preparing for future opportunities in school, college, or a career, NYLT provides leadership lessons that last a lifetime.

/460-WFA.desc:
Be Prepared for the Unexpected
Whether you're heading to a Scouting America High Adventure Base or planning a backcountry trek, Wilderness First Aid (WFA) provides the knowledge and confidence to respond when professional medical help is more than 30 minutes away.
A current CPR certification is required before attending this course.
CPR training is NOT included with this class.
Course Information
Date:
February 20 and 21, 2027
Time:
8:00 AM - 5:00 PM each day
Location:
Camp Miakonda, Wildlife Center
Traveling from outside the area?
Limited overnight accommodations may be available. If you need lodging assistance, please contact Chuck Walker before registering.
What You'll Learn
This 16-hour certification course combines classroom instruction with realistic outdoor scenarios to prepare participants for medical emergencies in remote environments.
Participants will learn how to:
Assess and manage wilderness medical emergencies
Treat common backcountry injuries and illnesses
Make decisions when emergency services are delayed
Lead and care for a group during an emergency
Practice hands-on skills in outdoor scenarios
This course meets the Wilderness First Aid requirement for participants attending Scouting America High Adventure Bases.
Registration Information
Erie Shores Council Participants:
Free
Out-of-Council Participants:
$95 (includes WFA handbook and course materials)
Please note:
Pre-registration and payment are required.
Registration is limited to
24 participants.
Cancellations after the registration deadline (February 1) are non-refundable except in emergency circumstances.
Before You Attend
Please come prepared for both indoor and outdoor instruction.
Participants should:
Dress in weather-appropriate clothing (layers recommended)
Bring a backpack with practical outdoor items for scenario-based exercises
Hold a current CPR certification
Be at least
16 years old (Scouts BSA youth should have already earned the
Have a solid understanding of basic first aid skills
Certification
Erie Shores Council is a certified education center of the
Emergency Care & Safety Institute (ECSI)
and an official training partner of Scouting America. Upon successful completion, participants will receive Wilderness First Aid certification.

This 16-hour, overnight course trains interested scouters ages 18 and older to serve as Leave No Trace Level 1 Instructors. Level 1 Instructors are the backbone of Scouting’s outdoor ethics program, providing instruction to individuals and units wishing to adopt cutting-edge outdoor ethics into their unit programs. Level 1 Instructors are specially commissioned to teach the BSA Leave No Trace Basics course and to qualify individuals for the BSA Leave No Trace Basics card.  Each BSA Level 1 Instructors course is led by a recognized Leave No Trace Level 2 Instructors, so your Level 1 Instructors standing is recognized nationally by the BSA’s partner, Leave No Trace.
Instructed by: Leave No Trace Level 2 Instructors
Participants receive: Leave No Trace Level 1 Instructor card from the BSA, BSA Leave No Trace Basics Course Guide, Leave No Trace Level 1 Instructor certificate from Leave No Trace, and other Leave No Trace teaching resources.

/480-122579.desc:
Fall Encampment is an encampment for Scouts BSA Boy and Girl Troops and Venturers to learn in-depth skills and unique opportunities. A wide variety of experiences are offered each year. /488-120807.desc:
In-Person Blackbaud Training
We are pleased to announce that John Kuehn, National BSA CRM Application Specialist, will be conducting in-person beginner (101) and intermediate (201) Blackbaud courses at the Indian Nations Council office in Tulsa, Oklahoma Monday, February 22 – Thursday, February 25th.  Be sure to register early, registration is limited to provide more individual attention!
Who should attend:  FOS Clerks, Development support personnel, Development Directors to Directors of Development.
Blackbaud 101 – Begins at 8:30AM on Monday, February 22nd and will conclude at 11AM on Tuesday, February 23rd
This two day of training is for new users of the Blackbaud CRM and new to Revenue Data Entry. Understanding the creation of four Constituent types in CRM; how to use and maintain them is the backbone of the data. To enhance your success in CRM, we will be diving into each CRM functional area. Topic to cover – CRM Navigation, CRM Personalization, Constituent Management, Simple Reports and Data List, Revenue Entry (how it works and what drives it to the correct PeopleSoft Account).
Blackbaud 201 – Begins at 1PM on Tuesday, February 23rd and will conclude by Noon on Thursday, February 25th.
Discover the higher functions of CRM. We will cover some of the basics and then jump into Constituencies, Prospect Management, Gift Plans (Moves Management), Planned Giving, Reports Vs. Queries, Creating simple queries, Prospect list and Donor Research. The information that you place in CRM today benefits you and your fellow colleagues now and for the future. In the two days of training there will be hands-on exercises and opportunity for you to ask questions.
All participants will need to bring a laptop.
Each course is $200 but there is a $50 discount if you register for both courses.  Lunches will be provided Monday through Wednesday.  Councils are responsible for all other meals, hotel and travel.
Hotel Recommendations include:
Hampton Inn Tulsa/Broken Arrow – Close to the Scout Office and includes Free Breakfast
TownePlace Suites by Marriott Tulsa Broken Arrow – Close to the Scout Office and includes Free Breakfast
Hotel Indigo Tulsa Downtown – It’s a little more, downtown, 14 minutes from the office but puts you in the middle of the Blue Dome District surrounded by great restaurants and bars
The Mayo Hotel – You may be familiar with this historic hotel if you watched the TV series “Tulsa King”.  It too is downtown and 6-8 blocks from the Blue Dome District
Registration:
https://scoutingevent.com/488-120807
to Register   If you miss the cutoff, please leave your name on the wait list.  This will help national determine need for additional training opportunities and provide a list of those that want them.
Refund Policy:  100% refund will be given if individual cancellation is received at least 30 days or more prior to class start.  No refund given if cancellation is received within 30 days of class start.
For any questions concerning the course, please contact Laura Lovell at 530-770-1152 or laura.lovell@scouting.org.
For assistant with a refund if needed, please contact Jenny Brown at 918-392-1221.

What is Short-Term Camp Administrator Training?
Beginning January 1, 2021 a short-term camp is any council-organized overnight camping program, whether one-time or continuing, that is one, two, or three nights in length where the council or its agents provide the staffing and may provide program and food services, and includes camps conducted off council properties.
Each short-term camp must have a short-term camp administrator. This person is responsible for ensuring that the planned camp complies with the NCAP Short-term Camp Standards.  This means walking the property to ensure that it is appropriate for the event; ensuring that paperwork is filed and any written BSA approvals are completed and obtained through the council; confirms facilities and program are safe and in good order before starting operation; and that appropriate health, safety, and sanitation provisions are made.  This individual also ensures that all activities at the short-term camp comply with the applicable BSA National Camp Standards.
Advanced Registration is required by November 1, 2026 to receive Early Bird Pricing

All meals will be provided, and participants will get to experience the best our staff has to offer, including flag ceremonies, campfire and activities to keep you and your scouts engaged all weekend.
Cub Scout Super Weekend is put on by our Council's Order of the Arrow Lodge. /492-baldwin27.desc:
Camp Baldwin
Built on Grit. Defined by Adventure.
Renowned as the pride of the CPC, Camp Baldwin is the ultimate high-adventure destination for Scouts. Tucked deep in the Mt. Hood National Forest, this rugged camp delivers non-stop outdoor action — from horseback riding, mountain biking, and rock climbing to whitewater rafting, and more. Surrounded by towering evergreens and roaming wildlife, Baldwin is where you push limits, build skills, and create stories worth telling.
Learn More on Our Website:
Summer Camps Website
Main Features
Horsemanship Program
Hit the trail. Live the adventure.
Saddle up for trail rides deep into the Mt. Hood National Forest. Choose afternoon rides or overnight trips with a cowboy campfire and hearty old west breakfast. Older Scouts can level up in the
CL
Wrangler-in-Training program, learning advanced riding skills while working side-by-side with our wranglers.
High Adventure Outbounds
Go big. Go beyond.
Pack your days with adrenaline-fueled trips beyond camp! Tackle Class 3+ rapids on the Deschutes River or take on the Lower Deschutes while earning your Whitewater merit badge. Hit Mt. Hood’s Summer Adventure Park, explore historic landmarks like the Pioneer Woman’s Grave and Timberline Lodge, and hike the stunning White River trail.
Rock Climbing
Climb higher. Think bolder.
Along Calypso Canyon, the towering crags of Vulture Rocks rise over 100 feet—perfect for an unforgettable climbing experience. At Camp Baldwin, we don't pull on plastic, Scouts climb real rock, gaining skills and confidence on natural surfaces that can’t be replicated on a climbing tower.
Mountain Biking & Boarding
Ride the Ridge
If you love speed, flow, and forest trails, our mountain biking and boarding programs are ready for you. Camp Baldwin’s terrain is built for adventure, offering daily opportunities to ride through the pines on bike or board. From beginner-friendly routes to more challenging single-track sections, there’s something for every skill level.
Feast on This
Cook big. Eat bigger.
Campers cook half their meals right in the campsite, which supports Scouting's long-standing focus on developing teamwork and leadership skills using the Patrol Method. Everything is provided, including equipment, stoves, propane, and mess kits. You don't have to bring a thing except an appetite. All other meals are served to you hot and ready.
Rover Camp for Provisional Lone Scouts
Rover camp is offered during Session 3.
For Scouts unable to join their troop for summer camp or those who desire an extra week of adventure, there's an exciting opportunity: Rover Camp. Individual Scouts can sign up for a dedicated Rover Camp week, where they'll connect with fellow provisional Scouts upon arrival and form a cohesive Rover Troop making friends with youth from across the country. Adult leadership is provided by the camp.
Operating akin to a regular Scout Troop, Rover Troops engage in the full spectrum of summer camp activities, ensuring every Rover Scout experiences the same thrill and camaraderie as they would with their home troop.

/492-meriwether27.desc:
Camp Meriwether
The Ultimate Adventure on the Pacific Coast means discovery, adventure and fun like you can’t get anywhere else.
Camp Meriwether is located on the scenic Oregon Coast, one of the only Scout camps to feature an ocean beach. The beach-front property’s warm coastal breeze and high-adventure activities attract thousands of Scouts to this premier camp each year.
Learn More On Our Website:
Summer Camps Website
Oceanfront Discovery
With full beach access, Scouts dive into oceanography by exploring tide pools and rock formations. Our popular Polar Bear Swim and ocean-surf wading are highlights of Camp Meriwether. Plus, camp would not be complete without a bonfire on the beach.
Go Back in Time at Lewis & Clark’s Fort Clatsop
With a full-scale replica of Fort Clatsop, Lewis & Clark’s winter camp in 1805, Scouts can immerse themselves in the skills the real Corps of Discovery relied on during their journey west, including blacksmithing, candle-making, and black powder rifle marksmanship. Staff even dress in period-accurate clothing and give tours as members of the expedition to add to the experience.
Land Sailing
Take the ultimate ride on the beach with our new land sails! Learn to skid across the sand and zip down the beach in this incredibly fun, safe activity you’ll only find at Camp Meriwether.
World-Class Shooting
An Olympic-level shotgun range, the chance to fire a black powder rifle, and new rifle and archery ranges that each accommodate 16+ Scouts at once make Camp Meriwether the safest way to have a blast in the BSA.
Rover Camp for Provisional Lone Scouts
Rover camp is offered during Session 5 and Session 6.
For Scouts unable to join their troop for summer camp or those who desire an extra week of adventure, there's an exciting opportunity: Rover Camp. Individual Scouts can sign up for a dedicated Rover Camp week, where they'll connect with fellow provisional Scouts upon arrival and form a cohesive Rover Troop. Adult leadership is provided by the camp.
Operating akin to a regular Scout Troop, Rover Troops engage in the full spectrum of summer camp activities, ensuring every Rover Scout experiences the same thrill and camaraderie as they would with their home troop.

/492-nylt.desc:
NYLT is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home Troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a six-day course. Content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ the leadership skills.
National Youth Leadership Training
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must KNOW, and what a leader must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and audio-visual support, NYLT participants will be engaged in a unified approach to leadership that will give them the skill and confidence to lead well. Through a wide range of activities, games, and adventures, participants will work and play together as they put into action the best Scouting has to off
In order to attend a NYLT course
A youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA youth must be at least 13 and have achieved the rank of First Class.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade.
Recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience.
Must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills (ILST).
Have a unit leader recommendation.
Cascade Pacific Council is offering two courses in 2027:
Course #1: June 27 - July 2, 2027 at Camp Pioneer
Course #2: July 18 - 23, 2027 at Camp Baldwin
Cost
$448.00. A $50 non-refundable deposit is due at the time of registration. A non-refundable $150 per youth deposit is due to continue to hold your spot on March 1st. Final payment due by
June 1, 2026

Cancellations on or before March 1st:
all fees paid are transferable within the reservation. If the entire reservation is cancelled, the $50 per scout is forfeited.

/492-pioneer27.desc:
Camp Pioneer
For Scouts. By Scouts.
Pioneer is where the ordinary ends and the epic begins. Whether you’re questing through immersive roleplay or trekking across volcanic ridgelines, every path leads to personal growth. It’s a place where you’ll crawl through frigid ice caves, summit mountain peaks, or spend hours strategizing around a tabletop—and somehow, it all builds the same Scout skills: teamwork, resilience, and leadership. At Camp Pioneer, you don’t just attend camp—you live the adventure.
Learn More On Our Website:
Summer Camps Website
Scouts BSA Weeks
Camp Pioneer provides a traditional rugged mountain camp experience, balanced with modern-day Scouting activities. Scouts practice fundamental Scouting skills such as cooking, pioneering and rowing, alongside modern STEM activities which include engineering, inventing and robotics. Merit badges should be educational and fun in nature.
The camp’s small size is used advantageously to provide a highly-flexible program. Badges are earned through hands-on, collaborative processes that excite and prepare Scouts to apply what they learn. At Camp Pioneer, enjoy both wilderness and STEM-oriented exploration!
Who Can Attend?
Troops with their own adult leaders.
All youth and overnight adults must be registered Scouting members.
Eagle Camp
Ready to take a major step toward summiting Scouting?
Eagle Camp is built around preparation, accountability, and focused instruction. It is a focused 3-day experience designed to help Scouts make significant progress on Eagle-required merit badges in a structured, supportive environment without the distractions of a traditional camp schedule.. With preparation and commitment, Scouts can earn up to six Eagle-required merit badges during this program.
Who Can Attend?
Scouts can attend individually (adult leadership provided by the camp) or as part of a Troop with their own leaders.
Open to youth who are prepared to take on Eagle-required merit badges.
All youth and overnight adults must be registered Scouting members.
Cascade Chronicles
A Weeklong Adventure in Gaming, Roleplay, and Epic Quests
Calling all fans of tabletop games, roleplaying adventures, trading card games, and miniature battles! Cascade Chronicles
is a unique summer camp experience for Scouts who love immersive stories, strategy games, and exploring gaming culture.
This program runs Monday through Friday. Scouts are sorted into Guilds based on their interests (e.g., pirates, mages, adventurers). Guilds set the tone for your week of activities—ranging from escape room-style puzzles to treasure hunts and boat battles. This is not a traditional Scout camp week and no merit badges or advancements are offered.
Who Can Attend?
Scouts can attend individually (adult leadership provided by the camp) or as part of a Troop with their own adult leaders.
Open to youth who are ready to conquer the quest!
All youth and overnight adults must be a registered Scouting members.

/492-woodbadge2027.desc:
Reflecting the best of nearly a century of Scouting experience, Wood Badge draws upon the most current leadership models used by corporate America, academic circles and successful organizations throughout the country.
Next Level Leadership
Wood Badge training was started by Baden Powell in 1919 as a way to insure that the leaders of Scout troops were properly trained. Since then Wood Badge has been held worldwide, providing advanced leadership training to thousands of Scout leaders.
Wood Badge builds upon the best traditions and experiences of Scouting America and also draws from a wide range of courses within and beyond the bounds of Scouting to present the latest in leadership theory and team development. This training is perfect for any adult Scout leader, in any registered position in Scouting who wants to improve their scouting program, be a better partner in their personal relationships, and be a better employee or manager in their career.
Participants Must:
Attend both weekends to complete the course.
Complete Pre-Course orientation online modules to introduce a number of Wood Badge topics.
Be registered members of Scouting America. (Youth 18 and older may attend as long as they have completed the adult application and Youth Protection training. Participants under 21 do not need to be registered in an adult leadership role.)
Complete the basic training courses for their Scouting position prior to course.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
Provide the Annual Health and Medical Record form Parts A, B and C.

/502-2027CampMinsiSummer.desc:
Camp Minsi, located in the heart of the Pocono mountains, has been serving Scouts for over 100 years. The regional Scout summer camp encompasses more than 1,200 acres of beautiful and pristine Pennsylvanian woodlands along the shores of the 314-acre Stillwater Lake.
In the summer of 2026 Scouts from more than 100 different packs, troops and crews visited Camp Minsi (with representation from over 27 different BSA councils, 9 US states, and 4 countries) and enjoyed a week full of swimming, sailing, horseback riding, whitewater rafting, shooting, singing, hiking, mucking, canoeing, crafting, laughing, and so much more!
Camp Minsi provides unique and exciting programs for Scouts of all ages from throughout the United States. Summer camp is the pinnacle of Scouting’s outdoor program. Each summer is filled with new programs and activities designed to peak the interests of every Scout – including a top-notch first-year camper program to help Scouts on the trail to First Class and exciting high adventure opportunities (such as horseback riding, whitewater rafting and the unique Minsi Muck Hike) for the older Scouts.
We are extremely excited for the 2027 summer camp season at Camp Minsi. We have a great staff lined up of experienced and enthusiastic individuals who are dedicated to making sure every Scout’s stay at camp the absolute best. This summer we're planning to introduce a variety of great new programs and experiences while continuing to build on our lasting traditions. This website is your first resource to answering your summer camp questions. If you have any further questions, please feel free to contact us (campminsi@minsitrails.org).

In partnership with Minsi Trails Council Da Vinci Center is presenting the following exciting merit badge opportunities!
October 17, 2026: Digital Technology Merit Badge
Learn about digital technology—past, present and future! We’ll look at intellectual property, the 1’s and 0’s of how digital technology works, and use coding to create programs that are useful...and fun!
Scouts will complete Requirements 3, 4 , 5, 6(a) (c) and (f), 7, 8 (a) and (c), and 9 (a).

November 14, 2026: Artificial Intelligence Merit Badge
Artificial Intelligence is everywhere these days...but without understanding what it can and can’t do, we use it at our peril. We’ll give you the tools to understand and use AI smartly. We’ll examine automation, ethics, deepfakes, and how to harness AI for good.
Scouts will complete Requirements 1-6.
Bring a letter from Scoutmaster showing completion of requirements 7 and 8
December 5, 2026: Oceanography Merit Badge
From waves to wildlife, the ocean is full of wonders (and mysteries)! We will be learning about the geology of the seafloor, how landforms affect wave patterns, and about careers in oceanography and underwater exploration.
Scouts will complete all requirements to earn this badge during the session.
Scouts will also get time in the oceanography-focused Finding Titanic special exhibition!
February 20, 2027: Composite Materials Merit Badge
Composite materials are a key ingredient in making many of the things we use regularly stronger and more effective. We’ll look at the properties of these materials; how to use them safely; careers in composites and materials science, and even make a couple of composite products to take home.
Scouts will complete Requirements 1(b), 2(b), 3(b), 4(a) or (b ), 5, and 6(a).

/502-MTCWB2027.desc:
DO YOU WANT A MOUNTAIN TOP LEADERSHIP TRAINING EXPERIENCE?
REGISTER FOR THE 2027 WOOD BADGE COURSE TODAY!
In 1911, Baden-Powell took the first steps in training Scouting’s adult leaders by organizing a series of lectures for Scouters.  He made great strides in the years that followed, culminating in 1919 with the establishment of Wood Badge training.  Wood Badge recipients number more than 100,000 and can be found in all corners of the world.
A Scouter participating in Wood Badge has the opportunity to:
Understand Scouting as a family of interrelated, values-based programs providing age-appropriate activities for youth.
Recognize contemporary leadership concepts and discover how they are relevant to the Scouting movement.
Apply the skills learned as a member of a successful working team.
Revitalize their commitment to Scouting by sharing in an inspirational experience that provides Scouting with renewed leadership.
Many Scouters consider Wood Badge to be a peak experience of their Scouting careers.  It has served as a source of training and inspiration to thousands.
The Wood Badge Experience:
There are two parts to Wood Badge in the Boy Scouts of America, the practical part and the application period.  Both must be completed to receive the Wood Badge – two wooden beads to be worn around the neck on a leather thong.
The practical part is a two-weekend experience to demonstrate as practically as possible the aims and methods of Scouting.  The course is a multifaceted presentation of leadership skills, organizational tools, and participatory activities based on the best Scouting traditions and the latest in team development theory. In addition, participants will enjoy the fellowship of learning along side many other Scouters, and along the way will have a great deal of fun!
The application part of Wood Badge is a period of up to 18-month during which the participants practice and demonstrate a working knowledge of the leadership principles presented during the course.  This is accomplished by the use of the Wood Badge “ticket”, which represents the participant’s commitment to complete a set of personal goals related to their Scouting position.  These goals will significantly strengthen the program in which the participant is involved.
Throughout the period of application, each participant is assigned a counselor who serves as a resource, an evaluator and a Scouting friend.  When the counselor and the participant determine that the new skills are understood and can be applied to their Scouting position, a recommendation is made for the Wood Badge to be awarded.
When does Wood Badge happen?
The course is a 5 day course held over two weekends.
Weekend #1 will be Friday morning, September 17, 2027 to late Sunday afternoon, September 19, 2027.
Weekend #2 will be Saturday morning, October 16, 2027 to Sunday afternoon, October 17, 2027.
Patrols are also required to meet at least once in the interval between the two weekend sessions.
Attendance is required at both FULL weekends to receive credit for the course.
Who may attend Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is for all leaders in the Boy Scouts of America.  It has been developed for Cub Scout, Boy Scout, Varsity Scout and Venturing leaders, as well as council and district leaders.
The course content and leadership principles introduced apply to Scouters of all leadership positions and will provide a common foundation of leadership skills to be used throughout all program areas.
Qualifications:
Each Scouter invited to participate in Wood Badge training must be a registered member of the Boy Scouts of America, at least 18 years of age, have completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position and must successfully complete an Annual Health and Medical Record form, Parts A, B, and C.
Course Limit:
48 participants.  There will be a waitlist for those registering after the course maximum has been reached.  If openings become avaialble waitlisted individuals will fill in order of registratio

The College of Commissioner Science (CCS) provides Commissioners with opportunities to strengthen their skills, expand their knowledge, and become better equipped to serve Scouting units.
Through structured coursework, practical resources, and the sharing of best practices, participants gain tools they can put to use in supporting packs, troops, crews, ships, and posts. The College also provides an opportunity to connect with Commissioners from across the region and learn from one another's experiences.
Who Should Attend?
All Commissioners who have completed

are encouraged to attend. Whether you are a new Commissioner or have years of experience, the College offers opportunities to develop new skills, explore current practices in unit service, and connect with fellow Scouters.
Other Scouting volunteers interested in learning more about Commissioner service are also welcome to attend.

NOAC 2027 – National Order of the Arrow Conference
What: The National Order of the Arrow Conference (NOAC) is the flagship national Order of the Arrow event. It is held every 2-3 years at a major university campus and is attended by as many as 8,000 Arrowmen from all 50 states. It is second only to the National Scout Jamboree in size and scope. Our largest conference was in 2015, attended by more than 15,000 Arrowmen to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Order of the Arrow.
When: July 24th - July 31st, 2027
Where: University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign (Champaign, Illinois)
Estimated Cost: The estimated cost for this event is $1,300. There is a very likely chance that this cost is lowered due to fundraising efforts. We will determine a final cost and payment schedule after our contingent has been registered.
What do you get?: This includes the NOAC fee, transportation costs, a contingent t-shirt, exclusive Wagion NOAC patch sets, lodging during travel, meals before NOAC, and any other associated costs with side trips (ex. amusement park ticket, etc.)!
Registration Deadline: Initial deposits of $200 are due by November 7th, 2026. The next payment will be due by December 26th, 2026.
Cancellation Policy: Once the lodge has registered a member for NOAC, the spot is locked and nonrefundable. Therefore, in the case of a cancellation, we cannot guarantee the cancelee will receive a full refund. The only way a full refund is possible will be if the cancelee can find someone to take their spot and the new contingent member pays the cost in full.
If this cannot happen, the cancelee will not receive a full refund. They may receive a partial refund of, up to or equal to, the costs charged by the lodge. These costs are associated with transportation, lodging, apparel, etc. The amount of this refund cannot be determined until the final cost is established, and it will greatly depend on the date of the cancellation. No refunds will be possible after June 1st, 2027.

This couse will be run from 12pm - 4pm
Scouting requires all Range and Target Activities (including Cub Scout archery, BB guns, wrist rockets/slingshots, catapults or rockets) to be supervised by a certified range master. At the Cub Scout level, BB and archery
is
only allowed at district and council-operated events, and may NOT be conducted at the pack or den level.
This training does NOT certify someone to open an Archery range at the unit-level for Troops, Crews, or Ships.
This
training covers
setting up a range, safety, handling equipment, using a bow stringer, maintaining and storing equipment, and instructing Scouts. This certification is valid for two years from the course completion date.
Any questions for the Archery Rangemaster please email
JoAnne Strom

training covers
setting up a range, safety, handling equipment, using a bow stringer, maintaining and storing equipment, and instructing Scouts. This certification is valid for two years from the course completion date.
Any questions for the BB Rangemaster please email
Kevin Rossi

/525-2027MADC.desc:
Get ready for an unforgettable summer of adventure, discovery, and hands-on fun at Musser Scout Reservation!
Musser Adventure Day Camps are open to all youth entering 1st through 8th grade in Fall 2027—you do not need to be a registered Scout to attend! Whether your child is already part of Scouting or is looking for an exciting new summer experience, our Adventure Day Camps offer something for everyone.
2027 Camp Dates
Cub Adventure Day Camp – Week 1
July 12–16, 2027
Cub Adventure Day Camp – Week 2
July 19–23, 2027
STEM Adventure Day Camp
July 26–30, 2027
Each week combines outdoor adventure, hands-on activities, STEM experiences, and plenty of opportunities for campers to learn new skills, make friends, and have fun in the outdoors.
Camp Highlights Include:
Archery
BBs
Slingshots
Fishing
Hands-on STEM activities
Outdoor skills and exploration
Games and team-building activities
Camp-style activities and adventures
And much more!
Cub Adventure Day Camp brings the excitement of outdoor adventure to campers with engaging activities, games, and opportunities to build skills and confidence while focusing on earning several Cub Scout Adventures for each rank.
STEM Adventure Day Camp combines outdoor recreation with hands-on science, technology, engineering, and math activities, giving campers the chance to explore STEM concepts while having fun outside.
Your Registration Includes:
Daily lunch
Camper T-shirt
Camp patch
Camp sticker
A full week of fun, adventure, and memories!
Whether your child is an experienced Scout or has never participated in Scouting before, Musser Adventure Day Camps are a place to explore, learn, challenge yourself, and have fun!
Join us at Musser Scout Reservation for Summer 2027!
Have any additional questions? Sent them to
daycampdirector@mussersr.org
More information
is available at:
www.scoutingphilly.org/cubdaycamp
Multiple-Week Discount
- When you register for a second week of 2027 Cub Adventure Day Camp or 2027 STEM Adventure Day Camp, the $15 credit to your second week of camp will be automatically applied!  If you don't see the discount applied, please email camping@scoutingphilly.org.
Financial Aid
- Thanks to the generosity of other camp families and donors, we have money set-aside each year for financial aid that we call “Camperships”. Camperships are need-based, and are awarded for up-to 50% of the camp fee. The campership form will be live in January for families to complete. Campership requests are due April 1, and determinations will be made in late April.

National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what they must KNOW, and what they must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
The NYLT course is limited to a total of 112 participants. Because we always have more applicants than we can take, we will only be able to accept the first 112 applicants who are fully paid for the course. After that, fully paid applicants will be placed on a wait-list in the order that their full payment is received. Although we almost always have a few openings come up for various reasons, we cannot predict how many people from the waitlist will be provided the opportunity to attend the course.
Be sure to download the required forms BSA Annual Health and Medical Record and Supplemental Medical Form and bring with you to the course.
All participants must be experienced Scout campers. They must already know how to set up camp, prepare meals, maintain personal and campsite cleanliness, and generally work in a patrol camping situation It is important that the attendees do not attend prematurely either by age or rank.  Youth registered in Scouts, BSA must be 13 years of age; there can be no exceptions .  Scouts, BSA members must also be First Class Rank.  Venturers do not need to achieve the First Class rank, but must attend Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews (ILSC) prior to participating in NYLT.
It is not appropriate to send a Scout who has never camped without a parent to National Youth Leadership Training Conference.

/528-NRARSO.desc:
The NRA Range Safety Officer program provides nationally recognized certification for individuals responsible for supervising safe shooting activities and range operations.
The Range and Target requirement to run a rifle range on scouting property is 1 NRA RSO and 1 NRA Rifle Instructor.

This course is intentionally offered under market rate with the understanding that attendees will sign an agreement to assist with a set number of Hawk Mountain Council Range & Target Activities during the certification period.
After this course, you will be able to:
Supervise Live Fire:
Provide direct safety supervision for live-fire range events involving Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouts.
Enforce Safety Rules:
Manage range commands, monitor shooter behavior, and ensure adherence to range Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Inspect Ranges:
Conduct pre-activity range inspections and verify proper equipment and environmental setups.
Handle Emergencies:
Manage range emergencies, medical protocols, and firearm stoppages or malfunctions.

2027 Mountain Rescue Klondike Derby
Seven Bridges District | Susquehanna Council | Scouting America
A winter storm has stranded hikers in the mountains, and we need your help! Each patrol will become a mountain rescue team, taking on missions to rescue stranded hikers, clear trails, provide first aid, and safely evacuate victims.
Patrols will earn rescue points at each completed station. Awards will recognize the patrols that demonstrate the best combination of Scout skills, teamwork, leadership, and Scout spirit!
Date: Saturday, January 23, 2027
Location: Buffalo Valley Sportsmen's Association, near Mifflinburg, PA
Patrol and Sled Information
Sleds may include Arrow of Light Scouts from associated Cub Scout packs. Each sled must have a minimum of 6 Scouts and a maximum of 10 Scouts.
Lone Scouts and Scouts whose troops are not entering a sled are welcome! Please register and contact one of the event organizers if you would like to be paired with a troop that has room on its sled.
Lunch Included
Each registration includes lunch consisting of:
Two sandwiches: hamburger barbecue, hot dog, or grilled cheese
Baked beans
Chips
A drink
Choose two of the same sandwich or mix and match!
Friday Night Camping and Activities
Free camping will be available on Friday, January 22, for those who wish to arrive early.
Join us Friday night for an indoor movie with free popcorn!
Optional Breakfast: Scouts may add a hearty breakfast sandwich and hot beverage to their online registration for an additional $4. Breakfast must be ordered during registration. No walk-up breakfasts will be available.
Registration Fees
Scouts
- Through December 26: $18 per Scout
- December 27–January 10: $23 per Scout
Arrow of Light Scouts
- $15 per Scout, including lunch
Adult Leaders
- Through December 28: $10 per adult
- December 29–January 10: $15 per adult
Event Staff
- $10 per staff member
- Includes breakfast, lunch, and the event patch
- No late fee applies to staff registration
Registration Deadline
All registration closes Sunday, January 10, 2027.
Don't wait until the last minute! Get your patrol together, prepare your rescue sled, and get ready to test your winter survival and rescue skills.
Will your patrol rise to the challenge and become the ultimate Mountain Rescue Team?
Be prepared. Work together. Rescue lives!

Explore the science hiding behind the clouds while earning the Weather Merit Badge! Join us from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM at PARC for a full day of hands-on learning and advancement.
Scouts will discover how weather forms, learn about clouds, storms, and forecasting, and explore the impact weather has on our daily lives. Through interactive activities, observations, and discussions, participants will gain a better understanding of meteorology and the science that helps predict changing conditions.
Scouts will practice reading weather maps, interpreting forecasts, and learning how weather information is collected and shared. They will also examine weather safety and preparedness, helping them understand how to respond to severe weather events.

Make one of the following instruments: wind vane, anemometer, rain gauge, or hygrometer. Keep a daily weather log for one week using information from this instrument as well as from other sources such as local radio and television stations, NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards, and internet sources (with your parent or guardian's permission). Record the following information at the same time every day: wind direction and speed, temperature, precipitation, and types of clouds. Be sure to make a note of any morning dew or frost. In the log, also list the weather forecasts from radio or television at the same time each day and show how the weather really turned out.

Thursday Oct 29 (7 PM to 10 PM)

137 Modena Road
South Coatesville, PA
Next to the Citadel Credit Union - across the street from the South Coatesville Borough Building
Wilderness First Aid (WFA) is a hands-on training course designed to prepare participants to prevent, assess, and respond to medical emergencies that may occur in remote or back country environments. This course teaches essential skills for managing injuries and illnesses in settings where professional medical care may be hours away.
This course meets or exceeds the BSA Wilderness First Aid Curriculum and Doctrine Guidelines, 2017 Edition.
Participants will learn to:
Recognize and manage life-threatening emergencies using the Patient Assessment System
Treat common wilderness injuries, including bleeding, fractures, sprains, burns, wounds, and environmental illnesses.
Manage heat and cold emergencies, dehydration, altitude issues, and allergic reactions
Handle medical problems such as abdominal pain, infections, and respiratory issues
Make informed decisions about evacuation and extended care
Improvise first-aid solutions with limited supplies
Work effectively as a team in stressful and/or remote situations
Course Format
16–20 hours of classroom learning, practical skills sessions, and outdoor scenarios
Outdoor practical simulations build confidence in assessing and treating patients in the field and are an important part of the course.  They will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.
Upon successful completion of the course participants will receive both a CPR/AED and Wilderness First Aid Card good for 2 years.

How to Prepare for Merit Badge College:
Step 1: Choose Your Workshop(s) – EXPLORE
Talk with your parents or guardians about your options, but ultimately, choose a workshop that genuinely interests you. Don’t just pick a badge because it’s required for Eagle—this is your chance to step outside your comfort zone and discover something new. Merit Badge College is about learning, growing, and exploring topics that excite you.
Step 2: Consider Your Age
While there are no official age or grade requirements for any merit badge, some workshops at Merit Badge College are recommended for Scouts in 9th grade and above. These sessions often cover a large amount of material in a short time, which can be challenging for younger Scouts to keep up with. This may slow the pace of the class and prevent completion of the intended content.
We want every Scout to have a positive and successful experience, so please choose workshops that are age-appropriate and match your readiness level. Be sure to consult your Scoutmaster and get their approval
Step 3: Get Ready for Merit Badge College – LEARN
You’ve selected your workshops and registered—great job! Now it’s time to prepare so you can get the most out of your experience.
Did you know? Merit Badge pamphlets are available for free online! You can find them by visiting https://www.scouting.org/skills/merit-badges/all/ and clicking on the badge you’re working on.
Read the pamphlet thoroughly—yes, really read it! The more familiar you are with the material, the more confident and successful you’ll be in your workshop. You might even want to read it more than once.
Keep in mind:
Completion of a badge is not guaranteed.
Many workshops list prerequisites in the course catalog. These must be completed before MBC Day.
Bring all supporting materials to class—notes, pictures, reports, letters, or other evidence of completed work.
Some requirements may not be doable in a classroom setting. Even if not listed as prerequisites, you should attempt them ahead of time.
Ultimately, it’s up to you to ensure every requirement is completed. The better prepared you are, the more you’ll learn—and the more you’ll enjoy the day.
(And yes… read the book!)
Step 4: Day of Expectations
To ensure a safe, respectful, and productive experience for everyone, all Scouts attending Merit Badge College are expected to follow the guidelines below:

Scouts should demonstrate the values of the Scout Oath and Law throughout the day. These principles guide behavior

Certification Course
February 19-21, 2027
At Camp Coker
This is a 16-hour, skills-based course designed to prepare participants to evaluate, provide first-aid treatment and when necessary, safely transport injured or sick individuals who may be encountered in a remote or wilderness environment.  Weather permitting, the entire course will be held outside and will employ a variety of teaching scenarios as described in the schedule listed below.  All scenarios will follow the principles of Leave No Trace and are based upon the instructors’ experiences at Philmont Scout Ranch and other wilderness medical environments including military deployments, wilderness search and rescue, Wildland Fireline, and National Park Backcountry EMS.  Upon successful completion of this course the participants will receive a 2-year Wilderness and Remote First-Aid Certification by the American Red Cross.  This certification is endorsed by the Boy Scouts of America.

What is Winter Camp:
The Winter Camp is held December 18-21 at Camp Barstow. This Winter Camp is held at the beginning of winter break just before Christmas.  A volunteer camp staff provides program help, guidance, and supervision in the area of Scout-craft, Nature, Arts, and Citizenship as well as many other specialty merit badges.   These may include merit badges that are required for the Eagle Scout rank.
Scouts sign-up for Merit Badges by each day.  One for Saturday, one for Sunday, and one for Monday.  They will stay in that class
for the day to complete work in that Merit Badge.  There are some Merit Badges that have been "bundled" with another like badge.  Scouts will woork on those badges for the entire day.   Make sure to choose a
badge
per day (Saturday-Sunday-Monday) unless the
badge
states that it takes multiple days such as Cooking.  Some merit badges will have prerequisites to be completed before attending.  Each class has a maximum number of Scouts that can attend each day and may not be able to "squeeze" more in.

Provide advancement opportunities for Scouts
Familiarize youth with the Scouting program through the outdoor experience
Stimulate Troop programming before, during, and after attending camp
Enjoy the start of the Holidays with other Scouts
Make friends and have FUN
Share ideas and enjoy fellowship

Any registered Scouts BSA youth may attend.  Adults must attend with Scouts, be registered and have current Safeguarding Youth Training.

Scouts can not attend on on their own.

/553-woodbadge27.desc:
2027 Wood Badge Course 15-553-27
WOOD BADGE – ULTIMATE TRAINING PROGRAM
The 2027 Indian Waters Council Wood Badge Course will be held over 2 weekends (March 12-14, 2027 & April 17-18, 2027) at Camp Barstow.
You must attend both weekends.
Wood Badge is the ultimate leadership training program for the adult leaders of Scouting America. Wood Badge is a modern format of training that delivers the latest in 12 leadership skills that will help you be the best leader possible. These are skills that will become part of your everyday life.  We promise you friendship, camaraderie, knowledge, personal awareness, and most of all fun!
The fee for the course is as follows:
$275 for participants
Covers program and training materials, all your food for weekend one, and weekend two both lunches, course T-shirt, and Wood Badge presentation kit (upon completion of the training program).  Participants will be providing their own dinner and breakfast on weekend two. Details regarding weekend two meals will be provided during weekend one.
Wood Badge has been developed for ALL Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, and Venturing leaders, as well as council and district leaders. The course content and the principles introduced apply to scouters in all leadership positions in all of the program areas. It provides a common foundation of leadership and team skills used throughout the program. Who should attend?  YOU should attend!
To attend Wood Badge, you must:
Be a registered member of Scouting America
Have completed Safeguarding Youth Training
Have completed the basic training course for your Scouting position
Have completed the outdoor skills program for your Scouting position, if applicable
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment
