/598-WFA.desc:
About Wilderness First Aid
This course is required for Philmont and other high-adventure bases by the BSA. It is highly recommended for units involved in activities where you are further than 1 hour from EMS.
Prerequisites
Current certification in adult CPR/AED is required to take the Wilderness First Aid training course. You must provide a copy of your certification at the start of the WFA course.
CPR/AED Training
For those without a current CPR/AED certification, a separate CPR/AED course is offered on Friday night starting at 6:00 PM and will run until the training is complete.
Note
The fee includes course materials, meals, and camping accommodations. Please pack as if you were hiking in the backcountry! The class has limited slots and will be filled on a first-paid/first-in basis. After receiving your registration and payment you will be registered for the course. The class will be canceled if the minimum of 6 participants is not met. In case of cancellation, your fee will be refunded. Other than “Event Cancellation” there is a No Refund Policy for this event.
Medical
A current BSA Annual Health & Medical form is required to be submitted on arrival. Only Part A and Part B are required for this event.
Participants interested in signing up for both WFA and the First Aid/CPR/AED, sign up for WFA first and then under classes select the First Aid/CPR/AED.

Camp Rock Enon has 14 campsites within a short walking distance to all program areas and services with a maximum capacity of 325 Scouts and Scouters per week/session.  Each site is equipped with two-person tents on raised platforms. Some sites also have Adirondack (three sided) shelters that sleep up to 4 people or cabins that sleep up to 20 people. All campsites include sleeping cots, a shelter, picnic tables, latrine with wash station and potable water, flag pole, bulletin board and campfire circle. Within main camp you will find flush toilets and a shower house with hot water available all day and night. Program areas include Aquatics, Outdoor Skills, Nature, Handicraft, Climbing and Range & Target Sports. The dining hall provides meal service for all campers serving a variety of kid and adult friendly meals reviewed and approved by a certified nutritionist. Special dietary menus are available for a variety needs including gluten free, pork free and vegetarian.
Tiger, Wolf & Bear
Scouts can work on a few rank specific “Adventures” plus go swimming, shoot bb’s arrows and sling shots, climb our rock wall, visit the nature conservation area, go fishing, learn basic outdoor and first aid skills, make a craft or play some Cub Scout games.
Webelos and Arrow of Light
Scouts will choose which “Adventures” they want to work on to help develop the skills needed as they advance towards Scouts BSA. They can also go swimming, shoot pellets, arrows and sling shots, climb our rock wall, visit the nature conservation area, go fishing, learn outdoor and first aid Scout skills, make a craft or play some Scout games. Mid-week all Webelos and Arrow of Light Scouts will spend the day exploring the back woods of Camp Rock Enon, learning and testing new outdoor skills as part of the mid-week program and optional outpost camp sleeping under the stars.

Wood Badge is an advanced, national leadership course open only to Scouting volunteers and professionals. Scouters from Cub Scouting, Boy Scouting, Varsity Scouting, Venturing, Sea Scouts, and Explorers, and district and council Scouters all are welcome and belong here.
Wood Badge training was begun by Baden Powell in 1919 as a way to ensure that the leaders of Scout Troops were properly trained. Since then, Wood Badge training has been held worldwide providing advanced leader training to thousands of Scout Leaders.
Wood Badge is considered the premier leadership training course for Scout Leaders. Wood Badge for the 21st Century is available to registered leaders of all levels of the Scouting program – Cub Scouts, Boy Scouts, Varsity, and Venturing. It concentrates on providing training on modern leadership skills needed in today’s world for Scout leaders. Wood Badge Training will not only make you a better Scout Leader, but it will also assist you in improving your personal and professional life as well.
Through Wood Badge you will gain valuable tools in listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning, and leading change. You will learn to better understand and leverage diversity and the generational differences of society. You will learn to lead with a vision. You will learn the skills that will make you a better Scout Leader to benefit the youth we serve.
Every Scout deserves a well-trained leader. Are you that leader? Get Wood Badge trained and you will be. In doing so, you will change not only your life but also the lives of all that you touch.
Tickets
Have you heard of “The Ticket” and wondered what it is? The "ticket" is a group of five goals you set for yourself to do after the course, to improve your unit. You learn more about this in the course.
Purpose of Wood Badge
The purpose of Wood Badge is to develop skilled leaders who can strengthen Scouting units in achieving the mission of the Boy Scouts of America.
When we accomplish the mission of Scouting, we do it in the units. Therefore, the short form of the purpose is, that the purpose of Wood Badge is to strengthen units.

If you have just completed a tour as a Cubmaster, Scoutmaster, or any other adult Scouter position and want to continue to service Scouting in a different capacity, consider becoming a Unit Commissioner. Provisional Scouts Welcomed
Camp T. Brady Saunders provides a great outdoor experience with modern facilities and excellent program opportunities for Scouts of all ages! Come and see what fun and excitement Summer 2027 brings to Camp T. Brady Saunders.  You might even get the chance to run into our resident Bigfoot, or perhaps help us figure out what is lurking in Lake Dillon...
The Heart of Virginia Scout Reservation is located in Goochland County, Virginia.  It consists of 604 acres of land and comprises three separate camps. Camp T. Brady Saunders has 16 separate campsites, four shower houses with individual rooms, a large dining hall equipped with air-conditioning, a trading post, a health lodge, an aquatics program on Lake Dillon, C.O.P.E (Challenging Outdoor Personal Experience) Course, remote controlled multi-station shotgun range, covered archery and rifle range, STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) program, a 3D archery range, 10 miles of a mountain bike and hiking trails, a compass and geocaching course, a sandpit volleyball court, a Gaga Pit, a traverse wall, a nine-hole disk golf course, a 28-foot tall Wet Willy waterslide, Canoes, Kayaks, Paddleboards, Paddle boats, Sailboats, an administration building and dining hall equipped with high-speed wireless internet, Scoutmaster Lodge with Internet and a basketball court.
Summer Camp at T Brady Saunders has over 60 merit badges to select from, so there is something for everyone. There is also our Trailblazer course for first year Scouts. Trailblazers will work on requirements for Tenderfoot, Second Class and First Class ranks in the morning and in the afternoon will work on earning the Swimming merit badge or instructional swim and one of the handicraft merit badges (American Indian Culture, Space Exploration, Basketry, or Leatherwork). On Thursday night, there will be a special Trailblazer only evening event. For those who may be more adventurous, we have our Project COPE program or Ranger Challenge. In Project COPE, participants get to test their agility and skills while climbing, swinging and rappelling as well as work on building confidence, developing leadership, and inspiring cooperation a part of a team. Our Ranger Challenge is a program designed for older Scouts who seek a different Summer Camp experience. During the week, Ranger Challenge Scouts will participate in a variety of activities both on and off site that will challenge them both mentally and physically. They will have the opportunity to face our climbing tower or go white water rafting just to name a few possibilities.
We look forward to you joining us for a great summer adventure at T. Brady Saunders.

Winter Skills Adventure Program
Come spend an exciting and memorable weekend in the snow with us! Learn how to build a snow structure & stay warm.  Learn to identify dangerous avalanche conditions and how to avoid them. Learn basic winter survival skills and first aid. The seminar addresses all aspects of winter camping and outdoor travel in a condensed classroom session that assumes basic backpacking knowledge and builds on that for a fun and safe experience in the winter.

The class welcomes and encourages older Scouts to assist as junior leaders.

/609-115866.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth with leadership skills and experience that they can apply within their troops and in other situations requiring leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a six-day course that emphasizes hands-on learning in a fun, engaging environment. Through a blend of activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and games, participants will develop confidence and leadership abilities while working together as a team.
The course content is designed to build leadership concepts progressively, using practical exercises to reinforce learning. Participants embark on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership, which brings the leadership lessons to life as they apply their skills throughout the course.
In order to attend an NYLT course, youth must meet the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Annual Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members must be at least 13 years old by the first day of the course and no older than 17 years old. They must also have completed the Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops and achieved the rank of First Class.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14 years old (or 13 and completed eighth grade) and can be no older than 20 years old. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships and have some basic camping experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.

/609-DayCamp2027.desc:
Join Cub Day Camp as we venture into the Cretaceous!
Campers will learn new skills, make friends, and have more fun than they can imagine as they adventure in a host of fun-themed activities, games, and play. Activity stations include
games, cooking, crafts, STEM, BB Skills, Archery, Slingshots, Woodworking
, and many more group activities!
Who Can Attend Camp?
All youth must be entering 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, or 5th grade in September 2026. Youth entering Kindergarten in September 2026 do not meet the age requirements for Day Camp.
If your child is entering 1st Grade in September 2026, we require that a parent/guardian accompany them for the entirety of Day Camp. This adult must also register.
Day Camp is also open to non-Scouting families
Volunteers
A $50 discount is available to families who can provide an adult volunteer for at least 2 days of camp. Adults are welcome to volunteer for as many days as they would like. We would love to have you! Any adult volunteering must also register. Registration for adults is free.
We welcome youth volunteers over the age of 14! Come join us for a fun week of camp, earn service hours, and spend time with friends! Youth volunteers must also register. Registration for youth volunteers is free.

/609-LeaderTrainingWeekends2027.desc:
BALOO and IOLS
Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO) & Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills (IOLS) are required training for camping.These courses will help you provide the best experience possible for youth in your unit. Open to all registered parents and unit supporters. Find brief descriptions for each below.
Welcome to BALOO training! It is the Cub Scout leader training required for any Cub Scout den or pack outdoor event, including pack camping overnighters and Webelos den overnighters. BALOO training comprises two components—an online component and a practical, hands-on component. Both components must be completed to qualify as a “TRAINED” Cub Scout outdoor leader. The online component must be completed prior to the practical component. The online training contains introductory and basic information that will be built upon during the practical training.
Welcome to Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills training! The Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS) course builds and expands on the concepts and themes introduced in Scoutmaster Position-Specific Training and provides Scouters with the confidence to take youth into the outdoors. Specifically, this hands-on program gives adult leaders a practical introduction to the patrol method of a Scout-led troop by teaching many of the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the outdoors. In addition, the teaching methods, activities, and games model the variety of teaching used in effective and engaging Scouting programs.
IOLS is required to be position trained as a Scoutmaster or Assisstant Scoutmaster.
THANKS TO YOU, MILLIONS OF SCOUTS … … Develop self-reliance … Learn to work well with others … Are better citizens … Learn life skills … and have fun!! You have our unending thanks for helping make this a reality!
These trainings are also known by the following codes:
S11 Intro to Outdoor Leadership Skills (IOLS)
C32 Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO)

/609-PeninsulaMBC.desc:
Peninsula Territory Merit Badge Clinic Registration
Welcome to the Peninsula Territory Merit Badge Clinic!
Registration Deadline:
January 4th, or sooner if all classes are filled.
Clinic Dates:
January 9
January 23
February 6
Each merit badge class spans three sessions on the dates above. Attendance at all three sessions is required.
Important Details
Counselor Communication:
Counselors will contact registered Scouts up to two weeks before the first session to discuss preparation and initial requirements. After the final session, they will continue to assist as needed until March 1, the closing date for completing merit badges.
Completion Timeline:
Most Scouts should be able to finish their merit badge(s) during the clinic, but completion is not guaranteed. Scouts are responsible for meeting all requirements.
Guidance for Scouts
Pick a Merit Badge:
Choose from the Course Catalog and discuss your selection with your Scoutmaster and parents. Select a topic you truly want to learn—not just for rank advancement.
Consider Your Age:
While there are no age restrictions, some classes are better suited for older Scouts due to the amount of material covered.
Get Ready:
Obtain and read the Merit Badge pamphlet before the first session. Bring all required materials (notes, pictures, reports, etc.) to class.
Tracking Requirements:
Requirements will be tracked digitally, and records will be sent after the third weekend.
Day of the Event:
Wear your Field Uniform proudly and bring your Merit Badge pamphlet.

/609-STCA.desc:
Short Term Camp Administrator Training
A short-term camp is any council-organized overnight camping program, whether one-time or continuing, that is one, two or three nights in length where the council or its agents provide the staffing and may provide program and food services, and includes camps conducted off council properties. National training courses are subject to the short-term camp requirements, regardless of format or duration. (See NCAP standard SA-001).
Each short-term camp is administered by a short-term camp administrator. This National Camping School course will be conducted at the council level. Short-Term Camp Administrator National Camping School course consist of several modules designed to prepare the participant to manage the short-term camp from planning and program development to staff recruitment to assessment.
The Short-term camp administrator certification will be valid for 2 years from the course date. Your certification card will be mailed to you.
If you are an event chair, the cost of this training will be charged to your event. Please use the code sent to you via email to reassign the charge to your event. If you are an event chair and did not receive a coupon via email, please reach out to gillian.suhre@scouting.org.
Please plan for the course to last until 5pm, though we may end earlier. Lunch is provided;
be sure to include dietary restrictions and allergies if applicable.

/609-WoodBadge2027.desc:
Wood Badge 2027: Lead from the Inside Out
Ready to lead the way?
Wood Badge 2027 is here to equip you with the skills and confidence to inspire change and build a brighter future for your Scouting unit and beyond! This isn't just another training — it's an adventure in leadership that will empower you to make a lasting impact wherever you go.
What's Wood Badge All About?
Wood Badge is a dynamic and immersive course designed to make you a better leader in every area of life—at work, home, parenting, and, of course, in Scouting. Imagine five days filled with purpose-driven games, engaging presentations, and powerful small-group activities, all focused on giving you the tools to lead with vision and purpose.
Who Can Join?
Wood Badge is open to all adults in Scouting—whether you're with Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts, or involved at the district or council level. If you're 18 or older and registered with Scouting America, you're eligible!
What to Expect:
The course is over two weekends, covering five days, opening your eyes to a whole new level of Scouting. You'll understand why every moment counts, from the team challenges to the camaraderie around the campfire, as you learn to inspire change and build the future.

/611-CampGrizzly2027.desc:
CAMP GRIZZLY
Since 1938, Camp Grizzly has been the home to amazing summer adventures for many Scouts and Leaders and has helped to shape thousands of Scouts into amazing young people!  Nestled on the edge of the Hoodoo Mountains, Camp Grizzly is home to a fantastic shooting sports program, including six different ranges.  In the Eagle's Nest, new scouts will spend two full days learning Scout through First Class skills and the ins and outs of the scouting program.  Your scouts will return to their troop each evening thoroughly fired up about scouting and their achievements!  Our Tradescraft program features metalworking and welding merit badges, allowing your older scouts to explore potential lucrative careers.   Camp Grizzly has a proud tradition of unit service and great programs.  Your unit will have an exciting week that balances opportunities to earn merit badges and to work together as a troop and in patrols with service project opportunities, and our mid-week patrol games and competitions.
LOCATION
Nestled at the edge of the Hoodoo Mountain range in Idaho, Camp Grizzly is located along the Palouse River, 12 miles East of Potlatch, ID.  We enjoy warm and dry days during the summer season and cool nights.  Daytime temperatures in late July average around 82°F, and nights average at 54°F, with temperatures dropping swiftly once the sun sets.  Our small lake is perfectly sized for younger scouts to complete their boating merit badges and the water is pleasantly cool and refreshing!  Every program area and campsite has shade shelters and trails between areas wind through our regrowing forest.  Each campsite has canvas tents on platforms and an adirondak that sleeps 8 as well as a campfire ring, picnic tables and kybos.  Program areas are spread across less than a half mile with the majority within just 1/4 mile, allowing Scoutmasters ample opportunity to visit and observe all of their scouts in their classes during the week.  Several program areas are observable from the deck of our lodge where Scoutmasters can enjoy a quiet cup of coffee, observe the early morning polar plunge and watch the sun rise over the lake or enjoy their scouts' glee while they capsize boats for their merit badge classes!

The 2025 Leader's Guide is currently available in the attachments section.  The Program Guide will contain an updated class list and schedule and is due to be available in April for merit badge registration.  The final list of merit badges and schedule of classes is currently in development and we plan to have class registration open in April.  To register for classes, you must be fully paid up per the payment schedule.  A Leader Meeting will be scheduled in May and recorded for later viewing.  Don't hesitate to get in touch with Margaret Parsley, our Program Executive and Camp Director, with any questions we haven't answered with our currently available guide.

Merit Badge University at Eastern Washington University Computing and Engineering Building (Cheney Campus)
*****
All Classes will take both weeks to achieve, they will be the same period, both weeks****(2 sessions - both days TBD)
Class Fee -$10
LUNCH- Pizza is being provided by EWU College of STEM for scouts and their parents.
Mobile Trading Post option- We offer an array of items from the Scout Shop. Be sure to bring extra money to get things you may need!
You can also contact Marcia Hunt before the event to be certain that items will be at the Trading Post.
GUIDANCE FOR SCOUTS ATTENDING A MERIT BADGE COLLEGE
1.) Pick a Merit Badge
From the Course Catalog, you can select several Merit Badges that you have an interest in taking. We expect you to discuss with your Scoutmaster and parents which badge to earn. But in the end, we hope you select a topic that you truly wish to learn about. Don't let rank advancement be the only consideration.
2.) Consider Your Age
While there is no age or grade requirement for any merit badge, certain classes at the MBC are recommended for older Scouts. In the short duration of a single day, the nature and amount of material covered in these classes will possibly make it difficult for a younger Scout to keep up.  This can slow the pace of the class, and the class will not complete the intended material.  We want you to enjoy what you do here so you will do it well.
3.) Getting Ready for MBU Day (Read the book)
OK. So, you have selected your badges and registered online.  Congratulations! The next thing that you should do, if you have not already done so, is to get a copy of the Merit Badge pamphlet for yourself. (Read the book.) You should read through the pamphlet so that you are completely familiar with it. In fact (Read the book), you may want to read it through more than once. (Read the book.)
We do not guarantee that you will complete any badge.  Many MB classes will have published a list of prerequisites, or your instructor will contact you with a list they would like you to have completed before the first session.  These are requirements that you should complete before MBU day.  When you complete them, bring all materials to class with you, such as notes, pictures, writings, reports, and letters. (Read the book.) It is up to you to make sure that you complete every requirement. Even if they are not listed, some requirements may, by their nature, not be doable in a classroom. (Read the book.) You should at least attempt to complete these before the MBU.  If you can do this, then you will get the most out of the workshop.  If you do not, then you won't (Read the book.)
4.) Blue Merit Badge Cards
We will be tracking requirements digitally,
and will send out a record or digital copies fo the blue cards after the completion of the scon weekend.
If you have a blue card you can follow the following:
Before the MBU, you should fill out the card with your name, address, Merit Badge, and Troop information.  Your Scoutmaster should sign this card, indicating that they approve you taking the class (Read the book.)  You are responsible for your card. Keep it safe. (Read the book.)
5.) ON MBU Day LEARN and ACHIEVE
This is a formal event.  Proudly wear your Field Uniform. Make sure to have your Blue Merit Badge Card and any prerequisite work that you have done (or its proof) with you. Bring your Merit Badge Pamphlet. (Read the Book.)

November 7, 2026
Lunch is provided
Scouts are asked to select their TOP FOUR merit badge choices through Sunday, October 25.
After October 25, volunteers will
try
and use scout selections to optimize the class schedule and register scouts in TWO of their top four classes.
On Wednesday, October 28, Class selections will open for any scouts registered after October 25.
Registration CLOSES on Thursday, November 5.
Thoughts for Choosing Classes:
All of these classes are taught by professors from WSU and all of the classes are in four hour blocks.  Every effort is made to present material and instruct in a hands-on way and at the level of the scouts present.  That being said, please read through the merit badge requirements for the badges your child is interested in with your child in mind.  Perhaps following your scout for the day and helping to provide some support where needed would help them to be successful or perhaps your child would be most successful in taking just one class instead of two.  A reminder that it is also acceptable for a scout to NOT complete the badge during the class session.  Instructors are registered as Merit Badge Counselors and are happy to work with your scout after the event to sign off on requirements that were missed if your scout contacts them afterwards.  This typically happens when scouts are asked to do requirements like "research 3 careers in this field and the education required" but scouts are enthusiastically practicing the hands on skills they were previously working on instead - can't really be upset about the enthusiasm or the maximising of time in the lab!  If the badges your child requests have such research components, you are also welcome to prepare work for those questions and bring it with you to class.
ADULTS:
Adults are needed to support our classrooms through basic classroom management and help to support scouts by stepping in and guiding through challenging moments as they arise so that the instructor can keep the rest of the class on topic.  These are the same ways we support our scouts at troop meetings!  Event leadership will be available to step in should higher support be needed.
You do not need to be a registered leader to support the event.  All of our instructors are registered and Youth Protection trained as Merit Badge Counselors.  We do request that all adults take Safeguarding Youth training (formerly YPT) via my.scouting.org if not registered.
Adults who have indicated they are staying will also select which classrooms they are in or be assigned as needed (if indicating general availability to support)  Adults who plan on following their scouts to classes will be requested that they keep an eye on all scouts in the classrooms they are in as needed.  Contact info for event leadership will be provided to all classroom adults in case extra support of a scout is needed.

/612-121288.desc:
Cub Scout Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO) Trainin
About the Training
BALOO (Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation) is the essential outdoor training for all Cub Scout leaders and parent volunteers who want to plan and lead pack or den camping experiences. This course introduces participants to the basics of outdoor program planning, safety, and Cub Scout-level camping skills. The training emphasizes fun, simplicity, and confidence-building — helping new leaders bring the adventure of the outdoors to their pack. Upon successful completion of this course, participants will be certified to organize and lead pack or den overnighters, including Webelos and Arrow of Light camping activities.
Learning Objectives
By completing this hands-on course, participants will be able to:
Explain the focus of the Cub Scout camping program
Plan and carry out a safe, fun, and successful pack overnight experience
Demonstrate confidence in key outdoor skills
Identify available Scouting America and local resources
Understand requirements for running a Cub Scout-level overnight event
Prerequisites
To be considered “BALOO Trained,” participants must complete both components of the course:
Online component: Available through My.Scouting.org under “Training.”
Practical, hands-on component: This in-person weekend at Camp Thunderbird meets this part.
Participants must also:
Be registered with a Scouting America unit
Have current Safeguarding Youth Training (SYT) completed prior to the course
If the online portion is not completed before the weekend, “Trained” status will be withheld until both parts are finished.
Who Should Attend
BALOO is designed for:
New Cub Scout leaders or parent volunteers who have little to no camping experience
Pack parents and leaders who want to expand into outdoor programming
While current pack leaders are welcome, this course especially supports new volunteers ready to help plan and lead pack overnighters.
What to Expect
This is a practical, outdoor-based training that includes cooking, campsite setup, and Cub Scout-level camping activities. Participants will spend time both learning and practicing the skills needed to confidently lead their own pack overnight.
The environment is supportive, hands-on, and focused on learning by doing. Bring your enthusiasm, a sense of adventure, and a readiness to have fun in the outdoors!
What to Bring
Please review and pack based on our BALOO Gear List.
Comfortable outdoor clothing and shoes
Field uniform
Tent and sleeping gear
Personal items and toiletries
Notebook and pen
Snacks or comfort items (we will try to accommodate known allergies and dietary restrictions)
Additional Resources
Participants are encouraged to review these resources before attending:
Guide to Safe Scouting
Age-Appropriate Guidelines
Cub Scout Program Leader Resources
Pacific Harbors Council Camping

/612-26PistolNRA.desc:
This 2-day course is intended to develop the Knowledge, Skills, and Attitude necessary to plan and instruct Scouting America Pistol shooting programs, merit badges, and NRA Basics of Pistol Shooting classes. Successful completion of this program will qualify candidates as NRA Basic Pistol Instructors, which is required to supervise Scouting America Pistol shooting activities.
Prerequisite:
Possession of basic firearm safety and shooting skills is a perquisite for certification as an NRA instructor. Prior to the instructor training, candidates complete a pre-course questionnaire and demonstrate their firearm background in pre-course assessment exercises.  There will  opportunities for shooting the qualifying round on course.
Description:
Course is presented in three parts: Basic Instructor Training (BIT), Basic Pistol Shooting and Pistol Shooting Instructor. Students demonstrate organizational and teaching skills via participation in practical exercises during the course and complete an instructor certification examination. Students will receive the NRA Trainer’s Guide, NRA Pistol Instructor Candidate Packet, and NRA Basic Pistol Shooting course student packet.
During the course candidates will learn NRA policies and procedures; basic public speaking skills; training methodology; use of a training team and training aids; organizing a course, building a budget; and finally preparing to teach. Candidates take turns working in teams, conducting portions of the course to other candidates who portray basic students.
Schedule:
Saturday December 12th  – Basic Pistol Shooting
Sunday December 13th  – Pistol Instructor Course (BIT included)
7 AM to 6 PM both days
Fees:
The course fee is $150 and includes all program materials, snacks, water and
What to Bring:
Each participant will need to provide a .22 LR pistol, 100 rounds of ammunition plus ear and eye protection and must attend all classes and pass the tests with a 90% or better score
There are no nearby food establishments so participants must bring a lunch, hydration and snacks

Get ready to lace up your boots and hit the trail! The Great Scout Hike-Off Weekend is an exciting outdoor adventure designed for all levels of Scouting. Whether you're just starting your journey or blazing new paths, this event offers the perfect opportunity to connect with nature, build skills, face challenges, and have fun with your fellow Scouts.
Pacific Harbors Council Refund Policy applies to this event,
click here to read the refund policy
.

Cub Scout Day Hike 2026
We are thrilled to invite you to our 2nd Annual Cub Scout Day Hike at Camp Thunderbird! This exciting event features a 3-mile trail hike for our Cub Scouts, complete with engaging activity stations along the way. The hike will conclude at the parade field, where the Cub Scouts can enjoy a picnic-style lunch followed by several field games.
This is a family-friendly event that allows for individual family registration, ensuring everyone can participate. If you’d like to hike as a den or pack, please register individually and check-in together, with one person designated to lead your group.
We will be implementing staggered starts for each hike session to eliminate pre-hike wait times. Please arrive at Camp Thunderbird at least 30 minutes before your scheduled hike time.
The hike is designed to be a self-paced event, allowing the Cub Scouts to explore nature and enjoy the journey -
this is all about fun, not speed!
Reminder:
A parent or legal guardian must be with their Cub Scout during the event.
Registration deadline is November 6, 2026
Pricing:
Cub Scout Youth: $15
Cub Scout Adult: $10
Things to bring:
Appropriate footwear – The ground will likely be wet and probably muddy in places
Raingear – Always be prepared for rain
Layered clothing – It’s cold in November under those trees
Your Cub Scout 6 essentials – Always good to reinforce “Being Prepared”
First-Aid kit – Scratches and cuts can happen on the trail
Water bottle – Stay hydrated
Flashlight – Never know when it will be needed
Trail snacks – Hiking makes you hungry
Sun protection - even in November
Whistle – for emergency use only
A great attitude and readiness to have fun!
Night Hike - BSA & Venture Scouts
Embark on an unforgettable adventure with our 10-Mile Night Hike Challenge! Trek under the stars through rugged terrain while testing your grit at 10 unique and challenging stations along the way. We will be having activites and merit badge midway during the day on saturday prior to night hike.
please be advised depending on hiking group size you may be asked to combine with another group. we try to keep hiking groups to around 15 participates.

/612-NYLT27.desc:
June 20th-June 25th, 2027 AT CAMP THUNDERBIRD
What is Bushmaster NYLT?
Bushmaster NYLT is a weeklong experience based on the activities of a typical unit during a month of program. The course is a combination of classroom and practical exercises, all taught by a youth staff, modeling the best in leadership skills, using the teaching E.D.G.E. The course is about vision-based team building with a wide variety of fun and challenging activities.
Who May Attend Bushmaster NYLT?
This course is a co-ed course open to Scouts BSA and Venture Crew Members. Scoutmasters and Crew Advisors select, nominate and fill out a unit leader recommendation for the participants who may attend NYLT, sending those who currently or will soon hold key leadership positions in the Unit.
Scouts attending must meet the following qualifications before the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Health and Medical Record form parts A. B, and C.
Must be at least 13 years old and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program.
Scouts registered in a Troop must have earned the First Class Rank before attending NYLT.
Have leader recommendation.
It is recommended they have at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is iportant that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
These requirements from Scouting America may be found
here
.
What is the cost for 2027?
The fee of $325 paid before 30 April 2027 ($360 if paid on or after May 1st) covers the cost of food, facility, program supplies, insurance, patch, cap, training materials, and one (1) course T-shirt (Additional T-shirts may be ordered). Personal camping gear and materials are to be supplied by each individual Scout. All fees are due no later than May 31st, 2027.
If financial assistance is needed please contact John Decker at jwdecker@myctl.net or (206) 999-1855 before 30 April 2027!

Scouts BSA – Ready to level up before summer camp?
If you're a new Scouts BSA member or working toward Tenderfoot, Second Class, or First Class, Trailblazers is the perfect opportunity to get a jumpstart on rank advancements before heading to summer camp. This camp focuses on essential Trail to First Class requirements, allowing Scouts to complete key skills now so they can focus on earning fun merit badges with their troop later in the summer.
Date:
Saturday - Sunday, May 2-3, 2026
Location:
Camp Thunderbird
Who Can Attend:
Any registered Scouts BSA youth working toward Scout, Tenderfoot, Second Class, or First Class.

Class sign-ups will occur on Saturday as part of check-in, giving Scouts and leaders time to review the schedule ahead of camp and plan their weekend before arrival.
Why Attend Trailblazers?
Jumpstart your rank advancements before summer camp.
Learn and practice essential Scouting skills like knots, lashings, fire-building, first-aid, and navigation.
Be better prepared for troop summer camp, where you can focus on merit badges.
Build confidence and meet fellow Scouts before your summer troop adventures.

Registration closes April 19, 2026 – Late registrations are subject to availability (patch not guaranteed).

Begin your journey to First Class and make the most of summer camp – register now!
We Need Staff – Join the Team!
Trailblazers cannot happen without dedicated staff members to guide and mentor Scouts. We are looking for youth and adult staff to help with skill instruction and leadership.
Positions Available:
Youth Staff (13+ and First Class recommended)

Areas of Instruction Include:
Lashings & Knot-Tying
First Aid & Emergency Skills
Aquatics & Water Safety
Fire Building & Tools (Fire Building, Knife, Saw, & Axe Safety)
Map & Compass Navigation & Hiking
If you are interested in staffing, please complete the staff registration form with your preferred area of teaching. We will reach out once staff selections have been made.

Cub Scout day camps are organized by the Mountaineer Area Council, Scouting America and conducted by volunteers from the local area.
Day camps are for youth entering the 1st through 5th grades the following school year. Participants entering Kindergarten or younger are not eligible to participate.

Mission of the Order of the Arrow
To achieve the mission of Scouting America through transformative fellowship that ignites limitless Scouting journeys.
Purpose of the Order of the Arrow
As Scouting’s National Honor Society, we forge lifelong bonds among the leaders in Scouting and:
Recognize those who exemplify the Scout Oath and Law in their daily lives and, through that recognition, cause others to act in the same way.
Reinforce a life purpose of leadership in cheerful service to others.
Create and deliver peer-led, adult-guided, advanced leadership experiences for Scouts and Scouters that positively impact their unit, community, and ultimately our nation.
Be an integral part of Scouting America and encourage participation in all it offers through units, outdoor adventures, and national events to further the Scouting experience.

/615-NYLT26.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
Camp Mountaineer
|    July 5-10, 2027
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
is an exciting, action-packed program designed to provide youth with leadership skills and experience that they can apply within their troops and in other situations requiring leadership of self and others.
NYLT is a six-day course that emphasizes hands-on learning in a fun, engaging environment. Through a blend of activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and games, participants will develop confidence and leadership abilities while working together as a team.
The course content is designed to build leadership concepts progressively, using practical exercises to reinforce learning. Participants embark on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership, which brings the leadership lessons to life as they apply their skills throughout the course.
REMINDER:  Please bring a letter of recommendation from your Unit Leader to attend NYLT.
WHO:
Scouts BSA or Venturing youth
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Annual Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members must be at least 13 years old by the first day of the course and no older than 17 years old. They must also have completed the Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops and achieved the rank of First Class.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14 years old (or 13 and completed eighth grade) and can be no older than 20 years old. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships and have some basic camping experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.
WHEN:
Monday, July 5 - Saturday, July 10
running concurrently with Scouts BSA resident camp at Camp Mountaineer
WHERE:
Camp Mountaineer
Address:
187 Camp Mountaineer Rd, Morgantown, WV 26508
FEES:
$275 per participant if paid by April 15, 2027 ($300 after April 15, 2027)
Cost includes all course materials, meals, tent housing, patch, course hat, and t-shirt.
While not required, it is common practice for a Scout's unit to fund their NYLT experience as an investment to their unit. Should a unit not have the finanical means to support their Scout attending, the unit leader should reach out to Mountaineer Area Council for information on available financial assistance.

Established in 1956, Ed Bryant Scout Reservation was constructed specifically to serve Scouts of what is now the Glacier's Edge Council.  Today, Scouts from all over the United States attend one of the 4 weeks of summer camp.  Our 244 acre property is nestled along the banks of beautiful Castle Rock Lake, not far from Mauston, Wisconsin and the Wisconsin Dells.  We offer a diverse set of programs, quality facilities, and a dedicated staff committed to outstanding service to Scouts and Scouters.

/635-114932.desc:
Register under
Are you searching for programs that will lead to member recruitment, reactivation, and retention?  Then we think we have just the Scouting America Supplemental Training course for you!  Like many things in Scouting, the Scouting America Certified Angling Instructor (CAI) training course is designed to be fun with a purpose!
What can Certified Angling Instructors do?
Teach the Scouting America Fishing Basics course.
Train and qualify Scouting America Angling Educators.
Serve on your Council’s Fishing Committee or Start one.
Be a subject matter expert for Fishing Derbies, Summer Camp, Merit Badge clinics, and fishing related advancement.
Course Highlights
Become recognized as a Scouting America Certified Angling Instructor and receive an Official Train the Trainer Certification CS-61 and a CAI patch.
Learn basic fishing and fly-fishing skills including fly casting, fly tying, knots, and how to teach them.  Receive the materials to assist you in delivering the program as well as online resource locations.
As a CAI you will have the opportunity to get fishing and fly-fishing equipment at greatly reduced rates for teaching Scouts.
Participants will
Understand available resources for unit angler education program development to inspire member recruitment and retention.
Gain education and insight through active participation in dozens of Angling Education learning activities.
Activities include
Age and Skill-Level based programs
Focused on the aims of Scouting America Cub Scout, Scouts BSA, Sea Scout, and Venturing programs.
Focus on the methods that include Outdoors, Angling and Conservation.
Who can attend
All registered adult volunteers.
Youth, that are 15 years or older can participate and must have earned their Fishing & Fly-Fishing Merit Badges.
Open to both In-Council and Out-of-Council attendees.
No prior fishing experience is required.
6 Virtual Sessions
6:00pm – 8:00pm CST with after class time from 8:00pm – 8:30 pm CST.
Course Dates:
(All 6 classes are required to receive your Certified Angling Instructor Certification)
Class 1: Thursday, October 1st - Intro, Pack and Troop fishing programs
Class 2: Thursday, October 8th - Fishing & Fly-Fishing Tackle
Class 3: Thursday, October 15th - Safety, Ethics, Fishery Management, and Knots
Class 4: Thursday, October 22nd - The nature of fish, Where to find fish, and Fishing Basics
Class 5: Thursday, October 29th - Casting, Fishing, Cleaning and Cooking
Class 6: Thursday, November 5th - Planning Fishing Events, Angling Educator, Special Offers, Deliver the Promise, and Graduation
Where:  Online via Zoom
Cost:  $10
For questions, contact
Course Director
Kathy Myszewski at
pinkbuffalo4@gmail.com

Come on out to Wisconsin International Raceway in Kaukauna for a fun on-track box-car race! Youth have the chance to decorate a cardboard box race car then race it through a dozen stations on the track. We also plan to have some vehicles from various public services, and even some actual race cars, that youth can get up and close with.
Our goal is to have a FUN event to kick off the upcoming Scouting year!  You can use this as a “bring a friend” style event to promote scouting in a fun, low-key way.  Feel free to wear your pack's t-shirt, your favorite Scouting t-shirt, or even a fun costume; uniforms are not required for this event. Registration is $10.00 per Scout via the link on this page.
For each registered Scout that signs up to attend this event, you may bring along a friend who is not currently in Cub Scouts for FREE.

Scouts will run around the WIR racetrack with their box cars they built, going through different stations along the way!
If you are interested in volunteering to help run one of the stations on the track, please contact the Event Chair, Chris Pohlman at cdpolkat@hotmail.com .

/635-LifetoEagleTraining1212.desc:
Life-to-Eagle Training takes place on Saturday, December 12, 2026 from 9:00 am-12:00 noon at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, 2736 Glendale Avenue, Green Bay. Instruction will be provided for current youth Life Scouts, adult Eagle Mentors, and other adult volunteers.
Life Scouts, please print and bring with you a copy of the Eagle Scout Leadership Service Project Workbook attached in the lower, right-hand corner of this page.
This informational session is free to attend, but registration is required for planning purposes. Thank you.
+ + +
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Life Scouts
Should I wear my uniform?
Field uniform (button-down shirt) is encouraged, but not required.
Should I bring my parents?
Yes, it is encouraged that one parent attend.
Does my Scoutmaster need to be there?
All are welcome. If your Scoutmaster is seasoned and knowledgeable of the process, they do not need to attend. If they are a new leader, it would be helpful for them to learn the process.
Is Eagle Mentor the same as Eagle Coach?
Technically, the Eagle Mentor is the one that works with the Scout at the unit level throughout all of the requirements. The Eagle Coach is the one that works with the Scout once they begin the Eagle Scout Service Project process. That being said, in some units, this is the same individual.
Do I need to know my project?
No, you do not need to know what your project will be to attend this training.
Should I attend if my project is already approved?
It might be helpful for you to attend so you have a better understanding of the entire process and get answers to any questions you may have.
Parents
May I bring my younger children, including non-Scouting children?
It is discouraged to bring younger children as they will need to sit through three hours of training. It will be your responsibility to keep them entertained. There is also a concern of space in the facility to have them there as well.

xperience the outdoor adventure of Camp Rokilio!
The Rokilio Experience is an exciting introduction to the meaning of summer camp, with an opportunity for youth and parents to see camp in action. Welcome to BALOO training! It is the Cub Scout leader training required for any Cub Scout den or pack outdoor event, including pack camping overnighters and Webelos den overnighters. Why Wood Badge?
Some Scout units thrive because of strong, purposeful leadership. Wood Badge helps you develop that leadership clear vision, effective communication, teamwork, and follow-through—through hands-on learning and adventure.
What You’ll Gain
Stronger Scout units
: Empower your team to deliver impactful programs.
Renewed passion
: Rediscover the spark that brought you to Scouting.
Connections
: Build lasting relationships with fellow leaders.
Deeper insight
: Understand not just how Scouting works, but why it matters.
Practical skills
: Learn communication, conflict resolution, servant leadership, and team development.
Broader impact
: Apply lessons to your unit, workplace, family, and community.
The Experience
Wood Badge is a two-weekend immersive leadership experience in an active outdoor setting taking place August 20-22, 2027 and September 11-12, 2027. Open to all registered adult Scouters with Safeguarding Youth Training and position training, no prior leadership experience required. After the course, you’ll set five goals to complete within 18 months with counselor support.
Accessibility
Don’t let cost stop you—many units and employers cover training, and scholarships are available. Contact Course Director, Shalimar Thiel at shalimar.thiel@gmail.com for details.
Wood Badge is where you strengthen your leadership, make a lasting impact, and grow with confidence.

/640-116221.desc:
You are invited to join us on the Delaware River for the
2027 GNYC Spring Raft-O-Ree!
Program includes a day of rafting on the Delaware as well as an evening movie! Units will camp in TMR Camp Keowa and will be transported to the Delaware River via Landers River Trips. Participants will be provided Saturday lunch on the river as well as dinner in the camp dining hall.
Unit awards for Best Themed Raft, Best Troop Mascot, Most Patriotic Raft, Funniest Hats Best Rafting Outfits and Scout Spirit will be issued.
Event Rules
All participants will need to bring with them the
BSA Medical Form Parts A and B
. Unit leaders should complete a
BSA Pre-Event Medical Screening Checklist.
In order to Participate in Rafting on the Delaware River participants will need to be clasified as "BSA Swimmers".
Dock Tests will be administered Friday Evening and Saturday Morning At the Camps Waterfront. Swimmers will complete this test:
Jump feetfirst into water over the head in depth.
Level off and swim 75 yards in a strong manner using one or more of the following strokes: sidestroke, breaststroke, trudgen, or crawl; then swim 25 yards using an easy resting backstroke.
The 100 yards must be completed in one swim without stops and must include at least one sharp turn. After completing the swim, rest by floating.
Only BSA Swimmers may participate in the rafting portion of the Raft-O-Ree.
Frequently Asked Questions
Q: What Medical Forms are needed for participation?
A: All Participants must arrive with completed Parts A and B of the BSA Medical Form as well as a BSA pre-event medical screening form.
Q: Is there additional Paperwork?
A: Each participant is required to computer a
Liability Waiver for Lander’s River Trips
Q: What is the BSA Swim Test?
A: Jump feet first into water over the head in depth. Level off and swim 75 yards in a strong manner using one or more of the following strokes: sidestroke, breaststroke, trudgen, or crawl; then swim 25 yards using an easy resting backstroke. The 100 yards must be completed in one swim without stops and must include at least one sharp turn. After completing the swim, rest by floating.
Q: Where will Troops Stay?
A: Units will be assigned to campsites within Camp Keowa. While some Summer Camp canvas tents may already be set up on platforms, units should bring tents and plan to use their own tents and sleeping bags. Be Prepared.
Q: Who Needs to Take a Swim Test?
A: Per BSA safe swim defense, individuals participating in boating activities must be BSA Swimmers. The Keowa waterfront will be set up and opened and tests will be offered Friday evening and Saturday morning. If your unit is planning to conduct tests prior to arrival please reach out to the event organizers- as unit swim records must be completed by “Council Approved” individuals, and their certifications must be included with the swim record. Raft-O-Ree will provide unit swim records for units that complete swim tests at the event.
Q: What Meals are Provided?
A: Units will be provided lunch Saturday at the Narrowsburg boat launch, at the half-way point of the rafting trip. Saturday dinner will be provided in the Camp Keowa Dining Hall. Each participant will get a bag of snacks for their river trip. Units should have a plan for Friday Dinner, Saturday Breakfast, and Sunday Breakfast.
Q: Is the Raft-O-Ree a Race?
A: This is a recreational rafting trip and groups are encouraged to raft together and have a great time. There are fun awards that rafts can win for: Best Themed Raft, Best Troop Mascot, Most Patriotic Raft, Funniest Hats, Best Rafting Outfits, and Scout Spirit.
Q: Can a family participate without a Troop?
A: Yes, Scouting families can register to participate without their full Troop. Rafts should seat 4-6 individuals . Groups smaller than 4 will be combined or placed with other groups to have a functioning raft. Youth must be members of Scouts BSA. BSA policy prohibits Cub Scouts from boating on moving water.

Nestled within 500 acres of picturesque woodlands along the breathtaking Palisades Park, Alpine Day Camp offers an unforgettable summer experience for your children.
Our expansive grounds feature miles of enchanting hiking trails, state-of-the-art indoor and outdoor climbing facilities, and a sprawling swimming pool. Every aspect of the Alpine Day Camp is meticulously designed to make the most of this natural setting, providing your children with a rich tapestry of adventures.
Register by December 1st 2026 and lock in this year's rates at only $560 a week!
Whether your child joins us for a single week or embraces the full eight-week experience, the memories forged at Alpine Day Camp will linger as cherished treasures for years to come. Immerse your child in the wonders of nature, foster lasting friendships, and watch them blossom through a summer filled with laughter, exploration, and growth. Alpine Day Camp is not just a camp; it's a canvas of experiences where every child's unique spirit is celebrated and nurtured. Join us for a summer of joy, adventure, and lifelong memories.
Dedicated to inclusivity, we joyfully welcome boys and girls entering grades 1-7 to join our vibrant camp community. /640-Woodbadge27.desc:
What is Wood Badge?
Reflecting the best of over a century of Scouting experience, Wood Badge draws upon the most current leadership models used by corporate America, academic circles and successful organizations throughout the country.
Wood Badge training was begun by Baden Powell in 1919 as a way to ensure that leaders of Scout troops were properly trained. Since then, Wood Badge has been held worldwide, providing advanced leadership training to thousands of Scout leaders. Wood Badge builds upon the best traditions and experiences of Scouting America and also draws from a wide range of courses within and beyond the bounds of Scouting to present the latest in leadership theory and team development.
Why Attend?
Whether you are a new or longtime Scouting leader, this course is for you. Wood Badge is the ultimate leadership training program for the adult leaders of the Scouting America. Similar corporate-focused courses cost thousands of dollars per attendee and may not offer the same depth.
Wood Badge is a modern format of training that delivers the latest in leadership skills that will help you be the best leader possible. These are skills that will become part of your everyday life. You will use these skills at home, career, religious institution, and anywhere leadership is needed. The course is made to provide the highest quality training with a highly experienced staff to a diverse audience. We promise you friendship, camaraderie, knowledge, personal awareness, and, most of all, fun!
By taking Wood Badge, Scouters will acquire valuable tools such as listening, communicating, conflict management, project planning and leading change. Participants will better learn to understand and appreciate diversity and differences in our society. They will learn skills that will make them a better Scout leader. Units with trained leaders are able to deliver an improved program and a more meaningful experience for the youth Scouting serves.
By attending Wood Badge, participants will internalize the five themes of Wood Badge: Living the Values, Growing, Connecting, Guiding, and Empowering.
Who Should Attend?
Wood Badge is designed to meet the advanced leadership needs of all Scouters, particularly unit-level Scouters, such as Cub Scout leaders, scoutmasters and assistants, Venturing crew advisors, Sea Scout skippers and mates, and unit committee chairs and members. Also, Scouters serving at the district and council levels can achieve greater effectiveness through Wood Badge.
To attend Wood Badge, individuals must:
Be registered members of Scouting America at least 18 years old.
(Venturers & Sea Scouts ages 18-20 do not need to be registered in an adult leadership role.)
Have completed the basic training courses for their Scouting position.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment.
Everybody must complete the Annual Health and Medical Record form, parts A, B & C.
Program:
The Wood Badge program consists of two parts: Practical Training and the Application Phase.
The Practical Training is a five-day experience where the Scouter lives as a member of a patrol, practices skills of leadership, and
learns how these skills apply in the role of the adult leader
in developing youth through the Scouting program. Through living in this setting for an extended period of time, they develop a Scouting spirit and zeal for the program that motivates them to do a better job in the Scouting position they have accepted. During the Practical Training, all participants develop a “Ticket.” This Ticket will help you develop a vision for your contribution to the mission of Scouting, and then help you develop goals and execute a plan to achieve that vision.
A Ticket Counselor from your council will be appointed to provide assistance and guidance as this Ticket is worked. The “working of the ticket” is called the Application Phase of Wood Badge.

No Registration Needed
In an effort to make NYLT available to as many participants as possible, registration is now open and may be completed by any parent or guardian. Once submitted, your Scout will be placed on the reservation list immediately.
Typically, Units are limited to 2–3 participants. Any additional registrants from the same Unit will be placed on a waitlist, and the NYLT team will reach out to discuss available options as space permits.
To secure your Scout’s seat on the course, we strongly encourage you to register as soon as possible.
Campership assistance is available at:
https://nycscouting.org/campership/
Scout Unit Leader Recomendation is Required
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
For many years, junior leader training (JLT) was an important part of the leadership training continuum of Scouting America's local councils. In 2003 and 2004, a task force of leadership experts and hundreds of Scouts in pilot courses across the nation reviewed and tested every aspect of the new NYLT syllabus, which incorporates the latest leadership ideas and presents fresh, vital and meaningful training for today’s Scouts.
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what he must KNOW, and what he must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
NYLT is a six-day course. Content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment. Interconnecting concepts and work processes are introduced early, built upon, and aided by the use of memory aids, which allows participants to understand and employ the leadership skills much faster.
Built on the legacy of past JLT successes, the new NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and audio-visual support, NYLT participants will be engaged in a unified approach to leadership that will give them the skill and confidence to lead well. Through a wide range of activities, games, and adventures, participants will work and play together as they put into action the best Scouting has to offer.
In order to attend a NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Scouting America Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members (male and female) must be at least 13 and First Class,  they must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops, Venturers, and Sea Scouts (male and female) must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Must have a unit leader recommendation form. Form can be downloaded to the right.

Get ready for the most expansive TrEx yet! This year’s Training Extravaganza offers nearly 70 sessions across every corner of Scouting—Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts, OA, and Exploring—along with an incredible lineup of general interest, leadership, camping, and tech-awareness workshops. Youth can dive into 5 new Merit Badge classes offered and career-building opportunities like résumé coaching, financial literacy, college pathways, and drug awareness/Narcan training. Adults can choose from dozens of new and returning sessions covering program development, safety, recruitment, STEM, high-adventure planning, budgeting, Scoutbook tools, and best practices for strengthening units. With course options ranging from hands-on knot tying and Dutch oven cooking to internet safety, Eagle project guidance, patrol games, and bilingual “What Is Scouting” presentations, TREX 2027 delivers something for every leader, parent, and Scout. Explore new ideas, sharpen your skills, and learn from Scouters across all five boroughs as we come together for a full day of training, growth, and fun.
What is TREX?  Why should You attend?
GNYC Training Extravaganza is a supplemental training opportunity organized and taught by volunteer instructors.  It is the only time during the year when you can find, all in one place, the widest variety of training opportunities in all program areas: Cub Scouting, Scouts BSA, and Venturing, as well as sessions for district volunteers and commissioners. Whether you are new to Scouting or a veteran, TREX provides interesting courses for all. Courses will include some of your favorites from years past and some exciting new content. You don’t want to miss TREX!

/653-WoodBadge2028.desc:
Wood Badge
Wood Badge is for the adult leaders (18yrs and up) in Scouting America. Similar corporate courses cost thousands of dollars per attendee. Wood Badge is a modern format of training that delivers the latest in 12 leadership skills that will help you be the best leader possible. These are skills that will become part of your everyday life. You will use these skills not only in scouting, but also at home, at work, in your community and anywhere else leadership is needed. The course is made to provide the highest quality experience with the most knowledgable staff to a diverse audience. We promise you friendship, camaraderie, knowledge, personal awareness, and
most of all FUN! Because . . . if you’re not having fun . . . you’re doing it wrong!
What do we see on course?
We discuss and apply many things on course, like:
Listening
Managing conflict
Leading change
Stages of team development
Coaching & Mentoring
Leadership for different stages
Servant leadership
Project planning
And more!
These come to you in presentations, games, discussions, activities, and other direct and indirect methods.
Why do you want to go?
You want to participate in a Wood Badge course because of the things you will learn and do. Here are some of the benefits:
Stronger units. You will make your Scouting unit — and your sons’ and daughters’ units — stronger.
What and why of Scouting. You will have a deeper understanding of what Scouting is and why we do it.
Experience. You will learn and experience things that will stay with you in Scouting and the rest of your life.
Fun. You will have fun and you will meet interesting people.
Other groups. You will make your other groups, like work, church, even family, stronger.
New skillset.  You will use these new skills not only in scouting, but in your everyday life as well.
Wood Badge is here for you. This is not just a Troop leader training but is designed for all registered leaders in Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, or those that assist any or all of these programs at the district and/or council level. This course will help you better understand “how” and “why” all the Scouting programs tie together.
It is also meant to make you think and understand your “why” . . . the “why” that made you decide to volunteer in Scouting.
It will provide you with many useful servant leadership tools to help empower our youth to have the best possible Scouting experience. The time is NOW, for the future of our youth members and the Scouting program that serves them - there is no better time to attend Wood Badge and make a difference in your unit!
The Ticket
Have you heard of “The Ticket” and wondered what it is? The ticket is a group of five S.M.A.R.T. goals you set for yourself to accomplish after the curriculum phase with the end result being to improve your unit strength, membership, depth of trained leaders and overall unit health. Your Wood Badge training helps you develop and/or hone your unit programming; once that happens, the program will speak volumes and sell itself. You will learn more about this on the course.
Purpose of Wood Badge
The purpose of Wood Badge is to develop skilled and servant leaders who can strengthen Scouting units in achieving the mission of Scouting America.
When we accomplish the mission of Scouting, we execute the program at the unit level.  Every scout DESERVES A TRAINED LEADER.
Although the course is different today, what Baden-Powell said in 1919 still applies:
“One of the purposes of Wood Badge training is to get Scouters to think about the practice of Scouting, to meet together, to exchange experiences, and to live together in the spirit of the Scout Oath and Law.”
For More information: Contact the course director, Paul Vassos (Sherpa), at paulv093-arch@yahoo.com
Do not let the cost deter you from attending this premier leadership course!  Some employers will assist in paying for the course. Individual scouting units and their chartered organizations may have scholarship opportunities

/661-122442.desc:
El Concilio de Puerto Rico y Guajataka Scout Reservation se encuentran listos para ofrecer su tradicional campamento de verano. Los esperamos con un programa variado y lleno de experiencias memorables para niños, jóvenes y líderes adultos. Crearemos un entorno de aventura, hermandad y desarrollo para todos los acampadores, dentro de las hermosas y actualizadas facilidades. Con una nueva imagen y actitud, buscamos horrar los 87 años de historia de nuestro Santuario de amistad, pero atemperándonos al Scouting del día de hoy. En esta sesión de campamento de verano ofreceremos un programa variado para Cubs Scouts, Scouting y Venturing. Entre los ofrecimientos estarán sobre 55 Insignias de Mérito, los rangos de Tenderfoot, Second Class y First Class, sobre 65 Aventuras para Cub Scouts, incluyendo por primera vez a los Lions y un entretenido programa complementario de diversión y aventura.
___________________________________________________________________________________________________
The Puerto Rico Council and Guajataka Scout Reservation are ready to offer their traditional summer camp. We look forward to seeing you with a varied program full of memorable experiences for children, youth, and adult leaders. We will create an environment of adventure, brotherhood, and development for all campers within our beautiful and updated facilities. With a new image and attitude, we seek to honor the 87 years of history of our Sanctuary of Friendship while adapting to the Scouting of today. In this summer camp session, we will offer a diverse program for Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, and Venturing. Offerings will include over 55 Merit Badges, the ranks of Tenderfoot, Second Class, and First Class, over 65 Adventures for Cub Scouts — including Lions for the first time — and an entertaining complementary program of fun and adventure.

/662-113919.desc:
2027 Phil-A-Palooza Trek Training Program
Are you going on a backpacking trek at the Philmont Scout Ranch in the Summer of 2027? If you are going on a 7, 9, or 12 day trek in 2027, then you and your crew (all adults and all youth) are invited to the 2027 Philmont PHIL-A-PALOOZA Trek Training program hosted by our Longhorn Council Philmont Ambassadors on the weekend of Friday, February 19 through Sunday, February 21, 2027, at Sid Richardson Scout Ranch, Camp 9 Dining Hall. Bring your entire crew out to learn valuable skills the entire weekend and camp, hike. Use this weekend as one of your Shakedown campouts. This year we have incorporated Ranger Skills, including Philmont style cooking and cleaning methods Saturday night
At the PHIL-A-PALOOZA. The Ambassadors will go over topics to make your trek be the best that it can be!
The program will start Friday evening at 8:00 PM on February 19, 2027, inside the Camp 9 Dining Hall. And it ends Sunday, February 21, 2027 after your crew does a hike on the Sid Trail.
The program will cover:
YOUR FIRST 48 HOURS AT PHILMONT | FITNESS TRAINING | YOUR HEALTH AND THE HEALTH OF YOUR CREW | BEST PRACTICES | LESSONS LEARNED | SPECIAL DIET | (Saturday LUNCH and DINNER is included in your registration) | MAP STUDY/ UTM TRAINING | HYGIENE BREAKOUTS, ONE FOR MALES AND ONE FOR FEMALES | BREAKOUTS (Hands on gear) TO DISCUSS TENTS, SLEEP SYSTEMS, BACKPACKS, FOOTWEAR, CAMP STOVES, CAMP KITCHEN, CLOTHING AND GEAR | ITENARY TREK REVIEW ON THE PHILMONT MAP (LOGISTICS).
** And Ranger skills training by the staff, like setting up your campsite, bearmuda triangle, bear bag rope throwing practice, setting up actual Philmont Tents and Crew Flys, trail etiquette, pack lines. Practice Philmont style cooking Saturday night dinner (Saturday night meal is now included in registration). Practice cleaning of the dinner pots, bowls, spoons, etc. with our portable sumps. And a campfire program after dinner.**
The program will be conducted by our own Longhorn Council Philmont Ambassadors, Circle Ten Philmont Ambassadors, which includes current and past Philmont Staffers and Philmont Training Center Faculty. And this year we will have a min. of 2 current Philmont Camping Staffers joining us from Cimarron New Mexico.
When:
February 19 – February 21, 2027
Where:
Sid Richardson Scout Ranch, Camp 9 Dining Hall, Lake Bridgeport, TX.
Time:
9:00 pm CST Feb 19th – 2:30pm CST Feb 21st (Noon if you opt out of hiking the Sid Trail)
Lunch:
Saturday Lunch will be provided.
Dinner:

LHC USA Archery Level I Instructor Course
March 27th, 2027 &    Nov. 6th, 2027
Worth Ranch, LHC
Those wishing to run Troop and Venture Unit archery activities and to become an approved Archery Merit Badge Counselor, will need to complete the USA Archery Level 1 Instructor Certification or above.
The class will start at 8:00 am at the Archery Range. The Practical class is a busy, hands-on 4.5 hours. We will break for a short lunch and continue BSA Shooting Sports policy, LHC Archery Policy, and how to conduct the Archery Merit Badge including arrow making and string making. This will take an additional 2 hours.
There is a three-step process to becoming a USA Archery Level 1 Instructor. One, register and complete the USA Archery Level 1 on-line Instructor course ($40). Two, register for the USA Archery Level 1 Practical on the USA Archery website (no cost). Three, register for Practical on the Longhorn Council Training page, and attend the LHC USA Archery Level 1 Practical at a LHC camp.
Again, a three-step process. First, go to the USA Archery Level 1 Instructor Certification web page, register to take the on-line and successfully complete the On-Line Level I Instructor Couse. Cost $40 payable to USA Archery. It takes about 4 hours, is available 24 hours a day, and does not need to be completed all at once. Passing criteria on the exam is 75%. See link below.
Level 1 Instructor Certification - USA Archery (usarchery.org)
Second, once the participant has completed the on-line Level I class, they must then register on the USA Archery web site for an in-person Level 1 Practical Course sanctioned and conducted by a Level II Instructor Trainer. The Practical Course involves applying what has been learned in the on-line class through activities on an archery range. USA Archery does not charge for this section. Go to the link below, locate the LHC USA Archery Level 1 Practical Class and register for it. See link below.
Level 1 Practical Course - USA Archery (usarchery.org)
Third, the participant must also complete registration for the Practical class at the LHC camp through the LHC training page. The cost is $45.  (This is the page you are on now - click the REGISTER button in the top right corner!)
NOTE:
Registration needs to be complete 10 days in advance of the Practical class.
This class targets participants whom are 18 years or older. Youth, 15 and older, may attend with permission of the Instructor Trainer, and must be accompanied by a parent.
The USA Archery Level 1 Practical Class will be conducted at a Longhorn Council Scout Camp or Ranch. All Scouting rules are in effect.
Scouters should have a copy of their BSA Medical Form and their current YPT in case the Camp Ranger wishes to see them. Non-Scouters must be accompanied by a registered Scouter at all times.
The Practical Class is a busy 4.5 hours followed by BSA/LHC archery and MB Counselor information.
This class will be outdoors on an established archery range using camp and Instructor equipment. The class will start 8 to 8:30 am. After eating lunch the participant will provide, the BSA/LHC portion will continue for up to 2 hours.
Camping may be available if needed Friday night..
If you have questions, contact:

Three, register for Practical on the Longhorn Council Training page, and attend the LHC USA Archery Level 1 Practical at a LHC camp.
Again, a three-step process. First, go to the USA Archery Level 1 Instructor Certification web page, register to take the on-line and successfully complete the On-Line Level I Instructor Couse. Cost $40 payable to USA Archery. It takes about 4 hours, is available 24 hours a day, and does not need to be completed all at once. Passing criteria on the exam is 75%. See link below.
Level 1 Instructor Certification - USA Archery (usarchery.org)
Second, once the participant has completed the on-line Level I class, they must then register on the USA Archery web site for an in-person Level 1 Practical Course sanctioned and conducted by a Level II Instructor Trainer. The Practical Course involves applying what has been learned in the on-line class through activities on an archery range. USA Archery does not charge for this section. Go to the link below, locate the LHC USA Archery Level 1 Practical Class and register for it. See link below.
Level 1 Practical Course - USA Archery (usarchery.org)
Third, the participant must also complete registration for the Practical class at the LHC camp through the LHC training page. The cost is $45.  (This is the page you are on now - click the REGISTER button in the top right corner!)
NOTE:
Registration needs to be complete 10 days in advance of the Practical class.
This class targets participants whom are 18 years or older. Youth, 15 and older, may attend with permission of the Instructor Trainer, and must be accompanied by a parent.
The USA Archery Level 1 Practical Class will be conducted at a Longhorn Council Scout Camp or Ranch. All Scouting rules are in effect.
Scouters should have a copy of their BSA Medical Form and their current YPT in case the Camp Ranger wishes to see them. Non-Scouters must be accompanied by a registered Scouter at all times.
The Practical Class is a busy 4.5 hours followed by BSA/LHC archery and MB Counselor information.
This class will be outdoors on an established archery range using camp and Instructor equipment. The class will start 8 to 8:30 am. After eating lunch the participant will provide, the BSA/LHC portion will continue for up to 2 hours.
Camping may be available if needed Friday night..
