/662-AS2027.desc:
Aquatic School: An Unparalleled Leadership and Aquatic Training Program
Since its inception in 1954, Aquatic School has been the Longhorn Council's premier week-long program dedicated to cultivating leadership and advanced aquatic skills among Scouts.
Program Overview:
Who:
Scouts aged 13-17 seeking to enhance their leadership capabilities and aquatic proficiency.
Tradition:
For over seventy years, Aquatic School has consistently served as the foundational training ground for the Longhorn Council's most skilled instructors and leaders.
Merit Badges:
The program offers Scouts the opportunity to complete the following Merit Badges.
Swimming
Lifesaving
Rowing
Canoeing
Kayaking
Public Speaking (all but 1 requirement)
Additional Opportunities:
depending on abilities and performance, Scouts will have the opportunity to complete or make progress toward the following:
Mile Swim
National Outdoor Achievement Award - Aquatics Segment
Safe Swim Defense Training Cert
Safety Afloat Training Cert
Paddlecraft Safety Certification (ages 15+)
Swimming and Water Rescue Certification (ages 15+)
Four Goals of Aquatic Shool:
Aquatic School is structured around four primary goals designed to foster holistic development:
Leadership Development:
Participants will engage in activities that enhance their decision-making, teamwork, and overall ability to lead.
Skill Proficiency:
Emphasis is placed on achieving a high level of mastery in all aquatic skills taught.
Instructor Training:
Beyond personal skill acquisition, the program equips Scouts with teaching skills and strategies necessary to effectively instruct others.
Time Management:
Participants will refine their organizational and prioritization skills, essential for academic and professional success…beyond their Scouting career.
Financial Assistance:
Worried about costs? Fear not! Camperships are available to ensure that no Scout misses out on this life-changing experience. Apply by
May 1st
and seize your chance to embark on this epic journey!
Pre-requisite:
All participants must pass the Scouting America swimmer's test the day they arrive at Aquatic School or they will not be allowed to stay as being a swimmer is the baseline for the rest of the program and does not include a ‘learn to swim’ phase.
Additional Information:
For more information and to see pictures or read testimonials, please visit AquaticSchool.org.

/662-NYLT26.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)
National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT) is the premier youth leadership development course for Scouting America within the Longhorn Council. NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through a wide range of activities, NYLT participants will get the skills and confidence to lead well as they put into action the best that Scouting has to offer.
Participant Requirements:
If you are attending as a participant, you must:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current Scouting America Annual Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Scouts BSA members must be 13 years of age and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program registration. They must be ranked a First Class Scout or higher and have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops.
Venturers and Sea Scouts must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program. They must have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Crews or Ships. It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant has basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
A unit leader recommendation.
Important Note:
A maximum of 5 Scouts from the same unit may attend the same NYLT course.  In the case when a Scout is dual registered (in both a Scouts BSA Troop and in a Venture Crew or Ship), the primary registration will be considered.

/664-NYLT27.desc:
National Youth Leadership Training
January 16-18 & February 13-15
Scouts must attend BOTH weekends
Wallwood Scout Reservation, Quincy, FL
National Youth Leadership Training is an exciting, action-packed program designed for councils to provide youth members with leadership skills and experience they can use in their home troops and in other situations demanding leadership of self and others.
The NYLT course centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must KNOW, and what a leader must DO. The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the course as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership.
NYLT is a six-day course broken up over two weekends ( January 16-18 & February 13-15).
Participants MUST attend both weekends to complete the course.   When registering, you are registering for both weekends.  Content is delivered in a troop and patrol outdoor setting with an emphasis on immediate application of learning in a fun environment.  NYLT integrates the best of modern leadership theory with the traditional strengths of the Scouting experience. Through activities, presentations, challenges, discussions, and audio-visual support, NYLT participants will be engaged in a unified approach to leadership that will give them the skill and confidence to lead well.
In order to attend a NYLT course, a youth must have the following qualifications by the beginning of the course:
Must be a registered member of a Scouting unit.
Must have a current BSA Health and Medical Record form parts A, B, and C.
Members must have completed "Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops" (or Crew/Ship) by the start date of the NYLT course.  Unit leaders conduct this training.
All Scouts must be at least 14, or 13 and have completed eighth grade, and fall within the maximum age allowance for their program.
It is recommended that they have had at least one year of camping experience. While NYLT is not an outdoor skills course, it is important that each participant have basic camping and outdoor cooking experience.
Have a unit leader recommendation.
NYLT is a "leadership" course, therefore a certain level of maturity is needed to be successful.   Scoutmaster's are encouraged to consider a Scout's maturity level before recommending them for the course.

Wood Badge 2027
CST13-690-27
May 14-16, 2027                  &                 June 5-6, 2027
FRIDAY, SATURDAY, SUNDAY               SATURDAY, SUNDAY
Wood Badge is leadership training for all Scout Leaders and Scouters who are involved in the programs of Scouting America: Cub Scouting, Scouts BSA, Sea Scouting, and Venturing, as well as Council and District leaders, and professionals.
This contemporary training program focuses on leadership and team-building skills, not Scoutcraft or outdoor skills. Participants will learn techniques to make them better leaders, and also how to lead groups to achieve objectives. The Wood Badge course incorporates the best of over a century of Scouting experience in addition to drawing upon the most current leadership models used by corporate America, academic circles, and successful outdoor leadership organizations throughout the country. Skills developed from Wood Badge training will help the participant do a better job in any BSA program - at any level of involvement. Skills learned at Wood Badge can be used in other aspects of their life as well.
Eligibility
Be a registered member of Scouting America. There are no minimum tenure requirements. Youth older than 18 many attend.
Be capable of functioning safely in an outdoor environment. Successful completion of the
Annual Health & Medical Form
(Parts A, B) is required for all participants.
Have completed the basic training courses for their registered Scouting positions.
Have completed the outdoor skills training programs required for their Scouts BSA positions. This would be Introduction to Outdoor Leaders Skills for Scoutmasters, Assistant Scoutmasters, and Venturing Advisors.
If you previously completed a Wood Badge course, agree not to wear your regalia until your new ticket is complete.
Application
The course fee is $375, but if you register before November1, 2026, you qualify for the Early Bird $50 discount. A deposit of $100.00 is needed with your application to secure your position on the course, and all balances are due by April 1, 2027.  Each participant will receive one course t-shirt; additional shirts can be ordered in advance of the course for $15 each.
Why do you want to go?
You want to participate in a Wood Badge course because of things you will learn and do. Here are some of the benefits:
Stronger units. You will make your Scouting unit stronger.
What and why of Scouting. You will have a deeper understanding of what Scouting is and why we do it.
Experience. You will learn and experience things that will stay with you in Scouting and the rest of your life.
Fun. You will have fun and you will meet interesting people.
Other groups. You will make your other groups, like work, church, even family, stronger.
Participant Survey
When your registration is complete, look for an email confirmation from no-reply@247scouting.com. This email contains a link to a Google Form that the course organizers need participants to complete. If you do not receive your registration confirmation email, please contact 690woodadge@scouting.org

/690-120492.desc:
Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills Training
JOIN US FOR ITOLS TRAINING!
Outdoor skills are critical to the success of the Scouting program, and this training will provide Scout leaders with the basic outdoor skills and confidence needed to take youth into the outdoors. The course focuses on skills needed for leaders to conduct outdoor camping experiences. In addition, the teaching methods, activities, and games model the variety of teaching used in effective and engaging Scouting programs. We hold this course outdoors to help reinforce the “outdoor” experience that you will bring back to your Scouts and Troop. Participants should leave the training experience with a feeling of comfort in working with and instructing their Scouts, and an increased level of confidence taking Scouts outdoors safely.
ITOLS (INTRODUCTION TO OUTDOOR LEADER SKILLS) is one of the BSA courses Scoutmasters and Assistant Scoutmasters are required to complete to earn the TRAINED emblem. With ITOLS, your classroom is the outdoors, your guidebook is the BSA Handbook, and the Patrol Method is the method of learning. This course will enhance your skills and give you the tools to offer an outdoor program for your troop. ITOLS is a hands-on, fun filled, skill training program that is designed to help you become familiar with the basic camping skills required from Scout rank to First Class. By using these skills sessions in conjunction with the Scouts BSA Handbook, Scouts BSA leaders will gain an exposure to not only many of the basic outdoor skills through First Class rank, but also the patrol method and numerous teaching methods and learning games.
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
Setting up camp
Planning a Menu
Cooking Techniques using wood and other fuels
Safe camp sanitation
Working with wood tools-knives and axes
Planning a campfire program
How not to get lost by using a compass
Reading a map
Working with ropes and knots
Techniques for hiking
Packing what to take and leave home
Nature identification
Leave No Trace Camping
WHO SHOULD ATTEND?
Registered leaders of Troops and Crews who participate with their unit’s outdoor program:
SCOUTMASTERS & ASSISTANTS are
required
to complete this course in order to complete the training required for their position.
TROOP COMMITTEE MEMBERS/PARENTS planning to participate with your troop's camping program; the course is highly recommended or may be required by your troop.
VENTURING ADVISORS & ASSISTANTS using high adventure or camping programs are encouraged to complete this course.
WHERE and WHEN:
Saturday Morning starting at 8:30 am through Sunday 12:00 pm Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills (S11)

:

REFUNDS--NO REFUNDS within seven (7) days of the course start date.
TEXT BOOK--The current edition of the Scouts BSA Handbook is required for the course.

BSA Medical Forms A & B
must be brought to your first day and will be returned on Sunday.

/690-120504.desc:
Kuweike Trek Camp
August 15–20, 2027
Kuweike Trek Camp returns for its fifth year! This premier
high-adventure
program is designed for Scouts BSA,Venturers, and Sea Scouts ages 13 and older who are ready to challenge themselves, explore the outdoors, and take their Scouting skills to the next level.
Experience the beauty and challenge of New Jersey’s legendary Pine Barrens as you hike, bike, and canoe through one of the most unique ecosystems in the United States. Along the way, participants will test their outdoor skills, develop leadership and teamwork, build lasting friendships, and have the opportunity to complete the requirements for the prestigious 50-Miler Award.
Kuweike means
“among the pines”
in the Lenni Lenape language. Kuweike Trek Camp immerses Scouts in the natural beauty, history, and ecology of the Pine Barrens—a remarkable landscape home to unique plants, wildlife, waterways, and natural features.
Whether you are preparing for a future national high-adventure experience or simply looking for your next great Scouting challenge, Kuweike Trek Camp offers an unforgettable adventure right here in our own backyard.
Hike • Bike • Canoe Trek
50+ Miles of Pine Barrens Adventure!
The Hike-Bike-Canoe Trek is the trifecta of the Kuweike Trek Program!
Participants will travel 50+ miles through Wharton State Forest, combining biking, hiking, and canoeing while camping along the trail.
The Trek includes:
Cycling to and from base camp at the Pine Tree Education & Environmental Center
Hiking sections of the Batona Trail, locally known as the “Back to Nature Trail”
Canoeing from Quaker Bridge to Batsto Lake
Overnight camping at Lower Forge and Buttonwood Hill
Exploring Pine Barrens landmarks including Apple Pie Hill, Batsto Village, and Atsion Lake
Along the way, Scouts will experience remote trails, scenic waterways, rich history, and the unique ecology of the Pine Barrens.
Program Details
Open to: Scouts BSA, Venturers and Sea Scouts ages 13+
Registration: Limited to 32 participants
Achievement: Opportunity to earn the 50-Miler Award
Activities: Hiking • Cycling • Canoeing • High Adventure
Cost
$500 per Scout participant
$150 per adult leader
We Provide
Bikes and helmets
Canoes, paddles, and PFDs
Guides and maps
Food
Conservation project tools and supplies
Scouts Should Provide
All personal camping gear, including tents, sleeping bags and pads, and backpacking stoves with fuel
Weather-appropriate clothing
Water shoes
Closed-toed shoes are REQUIRED
Important: The Trek concludes Friday afternoon at approximately 2:00 p.m. All participants must be out of camp by 4:00 p.m.
Location
Pine Tree Education & Environmental Center
Tabernacle, New Jersey

/695-MMSR2027SummerCamp.desc:
Medicine Mountain Scout Ranch (MMSR) and the Medicine Mountain Adventure Base (MMAB) is 160 acres of Scouting paradise surrounded by 1.3 million acres of National Forest Service land. Our camp rests like a jewel in the beautiful Black Hills of South Dakota. We boast a private fresh water lake stocked with trout, countless miles of local trails for mountain biking and hiking, breathtaking views, rustic serenity, access to local natural-face rock for climbing, and access to both public and non-public caves for spelunking and exploring. Scouts bring and pitch their own tents in forested campsites and dine in the comfort of their troop's own campsite "Troop / Patrol Style." The combination of our mild climate and 6,100 foot elevation renders us virtually mosquito free!
Reserve your campsite today!

/696-122438.desc:
Each year the Midnight Sun Council honors those who make a substantial contribution to our community.
In 2026 we are excited to honor the father and son team of Howard & John Thies as our 43rd Annual Distinguished Citizens.
We are asking you to join us at this fundraiser for the Midnight Sun Council, Scouting America.
This father and son duo were both born and raised in Fairbanks, graduated from Lathrop High School. Howard (1967) and John (2006 with SUMA CUM LAUDE) received full college scholarships and attended University of Alaska Fairbanks. John graduated on the Dean’s List.
Howard & John are both actively involved in the community. Howard has worked hard at bringing Arctic Man Ski and Snogo, Classic Chamber Rubber Duck Race & The Morris Thompson Golf Tourney. John, founded Worry-Free Alaska, established Golden Heart Waste Management (GHWM) & the Shred Way Company.
Howard and John are grateful for residing in Fairbanks and contributing to its betterment. The 43rd Annual Distinguished Citizens banquet honoring Howard & John will be held at the Wedgewood conference center (the old Antique Car Museum) in Fairbanks on Wednesday, December 9th, 2026. Please join us in donating to this worthwhile cause & thank you for supporting Scouting in Interior.
If you are unable to attend but still want to underwrite this event, we have special opportunities just for you.
To RSVP, contact the council office - call 907-452-1976.

/702-novemberscoutmaster.desc:
Scoutmaster Position Specific Training & Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills (IOLS)
2 options for registration:
1) Full Weekend and 2) IOLS Only
Pricing:
$25 In Council, $40 Out of Council
You only need to attend one session (one weekend) to complete IOLS training.
Scoutmaster Position Specific Training?
This training is the in-person version of the online Scoutmaster Position-Specific training program required for everyone registered as Scoutmaster or Assistant Scoutmaster and optional for all other adults involved with a Scouts BSA Troop.
This training introduces you to everything you need to know about serving as a Scoutmaster for a Scouts BSA Troop, and just how different it is from a Cub Scout Pack.
This course, combined with Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills (IOLS) course, Safeguarding Youth Training, and Hazardous Weather ID, will make you a “fully trained” Scouts BSA leader.
If you have completed all online position-specific training, the Friday evening portion is not required. If you’re unsure, please reach out to the course contact to check your training status.
What is IOLS?
IOLS stands for Introduction to Outdoor Leader Skills. This hands-on Scouts BSA Troop leader program gives adult leaders a practical introduction to the patrol method of a Scout-led troop by teaching many of the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the outdoors. This training is required for all Scoutmasters & Assistant Scoutmasters to be considered as fully position-trained. Other registered adults are also encouraged to attend.
PARTICIPANT FORMS:
Each participant must complete an Annual Health and Medical Record (Parts A & B) and turn it into the health officer upon arrival. ALL participants must have completed the online Safeguarding Youth Training,  Hazardous Weather Training, and, unless you are attending the Friday evening position specific training, you must also have completed position-specific training available at my.scouting.org.
ACCOMODATIONS:
You will be sleeping outside in tents, with most of the course taking place outdoors. If you have a special need or mobility issue, please bring it to our attention when you register or with the Course Contact.
MEALS:
Participants will be provided Cracker Barrel on Friday, Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner on Saturday, and Breakfast on Sunday. Please eat dinner prior to arriving at camp Friday evening.
Coffee, tea, and hot chocolate will be provided.
If you have any food allergies, please contact the Course Contact at least 10 days prior to the event.
PRE-REGISTRATION IS REQUIRED FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS!
This is required so we can have proper amount of materials and food prepared for the event.
CHECK-IN:
Full Weekend:
Participants may arrive as early as 5 pm Friday. Check in will begin between 6:00 - 6:15 PM. Training starts at 6:30 pm Sharp! Training will be finished by 10:00 am Sunday.
IOLS Only:
Participants may choose to camp Friday night as well. Saturday morning check in will begin at 7:00 AM and training will begin at 8:00 AM SHARP!
Registration closes 10 days prior to the event. Must have at least 6 participants for the class to run.  Maximum number is 24 participants.
This training is for Scouts BSA adults or Cub Scout Pack Adults that crossed over in 2026 or are crossing over in 2027.

/713-120170.desc:
This course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout Outdoor Program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities. Friday dinner, Saturday breakfast and lunch will be provided.
Who should take BALOO?
The BSA requires that you have at least one BALOO-trained adult in every Cub Scout den or pack overnight outdoor event. That includes pack camping and Webelos den overnighters. A BALOO-trained leader should be at any overnighter regardless of whether it is a pack, district, or council event.
Having at least one BALOO-trained adult will make your Cub Scouts’ camping experience as awesome as possible.
Why should I take BALOO?
Leaders who complete BALOO training are better prepared to plan pack den or pack overnight events. You’ll learn how to make camping activities and outings fun. You’ll discover how to keep your Cub Scouts safe and entertained. And you’ll learn how to plan an event rooted firmly in Cub Scouting’s principles.
Successful experiences in the outdoors make Cub Scouts — and their parents — more likely to return.
How do I take BALOO?
BALOO consists of two components: online and hands-on. You’ll need to complete both — in order — to qualify as a “Trained” Cub Scout outdoor leader and receive the BALOO recognition patch.
Online component: The online portion of BALOO is available 24/7 on the BSA Learn Center. Just log in to My.Scouting.org to begin. The goal of the online portion is to make the best use of time to allow leaders to experience as much as possible during the practical hands-on training.
Practical, hands-on component: This component includes an overnight stay and is designed to introduce the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities.
Further reading
For more on BALOO, including how to make the most of your BALOO weekend and the thinking behind the decision to combine BALOO and OWL, read
Mark Ray’s Scouting magazine story.

/713-WB27.desc:
The Sequoyah Council will be holding Wood Badge April 2nd-4th and April 17th-18, 2027.  Attendance at both weekends is required.
The new syllabus is revised, revamped, and repackaged. Scouters who have previously taken Wood Badge may return and take the new course. They must complete another ticket and cannot wear their beads at the course.
What is Wood Badge?
Wood Badge is the premier training program for Scouting America. It teaches contemporary leadership and team development skills in an outdoor setting. Its purpose is to aid Scouters in providing a quality program that will enable scouts to grow to their greatest potential.
The course encompasses the key concepts of management from top leaders in the management field. Therefore, this course can be helpful in your career as well as in your scouting position.
The Wood Badge course will be conducted during a three-day weekend (7:30 AM Friday through Sunday at 5:00 PM) and a two-day weekend (7:30 AM Saturday to Sunday at 4:30 PM).
Wood Badge experience consists of two parts: practical training and application. Practical leadership experiences are gained in a camp setting where leadership and management skills can be learned and practiced as a patrol.
After practical training, each participant has at least four months and a maximum of 18 months to complete the application phase (ticket) and meet all the goals agreed upon during the course.
Course Cost
Participants' cost is $275; $50 deposit is due at the time of registration, with the balance due 30-days in advance.  A late fee of $50 will be applied to any registration not paid by the 30-day deadline.  Payment plans are available through the registration system.

/763-2027VAHCOutdoorSchool.desc:
The VAHC Outdoor School held at Camp Shenandoah will feature Basic Adult Leader Outdoor Orientation (BALOO), Introduction to Outdoor Leadership Skills (IOLS), Rangemaster, Scouting America Chainsaw Safety, and Leave No Trace Level 1 Instructor training.
BALOO.
This one-and-a-half day course is designed as an introduction to the Cub Scout outdoor program for leaders interested in adding a camping component to their Pack activities. BALOO training consists of an
online pre-requisite
component in addition to an overnight hands-on practical. Scouting America's Cub Scout level camping policies will be taught along with the discovery of the necessary tools to help units carry out a successful camping experience.
IOLS.
Working as patrols, this hands-on course provides adult leaders the practical outdoor skills they need to lead Scouts in the out-of-doors. Upon completion, leaders should feel comfortable teaching Scouts the basic skills required to obtain the First Class rank. Along with Scoutmaster Specifics this course is required of all direct contact leaders registered in Scouts BSA Troops in order to be considered trained.
Rangemaster.
The rangemaster training is geared at cub scout activities but also has benefits for Scouts BSA.  The training will teach the basics for setting up and running a BB, Archery (cubs only), Slingshot, real and water-based rockets, and other cub-appropriate Range & Target Activities.  Rangemasters are required to run all of those events so if you plan to attend and might want to help at cub resident camp, webelos resident camp, the cub camporees, any other district/council event with range and target activities, this training is for you.
Chainsaw Safety Training.
This is an In-Council Chainsaw Safety Course for use of chainsaws on VAHC properties. This is designed to help volunteers get trained in the safe use of chainsaws to help clear trails, remove deadfalls, clear hazards, and stockpile firewood. Must be 21 years old to participate.  BSA chainsaw training is a 12-hour course which will cover both classroom saw safety operations and a field cutting day.  Participants should bring their own chainsaws, chaps, hard hat, hearing protection, gloves and ear protection.

/763-NYLT27.desc:
What is National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT)?
VAHC’s next course is being held 18-23 July, 2027 at Camp Shenandoah. Fee for the course is $295, and requires a $75 deposit. Full payment is due 45 days prior to the event start.
NYLT centers around the concepts of what a leader must BE, what a leader must KNOW, and what a leader must DO.  The key elements are then taught with a clear focus on HOW TO. The skills come alive during the week as the patrol goes on a Quest for the Meaning of Leadership. All while having fun, enjoying new experiences and making new friends.
This course is designed to model a month in the life of a youth-lead troop – three troop meetings (one each day for the first three days), all leading up to a big outdoor experience (an overnight outpost camp).  The course uses the patrol method and presents a model troop, Patrol Leader Council and patrol meetings.  Participants must be at least 13 years old, First Class [for ScoutsBSA] and have their Scoutmaster or Venture Crew Adviser approval.  We strongly encourage participants to have completed Introduction to Leadership Skills for Troops (ILST) or Crews (ILSC) at their units.

/802-CampAlpine2027.desc:
Camp Alpine is a fantastic, Nationally accredited Scouting America Summer Camp, nestled in the heart of the Alps at the Kandersteg International Scout Centre in Kandersteg, Switzerland. Camp Alpine takes advantage of this amazing location and offers a program focusing on the outdoors, nature, and exploration, all while implementing the Patrol Method. Being based at the World Center of Scouting, Scouts also get the opportunity to meet others from around the world, have a great experience, build amazing memories and international friendships.
PROGRAM
Camp Alpine offers an amazing Scouting Adventure for every level of Scout through three distinct program options:
BASE CAMP
-
Our Base Camp program is the perfect first step for your new Scouts, and a great start to their summer camp experience. Base Camp Scouts have an opportunity to learn all their essential Scout skills, completing multiple requirements while working toward 1st Class, Firem’n and Totin’ Chit, and even earn a merit badge, but most importantly have fun at every turn.
ASCENT
-
Geared for the next step in a Scout’s journey, the Ascent program is merit badge focused, with large blocks for better interaction.  Alpine continues to offer numerous academic and handicraft skills in the Crafts & Cultures area; Scoutcraft skills and experiences in Outdoor Skills; exploring nature in Ecology; perfecting your aim in Range and Target Activities (RATA); and releasing your inner fish with Aquatics.
SUMMIT
-
The Summit program is our specialty adventure program filled with outdoor adventure for older, more experienced Scouts. We are looking to offer an experience you'll remember for life.
WARNING
: may include glacial hikes, mountain peak summits, riding rapid waters, or climbing 100 foot cliffs.

/802-CampKenya26.desc:
Thank you for your interest in Camp Kenya '26! Camp will be held at the Savage Wilderness Adventure Camp, three hours outside of Nairobi, Kenya. Savage Wilderness leads the way in Kenyan adventure opportunities providing unique, breathtaking experiences in one of nature's most beautiful environments. Led by an international team of outdoor experts fully trained to provide the highest safety standards; you will cross rivers, plains and plateaus in an extraordinary and unforgettable adventure.
Camp Kenya is open to all youth and leaders who are registered with a Cub Scout Pack, Scouts BSA Troop, Venturing Crew, Sea Scout Ship or Explorer Post. Our Provisional Camper Program ensures Lone Scouts and smaller units can attend Camp Kenya by joining together provisional campers into provisional units. Participants age 11 to 13 require a designated responsible adult to be present at Camp, this may be a parent/guardian or a pre-determined unit leader.
Families wanting to join in the week can be accommodated in our Family Camping area and experience a family adventure holiday, with meals provided, while their youth participants spend their week in Camp Kenya activities. There are a limited number of Family Camping spots available, and only individuals that have a registrant in one of the Camp programs are eligible to attend as a Family Camp attendee.
Dates for our 2026 camp season:
Staff Arrival: December 27, 2026
Participant Arrival: December 29, 2026
Program Session: December 30, 2026 - January 3, 2027 (January 4, 2027 for Mlimi Camp and Majini Camp)
Staff/Participant Departure: January 4, 2027 (January 5, 2027 for Mlimi and Majini Camp Participants)
We offer Scouts the following program choices for the week of activities:
Shibli Camp - Cub Scout long-term camp offers Cub Scouts the opportunity to attend camp and work on Cub specific programming throughout the week. Each Cub must have a parent partner present for their week of programming.
Karibu Camp - "Trail to First Class" program to assist Scouts that are new to Scouting America programs by accomplishing many requirements towards the Scout, Tenderfoot, Second Class and First Class ranks.
Savannah Camp - For those more experienced Scouts we will offer a menu of merit badge classes throughout the week.
Kilele Camp - Youth age 14-20 participate in this unique high adventure option which will including hiking, offsite overnights and extended whitewater rafting, and much more.
Mlima Camp - Youth age 14-20 experience a once in a lifetime trek opportunity to sumit Mt. Kenya.
Majini Camp - Youth age 14-20 participate in a Sea Scout-specific week of activities and advancement.
Family Camp - Open to family members, adults and youth, who are accompanying a participant in another program to Kenya. Throughout the week family campers can utilize the various facilities and programs offered by Savage Wilderness.
Camp Kenya '26 rates - fees include all meals, transportation to and from Nairobi International Airport, 1/2 day Safari, visit to Lord Baden-Powell's Final Resting Place, and whitewater rafting, unless noted below:
$725 Cub Scouts and Family Camp attendees (age 5-10) (excludes Whitewater Rafting activities, in line with established Scouting America activity age restrictions)
$775 Karibu, Savannah, Kilele Campers and Adult Unit Leaders and age 11+ Family Campers
$850 Majini (Sea Scout) Campers
$950 Mlima (Trek) Campers
*There is a $100 Out-of-Council Surcharge for all registrants not registered in Transatlantic Council
**Kilele, Mlima and Majini Camp is ONLY open to youth age 14-20. Adults are NOT eligible to register for these programs as there are strict limits on the number of spots available for these programs. All registrations for these three programs are automatically WAITLISTED until age verification can be completed.
***All camp fees must be paid in full by October 31, 2026.

The Transatlantic Council (TAC) is one of three Scouting America Councils serving Scouting families abroad. We are based in Brussels, Belgium and serve families living in Europe, Africa, the Middle East, and Central Asia. TAC serves over 4,000 youth and volunteers.

Den Chiefs play a crucial role in transitioning and recruiting Cub Scouts into Troops, ensuring a steady flow of engaged, prepared new members. Adult leaders also play a key role in fostering this connection, making their participation in this training just as important!
Calling all Scouts and Scouters in NCAC!
Are you ready to take your leadership skills to the next level? Do you want to make a real impact while having a blast? Then it's time to step up and become Den Chief!
Join us for an exciting, hands-on Den Chief Training where you’ll learn everything you need to lead, inspire, and mentor younger Cub Scouts! This is your chance to become a role model, gain valuable leadership experience, and have an awesome time doing it.
Why should you attend?
Learn leadership & communication skills that will help you in Scouting and beyond!
Have fun while making a real impact on your local Cub Scout Pack!
Earn the Den Chief Service Award and enhance your path to Eagle!
Build friendships and exchange experiences with other Scouts across the NCAC who share your passion for Scouting!
Who can attend?
Cub Scout Packs looking to strengthen their program by implementing Den Chiefs.
Scouts BSA who want to serve as Den Chiefs (it is recommended Scouts  be active in their troops for at least one year before serving as Den Chiefs).
Adult Leaders & Scouters who want to learn how to work with and support Den Chiefs in their troops & packs.

Complete field uniform.

Anyone older than 18 years old must have the YPT to date.

/553-27wintercai.desc:
CERTIFIED ANGLER INSTRUCTOR
CAI COURSE 2027 SE-1
ONLINE
This is an online CAI training course.  Six online sessions and one in-person day at Camp Barstow.  18 hours total to complete.  Participants will be trained on Scout safety while fishing, techniques to rig, bait, and find fish.  Fish cleaning and preparation for cooking.  Fish identification and biology.  How to plan a fishing event at the pack, troop & crew levels.  We will also have hands on training for fly tying, fly rod use, spinning, spin cast, and telescoping pole fishing.  You must complete all online modules and in-person modules to complete the course.
Cost is $10.00 per participant.
This CAI course is for adult leaders and Scouting youth age 15 and up,
must have earned their Fishing & Fly-Fishing Merit Badges, and
enjoy teaching fishing skills to our youth and want to enhance their teaching and event planning skills in the fishing area. This course is open to participants from all BSA councils nationwide.
This class will be taught virtually online on Wednesday nights from 7:00pm-9:00pm.
The meeting link and password will be sent to participants prior to the start of the course once registration closes.
The course will be delivered as follows:
Module 1  February 3
(Intro, Cub Scout and Scouts BSA Fishing Programs)
Module 2  February 10
(Fishing Tackle)
Module 3  February 17
(Safety, Ethics, Fishery Management, Knots)
Module 4  February 24
(The nature of fish, Where to find fish, Fishing Basics)
Module 5  March 3
(Casting,  Fishing, Cleaning and cooking)
Module 6  March 10
(Planning fishing events, Angling Educator, Special offers, Deliver the Promise, Graduation)
Are you searching for programs that will lead to member recruitment, reactivation, and retention? Then we think we have just the Scouting America Supplemental Training course for you! Like many things in Scouting, the Scouting America Certified Angling Instructor (CAI) training course is designed to be fun with a purpose!
What can Certified Angling Instructors do?
· Teach the Scouting America Fishing Basics course.
· Train and qualify Scouting America Angling Educators.
· Serve on your Council’s Fishing Committee or Start one.
· Be a subject matter expert for Fishing Derbies, Summer Camp, Merit Badge clinics, and fishing related advancement.
Course Highlights
· Become recognized as a Scouting America Certified Angling Instructor and receive an Official Train the Trainer Certification CS-61 and a CAI patch.
· Learn basic fishing and fly-fishing skills including fly casting, fly tying, knots, and how to teach them. Receive the materials to assist you in delivering the program as well as online resource locations.
· As a CAI you will have the opportunity to get fishing and fly-fishing equipment at greatly reduced rates for teaching Scouts.
Participants will:
· Understand available resources for unit angler education program development to inspire member recruitment and retention.
· Gain education and insight through active participation in dozens of Angling Education learning activities.
Activities include:
· Age and Skill-Level based programs.
· Focused on the aims of Scouting America Cub Scout, Scouts BSA, Sea Scout, and Venturing programs.
· Focus on the methods that include Outdoors, Angling and Conservation.
Who can attend?
· All registered adult volunteers.
· Youth, that are 15 years or older can participate and must have earned their Fishing & Fly-Fishing Merit Badges.
· Open to both In-Council and Out-of-Council attendees.
· No prior fishing experience is required.
Learn more about the
BS
A’s Certified Angler Instructor program
, which trains leaders to execute fishing programs at the local council level. After completing the training make sure to update your training record with PAS Code: CS61

ATLANTA, GA

To:
Scouts, Troops, Crews, and Leaders
From:
Scout Challenge Task Force HQ
Subject:
Camporee[CLASSIFIED] 2027
YOUR MISSION:
Join over 2,000 Scouts BSA, Venturers, Sea Scouts, and leaders from across the Atlanta Area Council during
CAMPOREE
[CLASSIFIED]
: Scout Challenge 2027
at Bert Adams Scout Camp! The operation commences on March 12, 2027 and ends on March 14, 2027.
Every two years, our Council gathers for an unforgettable, jamboree-style weekend of adventure, competition, and Scouting camraderie.  For 2027, the camp transforms in an active training ground for "field operatives", challenging patrols to test their skills in espionage, tradecraft, codebreaking, physical challenges, covert signaling, and tactical problem-solving.
We have put the challenge back in Scout Challenge.
WHAT TO EXPECT IN THE FIELD:
Covert Operations
Program Challenges
Spend Saturday cracking ciphers, navigating obstacle courses, mastering surveillance tracking, and tackling patrol-versus-patrol challenges to unlock exclusive event patches and Council bragging rights.
When the field operations wrap up Saturday, the mission debrief will include a short live performance by
[CLASSIFIED & REDACTED]
.
Food & Trading Posts
-
Mission-Fueled Saturday Lunch:
To keep our agents moving through Saturday activities without needing to head back to camp, "Lunch Spot" style lunch will be provided for all agents and operatives.
-
Unit Cooking for All Other Meals:
We know agents have missions to complete for home HQ as well (hello, cooking requirements), so come prepared with your supplies for all other weekend grub (Friday dinner, Saturday breakfast & dinner, and Sunday breakfast).
-
Trading Posts & Merch:
A good agent is fueled and setup with the right gear. The Bert Adams Trading Post and a special Triple-J Cafe pop-up post will offer event merchandise, snacks, cold drinks, and essentials. Special Camporee [CLASSIFIED] event merch and Bert Adams 100 merch will also be available.
Flexible Unit Time
-
Program runs all day Saturday, and into the evening. Your unit can decide when they arrive and depart. Look for a briefing on details as we get closer.
FAQ
- W
ho can attend Camporee
[CLASSIFIED]
Scout Challenge 2027?
This field operation is exclusively for Scouts BSA, Venturing, and Sea Scouts (
no Cub Scout program this year
). Units register and camp together.
-
Will parking and getting into camp be the same as in years past?
HQ has received your intel—and we're making adjustments. We are modifying our approach to parking and arrival procedures in the hopes of some improvement. Parking will be available in designated central lots, and where available near home ops. Watch for additional instructions before deployment.
- What else is different this year?
- new parking and arrival procedures will hopefully remove some stress from our agents & operatives
- the removal of junior operatives (Cubs) will return this event to exclusively for Troops, Crews, and Ships.
- food truck operations have been terminated and we are offering a Saturday lunch to all agents & operatives included with the registration fee.
- Camping areas will be further spread out to give units more room to setup up home operations.
- Program enhancements will give agents & operatives plenty to do, and keep them moving all day long.
-
What if a participant needs mobility accommodations?
We want every Scout to have a great experience. Please be sure to note any needed physical or mobility accommodations directly in your unit’s online registration.
-
How can I help?
We are still looking for everything from highly trained special operatives to shift volunteers to help with field operations.
We welcome any and all assistance to make this event a success! Please reach out to the event registrar for details on volunteer opportunities. Volunteers may choose to camp

Scout Day at the Georgia State Capitol
Georgia State Capitol | March 4, 2027
Scout Day at the Capitol returns Monday, March 4, 2027! Scouting prepares young people to be good citizens. Spend the day witnessing first-hand the political process in Georgia. Watch your legislators recognize your Scouts from the House Gallery. And have a chance to ask actual representatives your most pressing questions!
Advancement opportunities are available for both Cubs and Scouts BSA youth who attend. More details on that coming soon!
The schedule will be finalized in collaboration with the Capitol; the traditional arrival time is 7:30 AM.  The event concludes prior to noon.
Attire:
Scout uniforms are prefered. Adult leaders may also come in uniform.
Arrival:

From 7:30 AM - 8:00 AM, Scouts will arrive at the
Georgia State Capitol Building
(18 Capitol Square Atlanta, GA 30334) to pick up Chick-fil-A breakfast and event packets. We will stop serving breakfast promptly at 8:00AM. Room Number to pick up breakfast and packets to be announced closer to the event.
Between 8:00 AM 8:30 AM, Scouts and attendees proceed to the
South Steps of the Capitol
for group photos.
All Scouts will gather at 8:30am at the South wing steps (second floor). Once you pass security, turn to the right, and take the steps immediately to your right up to the second floor.
Parking:
There are paid Public parking decks available at several locations around the Capitol building.
Here are a few options, all within 2 blocks:
Trinity United Methodist Church, 265 Washington St. SW
Capitol Ave SW Parking, 254 Capitol Ave. SW

Entering the Capitol Building:
The entrance to the Capitol building is located on the South side of the building, off Capitol Square SW. All adults will need a valid State issued ID. No weapons are allowed in the building, including pocket knives. All bags will be checked by security.

This program is designed to help you understand the concept of sustainability—
meeting our needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
We’ll explore what sustainability means in everyday life around our homes, schools and
businesses and discover practical ways we can all live greener. You’ll learn how small
changes can make a big impact and discuss how you can share this knowledge through
your Scouting, proving that sustainability is not just important but also easy!
Come ready to learn, work, and have fun as we move towards a more sustainable
future together!
Check-in will begin at 12 pm with the Badge session starting at 12:05 pm.
Bonus Opportunity:
We’re also offering a Morning Merit Badge session for those looking to earn two
badges in one day.
Interested in the Reptile and Amphibian Study Merit Badge? Come first for the Reptile
and Amphibian Study Merit Badge from 10:00-11:30am. Sign up for one or both!
Please note: If your child is staying for the double session and choose to bring
lunch, it must be peanut/tree nut-free.
